chapters.title: Reproduction in Lower and Higher Plants
chapters.description: Study of asexual and sexual reproduction in lower plants (algae, fungi, bryophytes, pteridophytes) and higher plants (gymnosperms and angiosperms), along with structure and development of flowers, pollen, ovules, fruits, and seeds.
learningObjectives: Differentiate between asexual and sexual modes of reproduction in plants.
Understand microsporogenesis and megasporogenesis processes.
Explain types and agents of pollination.
Describe double fertilization and post-fertilization events.
Understand fruit and seed development in angiosperms.

questions.text: Which of the following is an asexual method of reproduction?
questions.answer: Fragmentation

questions.text: Define vegetative propagation.
questions.answer: Vegetative propagation is a type of asexual reproduction in which new plants develop from vegetative parts like roots, stems, or leaves.

questions.text: What is microsporogenesis?
questions.answer: Microsporogenesis is the process of formation of microspores (pollen grains) from microspore mother cells through meiosis.

questions.text: State two differences between self-pollination and cross-pollination.
questions.answer: Self-pollination occurs within the same flower or plant, ensures purity of race; cross-pollination occurs between different plants of the same species and increases genetic variation.

questions.text: Double fertilization is characteristic of:
questions.answer: Angiosperms

questions.text: What is the function of the endosperm?
questions.answer: Endosperm provides stored nutrients required for the growth and development of the embryo.

questions.text: Explain the term megasporogenesis.
questions.answer: Megasporogenesis is the formation of megaspores from the megaspore mother cell inside the ovule through meiosis.

questions.text: Describe the process of double fertilization in angiosperms.
questions.answer: In double fertilization, one male gamete fuses with the egg cell to form the zygote (syngamy), while the other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (triple fusion). This unique process results in simultaneous formation of embryo and endosperm.

questions.text: Explain post-fertilization changes occurring in a flower.
questions.answer: After fertilization, the ovary develops into a fruit, ovules develop into seeds, endosperm forms to nourish the embryo, integuments form the seed coat, and petals and other floral parts wither away.

questions.text: Discuss types of asexual reproduction in lower plants with suitable examples.
questions.answer: Lower plants reproduce asexually through methods such as fragmentation (Spirogyra), spore formation (Rhizopus), budding (Yeast), and binary fission (Bacteria). These methods help rapid multiplication and survival under unfavorable conditions.

questions.text: The outer layer of pollen grain is thick and made up of complex, non-biodegradable substance called as
questions.answer: sporopollenin

questions.text: Sporoderm is made up of
questions.answer: exine and intine

questions.text: The number of meiotic and mitotic divisions necessary for development of female gametophyte in angiosperms is
questions.answer: 1 meiosis and 3 mitosis

questions.text: Identify the odd one with respect to pollinating agent
questions.answer: Bottle brush

questions.text: In vitro pollen germination and pollen tube elongation can be induced by
questions.answer: sucrose

questions.text: Self-incompatibility is found in flowers of plants
questions.answer: Thea

questions.text: Porogamy refers to entry of pollen tube through
questions.answer: micropyle

questions.text: An example of helobial endosperm
questions.answer: Asphodelus

questions.text: The single shield shaped cotyledon in monocot seed is known as
questions.answer: scutellum

questions.text: The example of dicot endospermic seed is
questions.answer: castor

questions.text: Why anther is called as tetrasporangiate structure?
questions.answer: Due to presence of four pollen sacs in dithecous anther it is called as tetrasporangiate structure.

questions.text: At which stage pollen grains are shed from the anther in Angiosperms?
questions.answer: At two-celled stage pollen grains are shed from the anther in angiosperms.

questions.text: What is hilum with respect to ovule?
questions.answer: Hilum is the point of attachment of funiculus to the main body of ovule.

questions.text: What is protandry?
questions.answer: Protandry is a condition in which anthers mature first but the stigma of the same flower is not receptive at that time.

questions.text: Name any one plant in which double fertilization was discovered?
questions.answer: Lilium

questions.text: Why fertilization process in angiosperms is called double fertilization?
questions.answer: In angiosperms both male gametes participate in fertilization, hence fertilization occurs twice in the same embryo sac.

questions.text: Which is the most common type of endosperm in angiospermic families?
questions.answer: Nuclear type is the most common type of endosperm found in angiospermic families.

questions.text: What is the role of suspensor during the development of embryo?
questions.answer: The suspensor helps in pushing the embryo into the endosperm.

questions.text: What is adventive polyembryony?
questions.answer: In adventive polyembryony, embryos may develop from somatic nucellus or integuments along with normally formed zygote embryo.

questions.text: Name the hormone produced by unfertilized ovary responsible for enlargement of ovary into fruit?
questions.answer: Auxin (Indole-3-acetic acid)

questions.text: Draw a well labelled diagram of T.S. anther.
questions.answer: T.S. of anther shows epidermis, endothecium, middle layers, tapetum and sporogenous tissue.

questions.text: Define microsporogenesis.
questions.answer: Microsporogenesis is the process of formation of haploid microspores from diploid microspore mother cell through meiosis inside microsporangium.

questions.text: State any two structural features of pollen grain.
questions.answer: Pollen grain is surrounded by two layered wall – outer exine made of sporopollenin and inner intine made of cellulose and pectin.

questions.text: What are germ pores?
questions.answer: Germ pores are thin areas present in the exine of pollen grain through which pollen tube emerges during germination.

questions.text: Define pollination.
questions.answer: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from anther to the stigma of a flower.

questions.text: What is double fertilization?
questions.answer: Double fertilization is a characteristic feature of angiosperms in which one male gamete fuses with egg forming zygote and the other fuses with secondary nucleus forming endosperm.

questions.text: Define polyembryony.
questions.answer: Polyembryony is the occurrence of more than one embryo developing in a single seed.

questions.text: What is endosperm?
questions.answer: Endosperm is a nutritive tissue formed after fertilization in angiosperms that provides nourishment to the developing embryo.

questions.text: Name the types of endosperm.
questions.answer: The types of endosperm are nuclear, cellular and helobial.

questions.text: What is fertilization?
questions.answer: Fertilization is the process of fusion of male and female gametes to form a diploid zygote.

questions.text: Describe internal structure of anther.
questions.answer: Anther wall consists of four layers: epidermis, endothecium with fibrous thickenings, middle layers which degenerate at maturity, and tapetum which is nutritive. The central region contains sporogenous tissue forming microspore mother cells.

questions.text: Explain development of male gametophyte in angiosperms.
questions.answer: Microspore develops into male gametophyte. It divides mitotically into vegetative and generative cell. Generative cell later divides to form two male gametes, completing male gametophyte development.

questions.text: Explain types of pollination.
questions.answer: Pollination is of three types: self-pollination (autogamy), cross-pollination (xenogamy) and geitonogamy where pollen transfer occurs between different flowers of same plant.

questions.text: Explain significance of double fertilization.
questions.answer: Double fertilization ensures formation of embryo and nutritive endosperm only after successful fertilization, preventing wastage of resources and ensuring proper seed development.

questions.text: Explain polyembryony.
questions.answer: Polyembryony is the development of more than one embryo in a single seed. It may arise due to cleavage of zygote or development from nucellus or integuments.

questions.text: Explain types of endosperm.
questions.answer: Endosperm may be nuclear, cellular or helobial based on sequence of nuclear division and cell wall formation during development.

questions.text: Explain apomixis.
questions.answer: Apomixis is a form of asexual reproduction in plants where seeds are formed without fertilization, commonly seen in Citrus and Mango.

questions.text: Explain development of dicot embryo.
questions.answer: The zygote divides into terminal and basal cells. Terminal cell forms embryo proper while basal cell forms suspensor which helps in nutrition and positioning of embryo.

questions.text: Explain pollen-pistil interaction.
questions.answer: Pollen-pistil interaction involves recognition, acceptance or rejection of pollen by stigma ensuring compatibility before fertilization.

questions.text: Explain fertilization in angiosperms.
questions.answer: Fertilization involves fusion of male gametes with egg and secondary nucleus leading to formation of zygote and endosperm respectively.

questions.text: Describe the structure of anatropous ovule with labelled diagram.
questions.answer: Anatropous ovule is inverted ovule with micropyle close to funiculus. It consists of nucellus, integuments, embryo sac, chalaza, hilum and micropyle.

questions.text: Describe development of female gametophyte in angiosperms.
questions.answer: Female gametophyte develops from functional megaspore through successive mitotic divisions forming embryo sac with egg apparatus, polar nuclei and antipodal cells.

questions.text: Explain double fertilization in angiosperms with diagram.
questions.answer: Double fertilization involves syngamy and triple fusion resulting in formation of zygote and endosperm. It is unique to angiosperms.

questions.text: Explain various devices to prevent self-pollination.
questions.answer: Plants show herkogamy, dichogamy, self-incompatibility and unisexuality to prevent self-pollination and promote cross-pollination.

questions.text: Explain development of dicot embryo with diagram.
questions.answer: Dicot embryo develops from zygote through proembryo, globular, heart-shaped and torpedo stages forming radicle, plumule and cotyledons.

questions.text: How many meiotic and mitotic divisions occur during the development of male gametophyte from microspore mother cell?
questions.answer: One meiotic and two mitotic

questions.text: Which of the following represents apomixis?
questions.answer: Seed formation without fertilization

questions.text: Define vegetative reproduction. Give any one example.
questions.answer: Vegetative reproduction is a type of asexual reproduction in which new plants are produced from vegetative parts like root, stem or leaf. Example: Potato.

questions.text: What is pollination? Name its two types.
questions.answer: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from anther to stigma. Types: Self-pollination and cross-pollination.

questions.text: Write any three differences between self-pollination and cross-pollination.
questions.answer: Self-pollination occurs within same flower/plant, needs no agents, produces less variation. Cross-pollination occurs between different plants, requires agents, produces genetic variation.

questions.text: Explain microsporogenesis.
questions.answer: Microsporogenesis is the process by which diploid microspore mother cells undergo meiosis to form haploid microspores.

questions.text: Explain megasporogenesis.
questions.answer: Megasporogenesis is the process of formation of haploid megaspores from diploid megaspore mother cell by meiosis.

questions.text: Describe the structure of a typical angiosperm ovule.
questions.answer: A typical ovule consists of nucellus, embryo sac, integuments, micropyle, chalaza and funiculus.

questions.text: Draw a neat labelled diagram of a mature embryo sac.
questions.answer: Diagram showing egg cell, synergids, antipodals, polar nuclei.

questions.text: Explain double fertilization in angiosperms.
questions.answer: One male gamete fuses with egg forming zygote (syngamy) and the other fuses with secondary nucleus forming endosperm (triple fusion).

questions.text: Explain post-fertilization changes in angiosperms.
questions.answer: Zygote develops into embryo, ovule becomes seed, ovary becomes fruit and endosperm develops for nutrition.

questions.text: What is polyembryony? Give one example.
questions.answer: Polyembryony is the occurrence of more than one embryo in a seed. Example: Citrus.

questions.text: Angiosperms are the most advanced plants.
questions.answer: Because they show double fertilization, enclosed seeds, efficient vascular tissues and complex reproductive mechanisms.

chapters.title: Reproduction in Lower and Higher Animals
chapters.description: Study of asexual and sexual reproduction in lower and higher animals, including gametogenesis, fertilization, embryonic development, reproductive health, and human reproductive systems.
topics: Reproductive Health and Assisted Reproductive Technologies
learningObjectives: Differentiate between asexual and sexual reproduction in animals.
Understand gametogenesis and structure of human reproductive systems.
Explain the menstrual cycle and hormonal regulation.
Describe fertilization and stages of embryonic development.
Learn about reproductive health and modern reproductive technologies.

questions.text: Binary fission is commonly seen in:
questions.answer: Amoeba

questions.text: Define fertilization.
questions.answer: Fertilization is the fusion of male and female gametes to form a diploid zygote.

questions.text: What is ovulation?
questions.answer: Ovulation is the release of a mature ovum from the ovary, typically occurring midway through the menstrual cycle.

questions.text: State two differences between external and internal fertilization.
questions.answer: External fertilization occurs outside the body and requires water; internal fertilization occurs inside the body and offers greater protection to the embryo.

questions.text: Which hormone triggers ovulation?
questions.answer: LH

questions.text: What is spermatogenesis?
questions.answer: Spermatogenesis is the process of formation of sperms from spermatogonial stem cells in the testes.

questions.text: Explain the importance of the placenta.
questions.answer: The placenta facilitates exchange of nutrients, gases, and waste products between mother and fetus and secretes essential hormones.

questions.text: Describe the phases of the menstrual cycle.
questions.answer: The menstrual cycle has four phases: 1. **Menstrual Phase** – Shedding of uterine lining. 2. **Follicular Phase** – Follicle development and increase in estrogen. 3. **Ovulation** – Release of ovum triggered by LH surge. 4. **Luteal Phase** – Corpus luteum forms and secretes progesterone; if no fertilization occurs, cycle repeats.

questions.text: Explain the process of embryonic development from zygote to blastocyst.
questions.answer: After fertilization, the zygote divides by mitosis into a morula, then develops into a blastocyst. The blastocyst forms a trophoblast and inner cell mass and implants into the uterine wall for further development.

questions.text: Discuss assisted reproductive technologies (ART) such as IVF and ICSI.
questions.answer: ART includes methods like IVF, where fertilization occurs outside the body, and ICSI, where a single sperm is injected into an ovum. These techniques help couples with infertility and ensure embryo development before implantation.

questions.text: The primary sex organ in human males is
questions.answer: testis

questions.text: Seminal fluid is _____ in nature
questions.answer: alkaline

questions.text: Which of the following is not a part of uterus?
questions.answer: Ovary

questions.text: Menarch, menstrual cycle and menopause are controlled by
questions.answer: gonadotrophic hormone

questions.text: Nebenkern is
questions.answer: middle piece of sperm

questions.text: Nervous system develops from _____ of embryonic layer
questions.answer: ectoderm

questions.text: The average period of pregnancy in human lasts for _____ days
_____ is not a permanent method of birth control
questions.answer: Withdrawal

questions.text: The organism which causes Gonorrhoea is
questions.answer: Neisseria

questions.text: How many pairs of testes are present in human male?
questions.answer: 1 pair

questions.text: Name the enzyme secreted by the prostate gland.
questions.answer: Acid phosphatase

questions.text: What is glans penis?
questions.answer: The swollen tip of external genital organ or penis is called glans penis.

questions.text: What is atresia with respect to ovary in human females?
questions.answer: The large scale destruction of primordial follicles during growth is called atresia.

questions.text: Name the hydrolytic enzyme secreted by acrosome.
questions.answer: Hyaluronidase

questions.text: What is morula?
questions.answer: The 16–32 celled stage formed during cleavage is called morula.

questions.text: What is the function of inner cell mass?
questions.answer: The embryo proper develops from the inner cell mass.

questions.text: Name the embryonic layer from which heart, blood and blood vessels develop.
questions.answer: Mesoderm

questions.text: What is the use of tablet Saheli?
questions.answer: Saheli is an oral contraceptive pill.

questions.text: Identify the IUD shown in the diagram.
questions.answer: Lippes Loop

questions.text: What is MTP?
questions.answer: Medical Termination of Pregnancy is the intentional termination of pregnancy before full term.

questions.text: Draw a well labelled diagram of L.S. human testis.
questions.answer: Diagram shows seminiferous tubules, rete testis, epididymis, vas deferens and tunica albuginea.

questions.text: Describe the structure of Graafian follicle.
questions.answer: Graafian follicle consists of oocyte, zona pellucida, granulosa cells, theca interna and theca externa.

questions.text: Write a short note on fallopian tube.
questions.answer: Fallopian tubes transport ovum from ovary to uterus and are the site of fertilization.

questions.text: Give an account of external genitalia in human females.
questions.answer: External genitalia include labia majora, labia minora, clitoris, vestibule and mons pubis.

questions.text: Explain the structure of secondary oocyte.
questions.answer: Secondary oocyte is haploid, surrounded by zona pellucida and corona radiata.

questions.text: Define cleavage.
questions.answer: Cleavage is rapid mitotic division of zygote forming blastomeres.

questions.text: What is lactation?
questions.answer: Lactation is the secretion of milk from mammary glands after childbirth.

questions.text: Mention any two goals of RCH programme.
questions.answer: Control population growth and improve reproductive health.

questions.text: Up to which month is MTP allowed?
questions.answer: Up to 20 weeks of pregnancy.

questions.text: What is morula stage?
questions.answer: Morula is a solid ball of cells formed after cleavage.

questions.text: Describe histology of testis with diagram.
questions.answer: Testis contains seminiferous tubules lined by germinal epithelium and interstitial cells producing testosterone.

questions.text: Describe histological structure of human ovary.
questions.answer: Ovary shows follicles at different stages, corpus luteum and corpus albicans.

questions.text: Explain structure of human sperm.
questions.answer: Human sperm consists of head, neck, middle piece and tail.

questions.text: Explain oogenesis.
questions.answer: Oogenesis is formation of female gamete involving mitosis and meiosis.

questions.text: Explain implantation.
questions.answer: Implantation is attachment of blastocyst to uterine wall.

questions.text: Explain parturition.
questions.answer: Parturition is the process of childbirth involving labour pains.

questions.text: Explain menstrual cycle.
questions.answer: Menstrual cycle includes menstrual, proliferative, ovulatory and secretory phases.

questions.text: Explain spermatogenesis.
questions.answer: Spermatogenesis is formation of sperms from spermatogonia.

questions.text: Explain fertilization in humans.
questions.answer: Fertilization is fusion of sperm and ovum forming zygote.

questions.text: Explain infertility.
questions.answer: Infertility is inability to conceive even after regular unprotected intercourse.

questions.text: Write an account of seminal vesicle and bulbourethral gland.
questions.answer: Seminal vesicles secrete fructose-rich fluid and bulbourethral glands secrete mucus for lubrication.

questions.text: Explain ovarian cycle with diagram.
questions.answer: Ovarian cycle includes follicular phase, ovulation and luteal phase.

questions.text: Describe spermatogenesis with diagram.
questions.answer: Spermatogenesis occurs in seminiferous tubules in three phases: multiplication, growth and maturation.

questions.text: Explain mechanism of fertilization in humans.
questions.answer: Fertilization involves capacitation, acrosome reaction and fusion of gametes.

questions.text: Explain assisted reproductive technologies (ART).
questions.answer: ART includes IVF, ZIFT, GIFT, ICSI and AI to treat infertility.

questions.text: Identify the permanent birth control method in given diagram.
questions.answer: Tubectomy (Tubal ligation).

questions.text: Identify the parts labelled in the given diagram.
questions.answer: A. Nucleus, B. Corona radiata, C. Zona pellucida, D. Cytoplasm

questions.text: Identify the labels from the given diagram.
questions.answer: A. Fallopian tube (Oviduct), B. Cervix, C. Vagina, D. Uterus (uterine wall / myometrium–endometrium region), E. Ovary, F. Fimbriae / Infundibulum of fallopian tube

questions.text: The hormone responsible for ovulation in human females is:
questions.answer: LH

questions.text: Which structure connects the fetus to the placenta?
questions.answer: Umbilical cord

questions.text: Define spermatogenesis.
questions.answer: Spermatogenesis is the process of formation of haploid sperms from diploid spermatogonia in the testes.

questions.text: What is menstrual cycle?
questions.answer: The menstrual cycle is a monthly sequence of changes in the ovaries and uterus of human females, lasting about 28 days.

questions.text: Explain fertilization in humans.
questions.answer: Fertilization is the fusion of male and female gametes in the ampulla of fallopian tube to form a diploid zygote.

questions.text: Explain implantation.
questions.answer: Implantation is the attachment of the blastocyst to the endometrium of the uterus for further development.

questions.text: Draw a neat labelled diagram of human sperm.
questions.answer: Diagram showing head, neck, middle piece and tail with labels.

questions.text: Draw a neat labelled diagram of human ovary showing stages of follicle development.
questions.answer: Diagram showing primary, secondary, tertiary follicles and corpus luteum.

questions.text: Describe spermatogenesis with suitable diagram.
questions.answer: Spermatogonia undergo mitosis, meiosis I and II forming spermatids which mature into sperms.

questions.text: Explain hormonal regulation of menstrual cycle.
questions.answer: FSH and LH regulate ovarian cycle; estrogen and progesterone control uterine cycle.

questions.text: Human placenta is said to be haemochorial.
questions.answer: Because maternal blood comes in direct contact with chorionic villi of the fetus.

questions.text: Give any three functions of placenta.
questions.answer: Nutrition, respiration, excretion and endocrine functions.

chapters.title: Inheritance and Variation
chapters.description: Study of Mendelian genetics, laws of inheritance, gene interactions, linkage, crossing over, chromosomal disorders, and variations in living organisms.
learningObjectives: Understand Mendel's experiments and laws of inheritance.
Analyze monohybrid and dihybrid crosses.
Differentiate between complete dominance, incomplete dominance, and co-dominance.
Explain linkage, crossing over, and sex-linked inheritance.
Identify chromosomal disorders and their genetic basis.

questions.text: Mendel is known as the father of:
questions.answer: Genetics

questions.text: Define phenotype.
questions.answer: Phenotype is the observable physical or physiological trait of an organism determined by genotype and environment.

questions.text: State Mendel's Law of Segregation.
questions.answer: The Law of Segregation states that alleles of a gene separate during gamete formation so each gamete carries only one allele.

questions.text: What is incomplete dominance? Give one example.
questions.answer: Incomplete dominance occurs when neither allele is completely dominant, resulting in an intermediate phenotype. Example: Pink flowers in Mirabilis jalapa.

questions.text: ABO blood group system shows:
questions.answer: Multiple alleles

questions.text: What is crossing over?
questions.answer: Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during meiosis, leading to recombination.

questions.text: Name two chromosomal disorders and state their chromosomal basis.
questions.answer: Down syndrome – trisomy 21; Turner syndrome – monosomy X.

questions.text: Explain Mendel's dihybrid cross and the Law of Independent Assortment.
questions.answer: Mendel crossed plants differing in two characters (e.g., yellow round × green wrinkled). The F2 generation showed a phenotypic ratio of 9:3:3:1. This demonstrated the Law of Independent Assortment, which states that alleles of different genes assort independently during gamete formation.

questions.text: Describe linkage and how it differs from independent assortment.
questions.answer: Linkage is the tendency of genes located on the same chromosome to be inherited together. Unlike independent assortment, linked genes do not assort independently unless crossing over separates them. Linkage reduces recombination frequency.

questions.text: Discuss the types of variation seen in organisms and their significance.
questions.answer: Variations include somatic and germinal variations, continuous and discontinuous variations. They arise from mutations, recombination, and environmental factors. Variations allow natural selection, help species adapt, and contribute to evolution.

questions.text: The three principles of Mendelism are
questions.answer: Dominance, segregation and independent assortment

questions.text: Which one of the following is back cross?
questions.answer: F1 × Recessive parent

questions.text: RR (Red) Antirrhinum crossed with white (rr) produces pink offspring. This is an example of
questions.answer: Incomplete dominance

questions.text: The word chromosome was coined by
questions.answer: Waldeyer

questions.text: Nullisomy is represented by
Identify the odd one
questions.answer: Diploidy

questions.text: In humans, the sex chromosome complement is
questions.answer: XX–XY

questions.text: A family has five daughters and expecting sixth child. The chance of its being a son is
In human beings 45 chromosomes/single X/XO abnormality causes
questions.answer: Turner syndrome

questions.text: Webbed neck is characteristic of _____ syndrome
questions.answer: XO

questions.text: Define inheritance.
questions.answer: The transmission of genetic information from generation to generation is called inheritance.

questions.text: What is allelomorph?
questions.answer: Two or more alternative forms of a gene present at the same locus are called alleles or allelomorphs.

questions.text: What is test cross?
questions.answer: A cross between F1 hybrid and its homozygous recessive parent is called test cross.

questions.text: Define euploidy.
questions.answer: When chromosome number in a cell is exact multiple of basic set, it is called euploidy.

questions.text: Give one example of complete linkage.
questions.answer: X chromosome of Drosophila males shows complete linkage.

questions.text: How many linkage groups are present in Drosophila melanogaster?
questions.answer: Four linkage groups.

questions.text: Which genes show straight inheritance?
questions.answer: Genes present on Y chromosome show straight inheritance.

questions.text: How are drones produced in honey bees?
questions.answer: Drones are produced by parthenogenesis.

questions.text: What is the reason for 21st trisomy?
questions.answer: Non-disjunction of autosomes during gamete formation.

questions.text: Give example of X-monosomy.
questions.answer: Turner syndrome.

questions.text: Discuss any two points due to which Mendel got success in his experiment.
questions.answer: He selected pure lines, studied one character at a time and maintained large sample size.

questions.text: Give any two points of difference between homozygous and heterozygous.
questions.answer: Homozygous has identical alleles while heterozygous has different alleles for a character.

questions.text: Explain test cross with suitable example.
questions.answer: Test cross helps to determine genotype of dominant individual by crossing with recessive parent.

questions.text: Give an account of incomplete dominance.
questions.answer: In incomplete dominance both alleles express partially resulting in intermediate phenotype.

questions.text: Explain codominance.
questions.answer: In codominance both alleles express equally, e.g., roan coat in cattle.

questions.text: Write an account of chromosomal theory of inheritance.
questions.answer: Chromosomal theory states that genes are located on chromosomes and transmitted through them.

questions.text: Write a note on sex linkage.
questions.answer: Sex linked genes are present on sex chromosomes and show different inheritance patterns.

questions.text: Differentiate between complete and incomplete linkage.
questions.answer: In complete linkage genes are inherited together while in incomplete linkage crossing over occurs.

questions.text: Explain sex determination in birds.
questions.answer: In birds females are heterogametic (ZW) and males are homogametic (ZZ).

questions.text: Give a brief account of thalassemia.
questions.answer: Thalassemia is an autosomal recessive disorder affecting hemoglobin synthesis.

questions.text: Enlist dominant and recessive characters in pea plant.
questions.answer: Axial/terminal flower, green/yellow pod, yellow/green seed colour.

questions.text: Explain pleiotropy with suitable example.
questions.answer: A single gene affecting multiple traits, e.g., sickle cell anemia.

questions.text: Describe structure of sex chromosomes with diagram.
questions.answer: X chromosome is larger while Y chromosome is smaller with fewer genes.

questions.text: Explain autosomal inheritance.
questions.answer: Inheritance of traits controlled by autosomal genes is autosomal inheritance.

questions.text: Explain inheritance of colour blindness.
questions.answer: Colour blindness is X-linked recessive disorder.

questions.text: Explain inheritance of haemophilia.
questions.answer: Haemophilia is X-linked recessive disorder affecting blood clotting.

questions.text: Explain sex determination in humans.
questions.answer: Sex is determined by type of sperm fertilizing ovum.

questions.text: Write a note on Down syndrome.
questions.answer: Down syndrome is caused by trisomy of chromosome 21.

questions.text: Explain Klinefelter syndrome.
questions.answer: Klinefelter syndrome occurs due to XXY condition in males.

questions.text: Explain Turner syndrome.
questions.answer: Turner syndrome occurs due to monosomy X (XO) in females.

questions.text: Define inheritance. Give statements for various laws of inheritance.
questions.answer: Inheritance is transmission of traits from parents to offspring. Laws include dominance, segregation and independent assortment.

questions.text: Explain intragenic and intergenic interaction with example.
questions.answer: Intragenic interaction occurs within same gene while intergenic interaction occurs between different genes.

questions.text: Explain structure of chromosome with labelled diagram.
questions.answer: Chromosome consists of chromatids, centromere, telomere and chromonema.

questions.text: Explain inheritance of colour blindness with chart.
questions.answer: Colour blindness is inherited as X-linked recessive trait.

questions.text: Explain inheritance of haemophilia with suitable chart.
questions.answer: Haemophilia is inherited as X-linked recessive disorder.

questions.text: Which of the following represents incomplete dominance?
questions.answer: Mirabilis jalapa flower colour

questions.text: In a test cross, the individual is crossed with:
questions.answer: Homozygous recessive

questions.text: State Mendel's law of dominance.
questions.answer: When two contrasting alleles are present together, only one expresses itself in the phenotype and is called dominant.

questions.text: Define codominance with an example.
questions.answer: In codominance, both alleles express themselves equally in heterozygous condition. Example: AB blood group.

questions.text: Explain incomplete dominance with a suitable example.
questions.answer: In incomplete dominance, neither allele is completely dominant; heterozygote shows intermediate phenotype, e.g., Mirabilis jalapa.

questions.text: Explain pleiotropy.
questions.answer: Pleiotropy is the phenomenon where a single gene influences multiple phenotypic traits.

questions.text: What is polygenic inheritance? Give an example.
questions.answer: Polygenic inheritance involves multiple genes controlling a single trait, e.g., human skin colour.

questions.text: Explain Mendel's monohybrid cross with phenotypic and genotypic ratios.
questions.answer: A cross between two individuals differing in one trait gives 3:1 phenotypic and 1:2:1 genotypic ratios in F2 generation.

questions.text: Explain dihybrid cross with expected ratios.
questions.answer: A cross involving two traits shows 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio in F2 generation due to independent assortment.

questions.text: Variation is important for survival of species.
questions.answer: Variations help organisms adapt to changing environment and ensure survival and evolution.

chapters.title: Molecular Basis of Inheritance
chapters.description: Study of DNA structure, replication, transcription, translation, gene expression, genetic code, regulation of gene activity, mutations, and concepts of genomics and proteomics.
learningObjectives: Explain the structure and functions of DNA and RNA.
Understand DNA replication and enzymes involved.
Describe transcription and translation processes.
Interpret the genetic code and protein synthesis.
Understand gene regulation, mutations, and modern molecular biology applications.

questions.text: DNA is made up of:
questions.answer: Nucleotides

questions.text: Define a gene.
questions.answer: A gene is a specific segment of DNA that codes for a particular protein or functional RNA.

questions.text: What is semi-conservative DNA replication?
questions.answer: Semi-conservative replication means each new DNA molecule consists of one parental strand and one newly synthesized strand.

questions.text: Differentiate between transcription and translation.
questions.answer: Transcription is the synthesis of RNA from DNA template, whereas translation is the synthesis of protein from mRNA with the help of tRNA and ribosomes.

questions.text: Which codon is a start codon?
questions.answer: AUG

questions.text: Explain the role of helicase enzyme in DNA replication.
questions.answer: Helicase unwinds and separates the two DNA strands by breaking hydrogen bonds, creating the replication fork.

questions.text: What is a mutation? Give an example.
questions.answer: A mutation is a sudden heritable change in DNA sequence. Example: Sickle-cell anemia caused by a point mutation in the β-globin gene.

questions.text: Describe the process of transcription in detail.
questions.answer: Transcription involves: 1. **Initiation** – RNA polymerase binds to promoter and unwinds DNA. 2. **Elongation** – RNA nucleotides pair with complementary DNA bases forming mRNA. 3. **Termination** – Polymerase reaches terminator sequence and releases mRNA. In eukaryotes, mRNA undergoes capping, polyadenylation, and splicing.

questions.text: Explain the lac operon model of gene regulation.
questions.answer: The lac operon in bacteria is regulated by lactose availability. - In absence of lactose, the repressor binds operator preventing transcription. - In presence of lactose, it binds repressor, inactivating it, allowing transcription of genes for lactose metabolism. This demonstrates inducible gene regulation.

questions.text: Discuss the central dogma of molecular biology.
questions.answer: The central dogma states that genetic information flows from DNA → RNA → Protein. DNA replicates, is transcribed into RNA, and RNA is translated into proteins, which determine phenotype. It explains gene expression at molecular level.

questions.text: Find the odd one out
questions.answer: H3

questions.text: What happened when heat killed S-cells along with live R-cells were injected into mice?
options: Mice died and showed live S-cells
Mice survived and showed live S-cells
Mice died and showed live R-cells
Mice died and showed dead R-cells
questions.answer: Mice died and showed live S-cells

questions.text: Find out the double ring compound
questions.answer: Adenine

questions.text: If a DNA has 20 adenine and 30 cytosine bases, total purine bases are
Semiconservative mechanism of DNA replication was detected using
During DNA replication, separation of DNA strands is prevented from recoiling by
questions.answer: SSBP

questions.text: Whole protein synthesis is related with
questions.answer: Genetic code is triplet

questions.text: Enzyme required for peptide bond formation is
questions.answer: Peptidyl transferase

questions.text: DNA segments are reunited after splicing by
questions.answer: RNA ligase

questions.text: In lac operon, lactose acts as
questions.answer: Inducer

questions.text: DNA segment has 75 cytosine and 40 thymine nucleotides. Total phosphates are
What is the principle of DNA profiling?
questions.answer: Identification of individuals using restriction fragment length polymorphism of DNA.

questions.text: What is southern blotting?
questions.answer: Technique of transferring DNA fragments from gel to membrane for hybridization.

questions.text: What is an operon?
questions.answer: A unit of coordinated gene regulation consisting of promoter, operator and structural genes.

questions.text: What is role of Mg2+ in translation?
questions.answer: Acts as cofactor for joining ribosomal subunits.

questions.text: What is mutation?
questions.answer: Sudden change in genetic material causing variation.

questions.text: Define heterochromatin.
questions.answer: Condensed, genetically inactive region of chromosome.

questions.text: What is SSBP?
questions.answer: Single strand binding proteins prevent recoiling of DNA strands.

questions.text: Define RFLP.
questions.answer: Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism.

questions.text: What is central dogma?
questions.answer: Flow of genetic information from DNA to RNA to protein.

questions.text: Differentiate between euchromatin and heterochromatin.
questions.answer: Euchromatin is transcriptionally active while heterochromatin is inactive.

questions.text: Define mutation and its types.
questions.answer: Mutation is sudden genetic change. Types are point and frameshift mutations.

questions.text: Explain role of lactose in lac operon.
questions.answer: Lactose acts as inducer by binding to repressor.

questions.text: Describe Hershey-Chase experiment.
questions.answer: Proved DNA is genetic material using bacteriophages.

questions.text: Explain DNA packaging in prokaryotes.
questions.answer: DNA is circular and supercoiled with proteins.

questions.text: Explain Avery–MacLeod–McCarty experiment.
questions.answer: Proved DNA as transforming principle.

questions.text: Explain Griffith's experiment.
questions.answer: Demonstrated bacterial transformation.

questions.text: Describe genetic code.
questions.answer: Genetic code is triplet, degenerate and universal.

questions.text: What is nucleosome?
questions.answer: DNA wrapped around histone octamer.

questions.text: Explain Okazaki fragments.
questions.answer: Short DNA fragments formed on lagging strand.

questions.text: Describe characteristics of genetic code.
questions.answer: Triplet, degenerate, non-overlapping and universal.

questions.text: Explain Meselson and Stahl experiment.
questions.answer: Proved semiconservative replication using N15 isotope.

questions.text: Explain operon model.
questions.answer: Gene regulation model proposed by Jacob and Monod.

questions.text: Explain transcription in eukaryotes.
questions.answer: DNA transcribed to RNA followed by processing.

questions.text: Explain translation mechanism.
questions.answer: Protein synthesis occurs on ribosomes.

questions.text: Describe semiconservative replication of DNA with diagram.
questions.answer: DNA replication produces one parental and one new strand.

questions.text: Explain mechanism of translation with diagram.
questions.answer: Translation occurs in initiation, elongation and termination steps.

questions.text: Explain DNA fingerprinting technique.
questions.answer: Technique used for identification based on DNA polymorphism.

questions.text: Explain lac operon with diagram.
questions.answer: Regulated gene expression system in bacteria.

questions.text: Describe structure of nucleosome with diagram.
questions.answer: DNA wrapped around histone octamer forming nucleosome.

questions.text: The bonds that hold the two strands of DNA together are:
questions.answer: Hydrogen bonds

questions.text: Which enzyme is responsible for the synthesis of RNA on a DNA template?
questions.answer: RNA polymerase

questions.text: Define transcription.
questions.answer: Transcription is the process of synthesis of RNA from a DNA template.

questions.text: What is genetic code?
questions.answer: Genetic code is a sequence of three nucleotides (codon) that codes for a specific amino acid.

questions.text: Explain the concept of degeneracy of genetic code.
questions.answer: Degeneracy means that more than one codon can code for the same amino acid.

questions.text: Explain the role of tRNA in protein synthesis.
questions.answer: tRNA carries specific amino acids to ribosomes and matches its anticodon with codon on mRNA during translation.

questions.text: Explain DNA replication with suitable examples.
questions.answer: DNA replication is a semi-conservative process involving unwinding, complementary base pairing and synthesis of new strands.

questions.text: Explain transcription in prokaryotes.
questions.answer: In prokaryotes, transcription occurs in cytoplasm and involves initiation, elongation and termination by RNA polymerase.

questions.text: Describe translation process in protein synthesis.
questions.answer: Translation occurs on ribosomes involving initiation, elongation and termination to form polypeptide chain.

questions.text: Genetic code is universal.
questions.answer: Because the same codon specifies the same amino acid in almost all organisms.

chapters.title: Origin and Evolution of Life
chapters.description: Study of theories of origin of life, early earth conditions, chemical evolution, biological evolution, Darwinism, Lamarckism, Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, and evidences of evolution.
learningObjectives: Understand early conditions on Earth and theories of origin of life.
Explain chemical evolution and Miller-Urey's experiment.
Differentiate between Lamarckism and Darwinism.
Interpret Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium and factors affecting it.
Recognize evidences of evolution and human evolutionary stages.

questions.text: Which scientist performed the experiment supporting chemical evolution?
questions.answer: Miller and Urey

questions.text: Define evolution.
questions.answer: Evolution is the gradual change in the heritable characteristics of populations over generations.

questions.text: State any two evidences supporting evolution.
questions.answer: Fossil records and homologous organs are strong evidences supporting evolution.

questions.text: What is natural selection according to Darwin?
questions.answer: Natural selection is the process where organisms with favorable traits survive and reproduce, passing those traits to the next generation.

questions.text: Which of the following violates Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium?
questions.answer: Migration

questions.text: Explain Lamarck's theory with an example.
questions.answer: Lamarck proposed that acquired characters are inherited. Example: Giraffes developed long necks because they stretched to reach leaves, and this trait was passed to offspring.

questions.text: What is speciation?
questions.answer: Speciation is the formation of new species through genetic divergence, often due to isolation and natural selection.

questions.text: Describe the Miller-Urey experiment and its significance.
questions.answer: Miller and Urey created an apparatus simulating early Earth conditions with gases like methane, ammonia, hydrogen, and water vapor. Electric sparks simulated lightning. After several days, organic molecules like amino acids formed. This supported chemical evolution and the idea that life originated from simple organic compounds.

questions.text: Explain the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium and factors affecting it.
questions.answer: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium states that allele frequencies remain constant in a population if conditions like random mating, no mutation, no migration, large population, and no selection are met. Factors disrupting equilibrium include mutation, migration, genetic drift, natural selection, and non-random mating.

questions.text: Discuss the major stages in human evolution.
questions.answer: Human evolution includes: 1. **Australopithecus** – bipedal, small brain. 2. **Homo habilis** – tool user. 3. **Homo erectus** – upright posture, fire use. 4. **Neanderthals** – strong build, cultural development. 5. **Homo sapiens** – modern humans with advanced intelligence and culture.

questions.text: _____ is considered as connecting link between ape and man.
questions.answer: Australopithecus

questions.text: Humans are most closely related to
questions.answer: Chimpanzees

questions.text: The proportion of an allele in the gene pool is called
questions.answer: gene frequency

questions.text: Transfer of genes to a non-homologous chromosome is called
questions.answer: translocation

questions.text: Random fluctuation in allele frequency by chance is called
questions.answer: genetic drift

questions.text: Define Mendelian population.
questions.answer: A population consisting of interbreeding individuals sharing a common gene pool.

questions.text: Define gene pool.
questions.answer: The total genetic information present in a Mendelian population.

questions.text: Who is known as Handy man?
questions.answer: Homo habilis

questions.text: Name the ancestor known as man with ape brain.
questions.answer: Australopithecus

questions.text: Whose fossils were found in Shivalik hills?
questions.answer: Ramapithecus

questions.text: Mention any two developments that helped humans move safely on land.
questions.answer: Bipedal locomotion and erect posture.

questions.text: What is hybrid sterility?
questions.answer: Hybrids become sterile due to failure of proper gametogenesis.

questions.text: Describe modern man.
questions.answer: Modern man (Homo sapiens) has erect posture, large cranial capacity and developed culture.

questions.text: Differentiate between New world and Old world monkeys.
questions.answer: New world monkeys have long prehensile tails, while old world monkeys have short non-prehensile tails.

questions.text: What is hybrid sterility? Give one example.
questions.answer: Hybrids are sterile due to meiotic failure, e.g., mule.

questions.text: Distinguish between Australopithecus and Neanderthal man.
questions.answer: Australopithecus had smaller cranial capacity, while Neanderthal man had larger brain and advanced features.

questions.text: Distinguish between Homo erectus and Neanderthal man.
questions.answer: Homo erectus was earlier and used fire, while Neanderthal man was more intelligent and used tools.

questions.text: Name any three pre-mating isolating mechanisms.
questions.answer: Habitat isolation, seasonal isolation and ethological isolation.

questions.text: Name any three post-mating isolating mechanisms.
questions.answer: Gamete mortality, zygote mortality and hybrid sterility.

questions.text: Explain geographical isolation.
questions.answer: Geographical barriers prevent interbreeding leading to formation of new species.

questions.text: Explain chromosomal aberrations.
questions.answer: Structural changes in chromosomes like deletion, duplication, inversion and translocation.

questions.text: Write a note on Homo habilis.
questions.answer: Homo habilis had stone tools, larger brain and lived about 2 million years ago.

questions.text: Explain genetic drift.
questions.answer: Random changes in allele frequency due to chance events.

questions.text: Explain genetic variation and its causes.
questions.answer: Genetic variation arises due to mutation, recombination, gene flow and genetic drift.

questions.text: Explain natural selection with reference to industrial melanism.
questions.answer: Industrial melanism in peppered moth shows survival advantage due to environmental changes.

questions.text: The theory of chemical evolution was proposed by:
questions.answer: Oparin and Haldane

questions.text: Which experiment provided experimental evidence for chemical evolution?
questions.answer: Miller–Urey experiment

questions.text: What is abiogenesis?
questions.answer: Abiogenesis is the origin of life from non-living matter.

questions.text: Define homologous organs.
questions.answer: Homologous organs are organs with similar origin and basic structure but different functions.

questions.text: Explain Lamarckism.
questions.answer: Lamarckism proposes that characters acquired during lifetime are inherited by next generation.

questions.text: Explain natural selection with reference to industrial melanism.
questions.answer: Dark coloured moths survived better in polluted environment due to camouflage, proving natural selection.

questions.text: What is adaptive radiation? Give an example.
questions.answer: Adaptive radiation is evolution of multiple species from a common ancestor adapting to different habitats. Example: Darwin's finches.

questions.text: Explain Darwin's theory of natural selection.
questions.answer: Organisms produce more offspring; struggle for existence; survival of the fittest; favourable variations are selected.

questions.text: Explain evidences of evolution from morphology and anatomy.
questions.answer: Homologous organs show common ancestry; analogous organs show convergent evolution.

questions.text: Evolution is a continuous process.
questions.answer: Because organisms constantly undergo genetic variations and natural selection over generations.

chapters.title: Plant Water Relation
chapters.description: Study of water absorption, water potential, diffusion, osmosis, plasmolysis, transpiration, ascent of sap, and factors regulating water movement in plants.
learningObjectives: Understand basic principles of water movement in plants.
Explain osmosis, diffusion, imbibition, and water potential.
Describe mechanisms of absorption and conduction of water.
Understand transpiration and its significance.
Explain ascent of sap and forces involved in water transport.

questions.text: Movement of molecules from higher concentration to lower concentration is called:
questions.answer: Diffusion

questions.text: Define osmosis.
questions.answer: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential to lower water potential across a semipermeable membrane.

questions.text: What is water potential?
questions.answer: Water potential (Ψ) is the potential energy of water, determining the direction of its movement. Pure water has the highest water potential (Ψ = 0).

questions.text: Explain plasmolysis with an example.
questions.answer: Plasmolysis is the shrinkage of the cytoplasm away from the cell wall when a cell is placed in a hypertonic solution. Example: Onion peel cells in concentrated salt solution.

questions.text: Which tissue is mainly responsible for upward conduction of water?
questions.answer: Xylem

questions.text: What is transpiration?
questions.answer: Transpiration is the loss of water in the form of vapor from aerial parts of plants, mainly through stomata.

questions.text: Explain imbibition.
questions.answer: Imbibition is the adsorption of water by hydrophilic substances like cellulose and seeds, causing them to swell.

questions.text: Describe the cohesion-tension theory of ascent of sap.
questions.answer: The cohesion-tension theory states that water molecules stick together by cohesion and adhere to xylem vessels. Transpiration pull creates negative pressure, which pulls water upward through the plant from roots to leaves.

questions.text: Explain the apoplast and symplast pathways of water movement.
questions.answer: In the apoplast pathway, water moves through cell walls and intercellular spaces. In the symplast pathway, water moves from cell to cell through the cytoplasm via plasmodesmata. The endodermis forces water into the symplast before entering the xylem.

questions.text: Discuss the significance of transpiration in plants.
questions.answer: Transpiration helps in cooling the plant, maintaining turgor, absorption and upward movement of water, mineral transport, and creating transpiration pull for ascent of sap.

questions.text: Water present in the form of hydrated oxides of silicon and aluminium is called
questions.answer: Combined water

questions.text: Most plant cells and tissues constitute _____ % water
_____ type of tissue is present in epiphytic roots
questions.answer: Velamen

questions.text: In the zone of absorption, epidermal cells form unicellular hair like extensions called
questions.answer: Root hairs

questions.text: Outer layer of root hair is made up of
questions.answer: Pectin

questions.text: Inner layer of root hair is made up of
questions.answer: Cellulose

questions.text: Cell wall is
questions.answer: Freely permeable

questions.text: Plasma membrane is
questions.answer: Selectively permeable

questions.text: Root hair is _____ extension of epiblema cells
questions.answer: Cytoplasmic

questions.text: Fine soil particles imbibe or adsorb water and hold it. This is called
questions.answer: Hygroscopic water

questions.text: Why water acts as a thermal buffer?
questions.answer: Due to high specific heat, high heat of vaporization and high heat of fusion.

questions.text: Define root hair.
questions.answer: Cytoplasmic extension of epiblema cell is called root hair.

questions.text: What is gravitational water?
questions.answer: Water that percolates deep in soil due to gravity.

questions.text: What is hygroscopic water?
questions.answer: Water tightly held by fine soil particles and unavailable to plants.

questions.text: What is combined water?
questions.answer: Water present in hydrated oxides of minerals.

questions.text: What is capillary water?
questions.answer: Water held in soil pores and available for absorption.

questions.text: Which tissue is present in epiphytic roots?
questions.answer: Velamen

questions.text: From which cells root hair originates?
questions.answer: Epiblema cells

questions.text: What is the composition of inner layer of root hair?
questions.answer: Cellulose

questions.text: What is the composition of outer layer of root hair?
questions.answer: Pectin

questions.text: Why water is called as elixir of life?
questions.answer: Water is best solvent, transport medium, thermal buffer and essential for biochemical reactions.

questions.text: What are the different types of water present in soil?
questions.answer: Gravitational water, hygroscopic water, combined water and capillary water.

questions.text: Explain structure of root hair.
questions.answer: Root hair is a unicellular, thin-walled, tubular extension with large vacuole.

questions.text: In which form water is available to roots?
questions.answer: Capillary water is available for absorption.

questions.text: Explain properties of water.
questions.answer: High specific heat, cohesion, adhesion and solvent property.

questions.text: Explain morphological structure of root.
questions.answer: Root has regions of division, elongation, absorption and maturation.

questions.text: Draw and label root tip showing root hair zone.
questions.answer: Diagram shows meristematic region, elongation zone, root hair zone and maturation zone.

questions.text: Write a note on morphological structure of root.
questions.answer: Root shows four regions from apex to base performing specific functions.

questions.text: How roots act as water absorbing organs?
questions.answer: Root hairs increase surface area and absorb capillary water.

questions.text: Explain types of soil water.
questions.answer: Soil water includes gravitational, hygroscopic, combined and capillary water.

questions.text: Explain structure of root hair with diagram.
questions.answer: Root hair is a unicellular extension with thin wall, large vacuole and selectively permeable membrane.

questions.text: Explain properties of water in detail.
questions.answer: Water acts as solvent, thermal buffer and medium for biochemical reactions.

questions.text: Explain how roots absorb water.
questions.answer: Roots absorb capillary water through root hairs by diffusion and osmosis.

questions.text: The movement of water across a semipermeable membrane from higher water potential to lower water potential is called:
questions.answer: Osmosis

questions.text: Which of the following is responsible for ascent of sap in tall trees?
questions.answer: Transpiration pull

questions.text: Define diffusion.
questions.answer: Diffusion is the passive movement of molecules from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.

questions.text: What is water potential?
questions.answer: Water potential is the potential energy of water which determines the direction of movement of water.

questions.text: Explain imbibition.
questions.answer: Imbibition is the absorption of water by hydrophilic colloids causing swelling, e.g., swelling of seeds.

questions.text: Explain root pressure.
questions.answer: Root pressure is the positive pressure developed in roots due to osmotic absorption of water, pushing sap upwards.

questions.text: Explain transpiration.
questions.answer: Transpiration is the loss of water in the form of vapour from aerial parts of plants, mainly through stomata.

questions.text: Explain ascent of sap with reference to transpiration pull theory.
questions.answer: According to transpiration pull theory, evaporation of water from leaves creates negative pressure which pulls water upward through xylem.

questions.text: Describe factors affecting transpiration.
questions.answer: Light, temperature, humidity, wind velocity and leaf area affect transpiration rate.

questions.text: Transpiration is called a necessary evil.
questions.answer: Because it causes water loss but is essential for ascent of sap, cooling and mineral transport.

chapters.title: Plant Growth and Mineral Nutrition
chapters.description: Study of plant growth phases, growth regulators, mineral absorption, essential elements, deficiency symptoms, nitrogen cycle, and role of macronutrients and micronutrients.
learningObjectives: Understand phases and characteristics of plant growth.
Identify essential mineral nutrients and their functions.
Explain mechanisms of mineral absorption.
Describe nitrogen cycle and nitrogen fixation.
Recognize deficiency symptoms of various nutrients.

questions.text: Which of the following is a micronutrient?
questions.answer: Iron

questions.text: Define meristematic growth.
questions.answer: Meristematic growth refers to growth due to continuous cell division in meristematic tissues.

questions.text: Name any two plant growth regulators and state their functions.
questions.answer: Auxins promote cell elongation; cytokinins promote cell division.

questions.text: What is the significance of nitrogen in plant nutrition?
questions.answer: Nitrogen is essential for synthesis of proteins, nucleic acids, chlorophyll, and enzymes.

questions.text: Chlorosis is caused due to deficiency of:
questions.answer: Iron

questions.text: Differentiate between macronutrients and micronutrients.
questions.answer: Macronutrients are required in large amounts (e.g., N, P, K), whereas micronutrients are needed in trace amounts (e.g., Fe, Zn, Cu).

questions.text: What is biological nitrogen fixation?
questions.answer: Biological nitrogen fixation is conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia by microorganisms like Rhizobium.

questions.text: Describe the sigmoid (S-shaped) growth curve in plants.
questions.answer: The sigmoid growth curve consists of lag phase (slow growth), log phase (rapid exponential growth), and stationary phase (growth slows due to limited resources). It represents the typical growth pattern of plant tissues.

questions.text: Explain passive and active absorption of minerals by plants.
questions.answer: Passive absorption occurs without energy expenditure through diffusion. Active absorption requires ATP and involves carrier proteins moving ions against concentration gradients.

questions.text: Discuss the nitrogen cycle and its significance in plant growth.
questions.answer: The nitrogen cycle includes nitrogen fixation, ammonification, nitrification, and denitrification. It converts atmospheric nitrogen into usable forms like nitrates. This maintains soil fertility and supports plant growth.

questions.text: A farmer is fed up of weeds in his wheat farm. Which chemical can he use to overcome the problem?
Gibberellins are synthesised from
questions.answer: Mevalonic acid

questions.text: First natural cytokinin was obtained from
questions.answer: Maize grains

questions.text: Which hormone is gaseous in nature?
questions.answer: Ethylene

questions.text: Bolting of beet is caused by
questions.answer: Gibberellin

questions.text: Natural auxin present in plants is
questions.answer: IAA

questions.text: Flowering in litchi can be induced by
questions.answer: NAA

questions.text: Epinastry of flower is caused by
questions.answer: Ethylene

questions.text: Which hormone breaks seed dormancy?
questions.answer: Gibberellin

questions.text: Anti-transpirant hormone is
questions.answer: Abscisic acid

questions.text: Which chemical is used for artificial ripening of fruits?
questions.answer: Ethylene

questions.text: Why is ABA known as anti-transpirant?
questions.answer: It closes stomata by causing efflux of K+ ions.

questions.text: Name the tissue that transports hormones in plants.
questions.answer: Xylem

questions.text: Name the first hormone discovered in plants.
questions.answer: Auxin

questions.text: Biological name of fungus from which gibberellins were isolated.
questions.answer: Gibberella fujikuroi

questions.text: Name given to first cytokinin discovered by Skoog and Miller.
questions.answer: Kinetin

questions.text: Name gaseous plant hormone.
questions.answer: Ethylene

questions.text: Standard bioassay method for auxins.
questions.answer: Avena curvature test

questions.text: Which hormone can overcome vernalization?
questions.answer: Gibberellins

questions.text: Name the phenomenon controlled by auxin at apex.
questions.answer: Apical dominance

questions.text: Match epinasty of flower with the hormone responsible.
questions.answer: Epinasty of flower – Ethylene

questions.text: How can a gardener give bushy appearance to plants?
questions.answer: By pruning to remove apical dominance.

questions.text: What is apical dominance?
questions.answer: Inhibition of lateral buds by apical bud.

questions.text: Write any two functions of gibberellins.
questions.answer: Stem elongation and bolting.

questions.text: Write any two functions of cytokinins.
questions.answer: Cell division and delay of senescence.

questions.text: Write two functions of ethylene.
questions.answer: Fruit ripening and senescence.

questions.text: Name the first plant hormone, its source and function.
questions.answer: Auxin, oat coleoptile, promotes cell elongation.

questions.text: Write names of gaseous hormone, its effect and source.
questions.answer: Ethylene, fruit ripening, ripening fruits.

questions.text: Explain role of gibberellins in plants.
questions.answer: They promote stem elongation, bolting and flowering.

questions.text: Explain apical dominance with example.
questions.answer: Apical bud suppresses lateral buds, e.g. sunflower.

questions.text: Name phytohormones related with given phenomena.
questions.answer: Apical dominance – Auxin; Bolting – Gibberellin; Fruit ripening – Ethylene; Anti-transpirant – Abscisic acid

questions.text: Write full forms of IAA, IBA, NAA and 2,4-D.
questions.answer: IAA – Indole acetic acid; IBA – Indole butyric acid; NAA – Naphthalene acetic acid; 2,4-D – 2,4-Dichlorophenoxy acetic acid

questions.text: Explain functions of different plant hormones.
questions.answer: Auxins promote elongation, gibberellins promote bolting, cytokinins promote division, ethylene causes ripening, ABA causes dormancy.

questions.text: Which of the following is a micronutrient essential for plants?
questions.answer: Zinc

questions.text: The hormone responsible for cell elongation in plants is:
questions.answer: Auxin

questions.text: Define macronutrients in plants.
questions.answer: Macronutrients are elements required by plants in large quantities for normal growth and development.

questions.text: What are plant growth regulators?
questions.answer: Plant growth regulators are organic substances that influence physiological processes of plants at low concentrations.

questions.text: Explain nitrogen cycle.
questions.answer: Nitrogen cycle involves nitrogen fixation, nitrification, assimilation, ammonification and denitrification.

questions.text: Explain role of auxins in plant growth.
questions.answer: Auxins promote cell elongation, apical dominance, root initiation and tropic responses.

questions.text: Explain deficiency symptoms of nitrogen in plants.
questions.answer: Nitrogen deficiency causes chlorosis, stunted growth and reduced protein synthesis.

questions.text: Explain the role of plant growth regulators with examples.
questions.answer: Auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins, ethylene and ABA regulate growth, flowering, senescence and dormancy.

questions.text: Describe biological nitrogen fixation.
questions.answer: Nitrogen fixation is conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia by Rhizobium in legume root nodules.

questions.text: Micronutrients are required in very small quantities.
questions.answer: Because they act mainly as enzyme activators and cofactors.

chapters.title: Respiration and Circulation
chapters.description: Study of respiratory mechanisms in humans, exchange and transport of gases, structure and working of the heart, cardiac cycle, blood vessels, and regulation of circulation.
topics: Transport of Oxygen and Carbon Dioxide
learningObjectives: Understand the structure and mechanism of human respiration.
Explain gaseous exchange at lungs and tissues.
Describe oxygen and carbon dioxide transport in blood.
Understand structure of the heart and working of cardiac cycle.
Explain blood circulation routes and blood pressure regulation.

questions.text: Which pigment is responsible for transport of oxygen in humans?
questions.answer: Hemoglobin

questions.text: Define tidal volume.
questions.answer: Tidal volume is the amount of air inhaled or exhaled during normal quiet breathing, approximately 500 mL.

questions.text: What is double circulation?
questions.answer: Double circulation refers to the separate pulmonary and systemic circuits in which blood passes through the heart twice during one complete circulation.

questions.text: Name the stages of the cardiac cycle.
questions.answer: Atrial systole, ventricular systole, and joint diastole.

questions.text: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from lungs to heart?
questions.answer: Pulmonary vein

questions.text: Explain Bohr effect.
questions.answer: Bohr effect refers to the decrease in hemoglobin's affinity for oxygen due to increased CO₂ concentration or lowered pH, enhancing oxygen release in tissues.

questions.text: What is systolic and diastolic blood pressure?
questions.answer: Systolic pressure is the pressure in arteries during ventricular contraction; diastolic pressure is the pressure during ventricular relaxation.

questions.text: Describe the mechanism of breathing in humans.
questions.answer: Breathing involves inspiration and expiration. During inspiration, diaphragm contracts and flattens, external intercostal muscles raise ribs, increasing thoracic volume, causing air to flow into lungs. During expiration, diaphragm relaxes, ribs move down, thoracic volume decreases, forcing air out.

questions.text: Explain the exchange of gases at alveoli and tissues.
questions.answer: At alveoli: O₂ diffuses from alveolar air to blood due to higher partial pressure, while CO₂ diffuses from blood to alveoli. At tissues: O₂ diffuses from blood to cells and CO₂ diffuses from cells to blood due to concentration gradients.

questions.text: Describe the structure of the human heart and its working.
questions.answer: The heart has four chambers: right and left atria, right and left ventricles. Valves ensure one-way flow. Deoxygenated blood enters right atrium → right ventricle → lungs. Oxygenated blood from lungs enters left atrium → left ventricle → pumped to body. Heart functions through rhythmic contraction and relaxation known as the cardiac cycle.

questions.text: In human respiration, chemical energy is released in the form of
questions.answer: ATP

questions.text: Alveoli provide the surface area for exchange of
questions.answer: Gases

questions.text: The movement of diaphragm, intercostal muscles and rib cage helps in
questions.answer: Respiration

questions.text: The volume of air that remains in the lungs after maximum expiration is
Due to absence of respiratory pigment, transport of respiratory gases does not take place in
questions.answer: Cockroach

questions.text: Which of the following has thickest wall?
questions.answer: Left ventricle

questions.text: The phase of contraction of heart is termed as
questions.answer: Systole

questions.text: The free edges of cuspid valves are attached to papillary muscles by fibres called
questions.answer: Chordae tendinae

questions.text: Ventricular depolarization is represented by
questions.answer: QRS complex

questions.text: The erythropoietic tissue in adult is mainly found in
questions.answer: Red bone marrow

questions.text: Name the cartilage which divides the nasal cavity into right and left chambers.
questions.answer: Mesethmoid cartilage

questions.text: Give the function of epiglottis.
questions.answer: It prevents entry of food into trachea.

questions.text: Define total lung capacity.
questions.answer: Maximum amount of air that lungs can hold after forceful inspiration.

questions.text: Define haematology.
questions.answer: The study of blood is called haematology.

questions.text: Which type of blood flows through pulmonary veins?
questions.answer: Oxygenated blood

questions.text: Define Bohr effect and Haldane effect.
questions.answer: Bohr effect refers to reduced oxygen affinity of haemoglobin at high CO2 concentration. Haldane effect states that deoxygenated blood carries more CO2.

questions.text: Give any two effects of carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.answer: CO forms carboxyhaemoglobin and prevents oxygen transport causing tissue hypoxia.

questions.text: Name the pigment and enzyme found in erythrocytes.
questions.answer: Pigment – Haemoglobin; Enzyme – Carbonic anhydrase.

questions.text: How does a portal vein differ from a normal vein?
questions.answer: Portal vein starts as capillaries and ends in capillaries of another organ.

questions.text: Distinguish between inspiration and expiration.
questions.answer: Inspiration is active with increased thoracic volume; expiration is passive with decreased thoracic volume.

questions.text: Write a note on Hering–Breuer reflex.
questions.answer: Stretch receptors in lungs inhibit inspiration when lungs are inflated and regulate breathing rhythm.

questions.text: Define Hamburger's phenomenon.
questions.answer: Exchange of chloride and bicarbonate ions between RBCs and plasma during CO2 transport.

questions.text: Write a note on coagulation of blood.
questions.answer: Conversion of fibrinogen into fibrin forming clot through clotting factors.

questions.text: Define hypertension. Explain coronary artery disease.
questions.answer: Hypertension is persistent high blood pressure. CAD occurs due to blockage of coronary arteries.

questions.text: Explain exchange of gases between alveolus and capillary with diagram.
questions.answer: Oxygen diffuses from alveoli to blood and carbon dioxide diffuses from blood to alveoli due to partial pressure gradient.

questions.text: With the help of chart identify and write the function of any four leucocytes.
questions.answer: Neutrophils – phagocytosis; Eosinophils – destroy antigen-antibody complex; Basophils – secrete histamine; Lymphocytes – immunity.

questions.text: Draw labelled diagram of internal structure of human heart and write functions of valves.
questions.answer: Tricuspid valve prevents backflow in right atrium; bicuspid valve prevents backflow in left atrium.

questions.text: Identify 'A' from the following ECG.
questions.answer: 'A' represents the R–R interval, i.e. one complete cardiac cycle.

questions.text: Identify the pulse point 'A' from below given diagram.
questions.answer: 'A' represents a ball and socket joint (shoulder joint).

questions.text: Draw the chart of double circulation and label A, B, C and D.
questions.answer: A. Vena cava, B. Left atrium, C. Right ventricle, D. Pulmonary artery.

questions.text: Which pigment is responsible for oxygen transport in human blood?
questions.answer: Haemoglobin

questions.text: The pacemaker of human heart is:
questions.answer: SA node

questions.text: Define respiration.
questions.answer: Respiration is the biochemical process of oxidation of food substances to release energy.

questions.text: What is cardiac cycle?
questions.answer: Cardiac cycle is the sequence of events occurring during one complete heartbeat, including systole and diastole.

questions.text: Explain aerobic respiration.
questions.answer: Aerobic respiration is the complete oxidation of glucose in presence of oxygen to release energy, CO₂ and water.

questions.text: Explain transport of oxygen in blood.
questions.answer: Oxygen is transported mainly by haemoglobin as oxyhaemoglobin and partly dissolved in plasma.

questions.text: Draw a neat labelled diagram of the conducting system of human heart.
questions.answer: Diagram showing SA node, AV node, Bundle of His and Purkinje fibres.

questions.text: Draw a neat labelled diagram of alveolus.
questions.answer: Diagram showing alveolar wall, capillaries and air space.

questions.text: Explain the mechanism of breathing in humans.
questions.answer: Inspiration occurs by contraction of diaphragm and intercostal muscles; expiration is passive due to relaxation.

questions.text: Describe double circulation in humans.
questions.answer: Blood passes twice through the heart in one cycle: pulmonary and systemic circulation.

questions.text: Human heart is called myogenic.
questions.answer: Because the heartbeat originates within the heart muscle itself from SA node.

chapters.title: Control and Coordination
chapters.description: Study of the nervous system, endocrine system, neurons, synapses, reflex action, hormones, and regulation of physiological processes in animals.
topics: Coordination Between Nervous and Endocrine Systems
learningObjectives: Understand the structure of neurons and the mechanism of nerve impulse transmission.
Differentiate between CNS, PNS, and ANS.
Explain reflex action and reflex arc.
Describe endocrine glands and hormone functions.
Understand feedback systems and coordination between nervous and endocrine systems.

questions.text: The structural and functional unit of the nervous system is:
questions.answer: Neuron

questions.text: What is a synapse?
questions.answer: A synapse is a junction between two neurons where nerve impulses are transmitted chemically or electrically.

questions.text: Explain the term reflex action.
questions.answer: Reflex action is an automatic, immediate response to a stimulus, controlled by the spinal cord without involvement of the brain.

questions.text: State any two functions of the autonomic nervous system.
questions.answer: The autonomic nervous system regulates involuntary activities such as heartbeat, digestion, glandular secretion, and smooth muscle contraction.

questions.text: Which gland is known as the master gland?
questions.answer: Pituitary

questions.text: What is the role of myelin sheath in neurons?
questions.answer: The myelin sheath insulates axons, increases speed of nerve impulse conduction, and prevents signal loss.

questions.text: Name two hormones secreted by the adrenal gland and state their functions.
questions.answer: Adrenaline – prepares body for 'fight or flight'; Aldosterone – regulates sodium and potassium balance.

questions.text: Describe the mechanism of nerve impulse transmission across a synapse.
questions.answer: When an impulse reaches the axon terminal, calcium ions enter, causing synaptic vesicles to release neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft. These bind to receptors on the postsynaptic membrane, generating a new impulse. Neurotransmitters are then broken down or reabsorbed.

questions.text: Explain the endocrine system with examples of glands and hormones they secrete.
questions.answer: The endocrine system consists of glands that secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream. Examples: Thyroid secretes thyroxine; Pancreas secretes insulin and glucagon; Pituitary secretes growth hormone; Adrenal secretes adrenaline and aldosterone.

questions.text: Discuss coordination between the nervous and endocrine systems with an example.
questions.answer: Both systems work together to maintain homeostasis. Example: Stress triggers hypothalamus, which stimulates adrenal glands via neural signals to release adrenaline, increasing heart rate and respiration. This illustrates neuroendocrine coordination.

questions.text: Diffuse type of nervous system is seen in
questions.answer: Hydra
