questions.text: Planaria shows _____ type of nervous system.
questions.answer: Ladder

questions.text: In order for a stimulus to be effective, it must have a minimum intensity called
questions.answer: Threshold

questions.text: The resting potential of neuron is
questions.answer: -70 millivolts

questions.text: The third ventricle of brain is connected to the fourth ventricle of brain through
questions.answer: Duct of Sylvius

questions.text: Degeneration of dopamine producing neurons in CNS causes disease
questions.answer: Parkinson's

questions.text: _____ is a mineralocorticoid secreted by adrenal gland.
questions.answer: Aldosterone

questions.text: _____ has an important role in development of immune system by maturation of T lymphocytes.
questions.answer: Thymosin

questions.text: Hypersecretion of growth hormone in childhood causes
questions.answer: Gigantism

questions.text: _____ slows gastric contractions and inhibits secretion of gastric juice.
questions.answer: Entero-gastrone

questions.text: Which cells of PNS secrete myelin sheath around the nerves?
questions.answer: Schwann cells

questions.text: Give function of astrocytes.
questions.answer: They regulate neurotransmission and maintain blood-brain barrier.

questions.text: What is the covering of nerve fascicle called?
questions.answer: Endoneurium

questions.text: Define saltatory conduction.
questions.answer: Rapid transmission of impulse from one node of Ranvier to another.

questions.text: Name hormone secreted by pars intermedia.
questions.answer: Melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH)

questions.text: Which disease is caused by hypersecretion of glucocorticoids?
questions.answer: Cushing's disease

questions.text: Which organ acts as temporary endocrine gland in females?
questions.answer: Placenta

questions.text: Give one role of hormone therapy.
questions.answer: Used in growth hormone deficiency.

questions.text: Name the hormone secreted by pineal gland.
questions.answer: Melatonin

questions.text: Which disease is caused by hyposecretion of vasopressin?
questions.answer: Diabetes insipidus

questions.text: Injury to medulla oblongata causes sudden death. Explain.
questions.answer: It controls vital activities like heartbeat and respiration; injury disrupts them.

questions.text: Which two hormones regulate calcium and phosphorus in blood?
questions.answer: Calcitonin and Parathormone.

questions.text: Describe any two hormones produced by ovaries.
questions.answer: Progesterone and Oestrogen.

questions.text: Name the glucocorticoid used in treatment of allergy and why?
questions.answer: Cortisol because it is immunosuppressive.

questions.text: Name hormone secreted by pineal gland and its function.
questions.answer: Melatonin regulates biological clock.

questions.text: Name three mixed cranial nerves with their numbers.
questions.answer: V–Trigeminal, VII–Facial, X–Vagus.

questions.text: Write a note on meninges of brain.
questions.answer: Dura mater, arachnoid mater and pia mater protect brain and spinal cord.

questions.text: Describe any three functions of hypothalamus.
questions.answer: Regulates temperature, hunger, thirst and pituitary control.

questions.text: Distinguish between cerebrum and cerebellum.
questions.answer: Cerebrum controls intelligence and memory; cerebellum controls balance and posture.

questions.text: Explain mechanism of hormonal action using second messenger.
questions.answer: Hormone binds membrane receptor and activates cAMP or Ca²⁺.

questions.text: Complete table of disorders caused by thyroid gland.
questions.answer: Hyposecretion – Myxoedema, Cretinism; Hypersecretion – Grave's disease.

questions.text: Describe the functional areas of cerebrum.
questions.answer: Motor, sensory, association, visual, auditory and speech areas.

questions.text: Distinguish between sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous system.
questions.answer: Sympathetic increases heart rate and BP; parasympathetic decreases them.

questions.text: Describe hormones secreted by adenohypophysis.
questions.answer: GH, TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH and Prolactin.

questions.text: Write a note on cells of pancreas.
questions.answer: Alpha, beta, delta and PP cells secrete glucagon, insulin, somatostatin and pancreatic polypeptide.

questions.text: Complete the flowchart of conduction of nerve impulse.
questions.answer: Stimulus → Na⁺ influx → depolarization → K⁺ efflux → repolarization → resting potential restored.

questions.text:
Answer the questions after observing the diagram given below.
1) What acts as the first messenger?
2) Why can't hormones like catecholamines enter their target cells through plasma membrane?
3) Name the mode of hormone action shown in the diagram.
questions.answer: 1. First messenger: The hormone itself (e.g., FSH shown in the diagram) acts as the first messenger. 2. Why catecholamines cannot enter the cell through plasma membrane: Catecholamines are polar, water-soluble molecules. Because the plasma membrane is lipid in nature, these hormones cannot diffuse through it and therefore act via membrane receptors. 3. Mode of hormone action shown: Second messenger mechanism

questions.text: Complete the table based on disorders caused due to under secretion or over secretion of Thyroid gland.
questions.answer: 1. Hyposecretion: Adults → Myxoedema, Children → Cretinism. 2. Hypersecretion: Adults → Graves' disease (Exophthalmic goitre), Children → Exophthalmic goitre.

questions.text: Complete the flowchart of the process of conduction of nerve impulse.
questions.answer: Application of stimulus on a resting nerve → Permeability of membrane changes → Sodium (Na⁺) gates open → Influx of Na⁺ ions into axon → Positive ions inside axon increase → Polarity reverses and depolarisation takes place → Repolarisation – potassium (K⁺) gates open → Efflux of K⁺ ions from axon → Resting membrane potential is restored → Axoplasm becomes negatively charged and ECF becomes positive again

questions.text: The functional unit of nervous system is:
questions.answer: Neuron

questions.text: Which hormone regulates blood glucose level?
questions.answer: Insulin

questions.text: Define hormone.
questions.answer: Hormones are chemical messengers secreted by endocrine glands and transported through blood to target organs.

questions.text: What is synapse?
questions.answer: Synapse is the junction between two neurons where transmission of nerve impulse occurs.

questions.text: Explain reflex action.
questions.answer: Reflex action is a rapid, automatic response to a stimulus mediated by spinal cord without conscious control.

questions.text: Explain mechanism of hormone action.
questions.answer: Hormones bind to specific receptors, triggering signal transduction that alters cellular activity.

questions.text: Draw a neat labelled diagram of a neuron.
questions.answer: Diagram showing dendrites, cell body, axon and synaptic knobs.

questions.text: Draw a neat labelled diagram of human brain.
questions.answer: Diagram showing cerebrum, cerebellum, pons and medulla.

questions.text: Explain nervous coordination in humans.
questions.answer: Nervous coordination involves reception of stimulus, transmission via neurons and response through effectors.

questions.text: Describe endocrine glands and their functions.
questions.answer: Endocrine glands secrete hormones like pituitary, thyroid, adrenal controlling growth, metabolism and stress.

questions.text: Hormonal coordination is slower than nervous coordination.
questions.answer: Because hormones travel through blood and take more time to reach target organs.

chapters.title: Human Health and Diseases
chapters.description: Study of infectious and non-infectious diseases, immunity, vaccines, immune response, AIDS, cancer, addiction, and strategies for disease prevention.
learningObjectives: Differentiate between infectious and non-infectious diseases.
Understand the structure and functioning of the immune system.
Explain types of immunity and principles of vaccination.
Recognize major diseases such as AIDS, cancer, and their causes.
Understand causes and consequences of drug and alcohol abuse.

questions.text: The pathogen that causes tuberculosis is:
questions.answer: Mycobacterium tuberculosis

questions.text: Define immunity.
questions.answer: Immunity is the ability of the body to resist and fight infections through defense mechanisms.

questions.text: What is the difference between innate and acquired immunity?
questions.answer: Innate immunity is present from birth and provides immediate defense, while acquired immunity develops after exposure to pathogens and is highly specific.

questions.text: Name any two sexually transmitted diseases (STDs).
questions.answer: AIDS and syphilis are two sexually transmitted diseases.

questions.text: Which cells produce antibodies?
questions.answer: B-lymphocytes

questions.text: Explain the term vaccination.
questions.answer: Vaccination is the process of administering weakened or inactive pathogens to stimulate immunity without causing disease.

questions.text: What is AIDS? How is it transmitted?
questions.answer: AIDS is Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome caused by HIV. It is transmitted through unprotected sex, contaminated needles, infected blood, and mother-to-child transmission.

questions.text: Describe the structure of the human immune system.
questions.answer: The immune system consists of lymphoid organs such as thymus, spleen, lymph nodes, bone marrow, and circulating immune cells like T-cells, B-cells, macrophages, and antigen-presenting cells. These organs and cells coordinate to detect, attack, and eliminate pathogens.

questions.text: Explain the causes and symptoms of cancer.
questions.answer: Cancer is caused by uncontrolled cell division due to mutations, carcinogens, radiation, viruses, or genetic factors. Symptoms include formation of tumors, weight loss, fatigue, abnormal bleeding, and organ dysfunction.

questions.text: Discuss the effects of drug and alcohol addiction on human health.
questions.answer: Drug and alcohol addiction affect the nervous system, cause liver damage, impair judgment, weaken immunity, lead to mental disorders, social problems, accidents, and long-term physiological damage.

questions.text: Immunity acquired after an infection is _____ immunity.
questions.answer: Natural acquired

questions.text: Passive immunity is _____
options: acquired through natural overt or latent infection
questions.answer: acquired through readymade antibodies

questions.text: Pathogens are _____
questions.answer: disease causing organisms

questions.text: Which of the following disease is communicable?
questions.answer: Malaria

questions.text: Most accurate definition of health is
options: complete physical, mental and social well-being
questions.answer: complete physical, mental and social well-being

questions.text: AIDS is caused by
questions.answer: virus

questions.text: Food prepared in unhygienic place spreads
questions.answer: Typhoid

questions.text: Carcinoma is cancer of _____ cells
questions.answer: epithelial

questions.text: Inactive gene that can cause cancer is
questions.answer: Proto-oncogene

questions.text: Antiviral proteins released by infected cells are
questions.answer: interferons

questions.text: Define health as per WHO.
questions.answer: Health is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being.

questions.text: What are non-communicable diseases?
questions.answer: Diseases which do not spread from one person to another.

questions.text: Name causative pathogen of Ascariasis.
questions.answer: Ascaris lumbricoides

questions.text: What is serology?
questions.answer: Study of antigen–antibody interactions.

questions.text: Name vector of malarial pathogen.
questions.answer: Female Anopheles mosquito

questions.text: What are congenital diseases?
questions.answer: Diseases present from birth due to genetic or metabolic defects.

questions.text: Name vector responsible for filariasis.
questions.answer: Female Culex mosquito

questions.text: Symptoms shown by drug addict when drug is withdrawn are called
questions.answer: Withdrawal syndrome

questions.text: What is leukemia?
questions.answer: Cancer of blood with excessive formation of WBCs.

questions.text: Define adolescence.
questions.answer: Period between onset of secondary sexual characters and end of body growth.

questions.text: Enlist four types of T-lymphocytes.
questions.answer: Helper T-cells, Killer T-cells, Suppressor T-cells, Memory T-cells.

questions.text: State significance of mother's milk to newborn.
questions.answer: Provides naturally acquired passive immunity via colostrum.

questions.text: Enlist any two features of acquired immunity.
questions.answer: Specificity and memory.

questions.text: Give any two symptoms of Ascariasis.
questions.answer: Vomiting, abdominal discomfort, presence of worms in feces.

questions.text: Enlist any two cancer therapies.
questions.answer: Chemotherapy and radiotherapy.

questions.text: Explain epithelial surface as innate immunity.
questions.answer: Skin, mucus, sweat, saliva, gastric acid and urine prevent entry of pathogens.

questions.text: Explain causes of substance abuse during adolescence.
questions.answer: Peer pressure, family conflicts, lack of supervision and risk-taking behavior.

questions.text: Explain stages of adolescence.
questions.answer: Early, middle and late adolescence marked by physical, mental and emotional changes.

questions.text: Explain modes of transmission of HIV.
questions.answer: Unsafe sex, blood transfusion, mother to child and needle sharing.

questions.text: How is tumor formed in body?
questions.answer: By uncontrolled and purposeless division of cells.

questions.text: Explain types of acquired immunity.
questions.answer: Acquired immunity is of two types: active (natural and artificial) and passive (natural and artificial).

questions.text: Explain clinical manifestations of AIDS.
questions.answer: Initial infection, asymptomatic stage, ARC and final AIDS stage with opportunistic infections.

questions.text: Explain any four therapies used in cancer treatment.
questions.answer: Chemotherapy, radiotherapy, surgery and immunotherapy.

questions.text: The causative agent of AIDS is:
questions.answer: HIV

questions.text: Which of the following is a bacterial disease?
questions.answer: Typhoid

questions.text: Define immunity.
questions.answer: Immunity is the ability of the body to resist and fight against pathogens and diseases.

questions.text: What are vaccines?
questions.answer: Vaccines are biological preparations that provide active acquired immunity against specific diseases.

questions.text: Explain acquired immunity.
questions.answer: Acquired immunity develops after exposure to antigens and can be active or passive.

questions.text: Explain the mode of transmission and symptoms of malaria.
questions.answer: Malaria is transmitted by bite of infected female Anopheles mosquito; symptoms include fever, chills and headache.

questions.text: Explain the mode of transmission and prevention of AIDS.
questions.answer: AIDS spreads through unprotected sex, blood transfusion and infected needles; prevention includes safe sex and screened blood.

questions.text: Describe the structure and functions of antibodies.
questions.answer: Antibodies are Y-shaped proteins with antigen binding sites; they neutralize toxins and pathogens.

questions.text: Explain innate immunity in humans.
questions.answer: Innate immunity includes physical, physiological, cellular and cytokine barriers that provide non-specific defense.

questions.text: Vaccination is an effective method of disease prevention.
questions.answer: Because vaccines stimulate immune memory and protect against future infections.

chapters.title: Enhancement of Food Production
chapters.description: Study of crop improvement, plant breeding, animal husbandry, dairy and poultry management, fisheries, biofortification, tissue culture, and modern agricultural technologies.
learningObjectives: Understand methods of improving crop yield and quality.
Explain plant breeding techniques like hybridization and mutation breeding.
Recognize the importance of animal husbandry and fisheries.
Understand biofortification and its role in nutrition.
Explain tissue culture and modern biotechnological tools in food production.

questions.text: Single-cell protein (SCP) is obtained from:
questions.answer: Bacteria and fungi

questions.text: Define plant breeding.
questions.answer: Plant breeding is the purposeful manipulation of plant species to create desired varieties with improved yield, quality, and resistance.

questions.text: What is biofortification?
questions.answer: Biofortification is the process of increasing the nutritional value of crops through breeding, genetic engineering, or agronomic practices.

questions.text: Name two applications of tissue culture in agriculture.
questions.answer: Micropropagation for mass production of disease-free plants and production of somaclones with desirable traits.

questions.text: Which of the following is a high-yielding variety (HYV) crop?
questions.answer: IR-8 rice

questions.text: What is animal husbandry?
questions.answer: Animal husbandry is the science of breeding, feeding, and caring for domestic animals to obtain useful products like milk, eggs, meat, and wool.

questions.text: Explain the importance of fishery development.
questions.answer: Fishery provides protein-rich food, employment, foreign exchange, and supports rural economies through aquaculture and marine fishing.

questions.text: Describe the steps involved in hybridization in plants.
questions.answer: Steps include selection of parents, emasculation, bagging, pollination, tagging, and collection of hybrid seeds. The resulting hybrids show improved traits such as yield, disease resistance, and stress tolerance.

questions.text: Explain mutation breeding and give an example.
questions.answer: Mutation breeding involves exposing seeds or tissues to chemicals or radiation to induce mutations, followed by selection of desirable mutants. Example: Sharbati Sonora wheat variety developed through gamma radiation.

questions.text: Discuss the role of biotechnology in enhancing food production.
questions.answer: Biotechnology helps increase yield and nutritional value through genetic modification, tissue culture, microbial fermentation (SCP), pest-resistant GM crops, improved varieties through marker-assisted selection, and biofertilizers improving soil fertility.

questions.text: Wheat Atlas 66 has high contents of _____.
questions.answer: Protein

questions.text: Species of _____ is involved in cheese formation.
questions.answer: Penicillium

questions.text: Aspergillus niger is used to prepare vitamin _____.
questions.answer: C

questions.text: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is used to produce enzyme _____.
questions.answer: Invertase

questions.text: Select the odd one from given herbicides.
questions.answer: Cactoblastis

questions.text: _____ associated with plants like Azolla and Cycas can be used as biofertilizers.
questions.answer: Anabaena

questions.text: Antibiotic Chloromycetin is obtained from _____.
questions.answer: Streptomyces venezuelae

questions.text: Indian curd is prepared by inoculating milk with _____.
questions.answer: Lactobacillus acidophilus

questions.text: What is biofortification?
questions.answer: Breeding crops to increase nutritional value like proteins, vitamins and minerals.

questions.text: Name biofortified wheat variety for high protein content.
questions.answer: Atlas 66

questions.text: What is the main function of a fermenter?
questions.answer: To provide controlled conditions for microbial growth to obtain desired product.

questions.text: What is mycorrhiza?
questions.answer: Symbiotic association between fungi and roots of higher plants.

questions.text: What are flocs in sewage treatment?
questions.answer: Masses of bacteria held together by slime and fungal hyphae.

questions.text: Name two amino acids found in fortified maize variety.
questions.answer: Lysine and tryptophan

questions.text: Name two acids produced using Aspergillus niger.
questions.answer: Citric acid and gluconic acid

questions.text: Give names of two organisations providing models of biogas plants.
questions.answer: KVIC and IARI

questions.text: Why mushrooms are advised in diet?
questions.answer: They are rich in proteins, vitamins, minerals and low in calories.

questions.text: Name two bacteria responsible for fermenting idli and dosa batter.
questions.answer: Leuconostoc and Streptococcus

questions.text: Name two benefits of biofertilizers.
questions.answer: Increase soil fertility and reduce pollution hazards.

questions.text: Name two benefits of mycorrhiza.
questions.answer: Enhances water uptake and mineral absorption.

questions.text: Name two uses of biogas.
questions.answer: Cooking and lighting.

questions.text: State any three benefits of biogas.
questions.answer: It is eco-friendly, cheap, renewable and improves sanitation.

questions.text: State any three benefits of mycorrhiza.
questions.answer: Improves mineral absorption, water uptake and protects against pathogens.

questions.text: Write chemical reactions representing methanogenesis.
questions.answer: CO2 + 4H2 → CH4 + 2H2O; CH3COOH → CH4 + CO2.

questions.text: Describe structure of a biogas plant.
questions.answer: Consists of digester, gas holder, inlet and outlet chambers.

questions.text: Explain sewage water treatment.
questions.answer: Includes preliminary, primary, secondary and tertiary treatments.

questions.text: Explain process of sewage water treatment before discharge.
questions.answer: Includes screening, sedimentation, aeration, activated sludge formation and digestion.

questions.text: Explain methanogenesis in biogas production.
questions.answer: Anaerobic bacteria convert organic acids and CO2 into methane.

questions.text: Explain role of biofertilizers in agriculture.
questions.answer: They increase soil fertility, supply nutrients and reduce chemical fertilizer use.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of biofertilizer?
questions.answer: Rhizobium

questions.text: The technique of producing disease-resistant varieties of crops is known as:
questions.answer: Plant breeding

questions.text: Define plant breeding.
questions.answer: Plant breeding is the science of improving crop plants by selecting and crossing plants with desirable traits.

questions.text: What is animal husbandry?
questions.answer: Animal husbandry is the branch of agriculture concerned with breeding, feeding and management of domestic animals.

questions.text: Explain hybridization in plant breeding.
questions.answer: Hybridization involves crossing two genetically different plants to obtain hybrids with desirable traits.

questions.text: Explain advantages of tissue culture technique.
questions.answer: Tissue culture enables rapid multiplication, disease-free plants and conservation of rare species.

questions.text: Explain single cell protein (SCP).
questions.answer: Single cell protein refers to microbial biomass used as protein source for humans and animals.

questions.text: Describe the steps involved in plant breeding programme.
questions.answer: Collection of variability, evaluation, selection, hybridization, testing and release of varieties.

questions.text: Explain role of biofertilizers and biopesticides in agriculture.
questions.answer: They enhance soil fertility and control pests without environmental pollution.

questions.text: Use of biofertilizers is encouraged in sustainable agriculture.
questions.answer: Because they are eco-friendly, cost-effective and improve soil health.

chapters.title: Biotechnology
chapters.description: Study of principles, tools, and applications of biotechnology including recombinant DNA technology, plasmids, restriction enzymes, PCR, transgenic organisms, and ethical issues.
learningObjectives: Understand the principles and steps of recombinant DNA technology.
Explain the role of restriction enzymes and vectors.
Describe PCR, cloning, and electrophoresis techniques.
Explore applications of biotechnology in various fields.
Understand ethical concerns and biosafety measures.

questions.text: The enzyme used to cut DNA at specific sites is called:
questions.answer: Restriction endonuclease

questions.text: Define biotechnology.
questions.answer: Biotechnology is the use of living organisms, cells, or biological systems to develop products or processes for human welfare.

questions.text: What is a cloning vector? Give an example.
questions.answer: A cloning vector is a DNA molecule that carries foreign DNA into a host cell for replication. Example: Plasmid pBR322.

questions.text: Explain the function of DNA ligase.
questions.answer: DNA ligase joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds, sealing nicks in the sugar-phosphate backbone.

questions.text: Which technique is used to amplify DNA fragments?
questions.answer: PCR

questions.text: What is recombinant DNA?
questions.answer: Recombinant DNA is artificially created DNA formed by combining DNA from two different organisms or sources.

questions.text: Name two applications of biotechnology in medicine.
questions.answer: Production of insulin using recombinant DNA technology and development of vaccines.

questions.text: Explain the steps involved in recombinant DNA technology.
questions.answer: Steps include: 1. Isolation of DNA. 2. Cutting DNA with restriction enzymes. 3. Insertion into a cloning vector. 4. Introduction of recombinant DNA into host cells. 5. Selection of transformed cells. 6. Expression of the inserted gene to obtain the desired product.

questions.text: Describe the process and significance of gel electrophoresis.
questions.answer: Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments based on size. DNA samples are loaded into agarose gel and subjected to electric current. Smaller fragments move faster towards the positive electrode. It is used in DNA fingerprinting, PCR analysis, and gene cloning.

questions.text: Discuss ethical issues related to genetic engineering and GM crops.
questions.answer: Concerns include ecological risks, gene transfer to wild species, loss of biodiversity, food safety issues, labeling requirements, and ethical debate over manipulating life forms. Biosafety regulations are necessary to prevent misuse.

questions.text: The technique which involves addition or deletion of genes is
questions.answer: genetic engineering

questions.text: EcoRI is obtained from
questions.answer: Escherichia coli Ry13

questions.text: The enzyme restriction endonuclease
questions.answer: cuts double stranded DNA

questions.text: Ti plasmid being used for introducing genes in plants is obtained from

questions.text: Polymerase chain reaction is most useful in
questions.answer: DNA amplification

questions.text: In Bt cotton transgenic plant, Bt refers to
questions.answer: Bacillus thuringiensis

questions.text: In transgenic crop substance provitamin A is obtained in

questions.text: In biotechnology GMO refers to
questions.answer: genetically modified organisms

questions.text: First biopatent to genetically engineered bacterium was given to
questions.answer: Pseudomonas

questions.text: In which transgenic plant the substance flavonoids obtained as antioxidants?
questions.answer: Transgenic tomato plant

questions.text: What is germline therapy?
questions.answer: Introduction of healthy genes into germ cells like sperms, eggs or embryos.

questions.text: Which recombinant protein is obtained for Hepatitis-B by r-DNA technology?
questions.answer: Hepatitis B surface antigen

questions.text: What is plasmid?
questions.answer: Circular, double stranded, self-replicating extrachromosomal DNA molecule.

questions.text: What is palindromic sequence?
questions.answer: DNA sequence that reads same in forward and reverse direction.

questions.text: Alu-I is obtained from which organism?
questions.answer: Arthrobacter luteus

questions.text: What is the role of Taq polymerase in PCR?
questions.answer: Polymerizes DNA molecules during PCR.

questions.text: What is biopiracy? Explain with respect to turmeric.
questions.answer: Biopiracy is patenting biological resources without compensation. Turmeric patents were revoked as Indians traditionally used it.

questions.text: How biotechnology is applicable with respect to genomics?
questions.answer: Includes whole genome sequencing, gene identification, bioinformatics and reverse genetics.

questions.text: Explain how transgenic fish is commercially beneficial.
questions.answer: They show faster growth, increased tolerance and improved food quality.

questions.text: Write any two human disorders and recombinant proteins used to cure them.
questions.answer: Diabetes – Insulin; Anaemia – Erythropoietin.

questions.text: Write a note on somatic cell gene therapy.
questions.answer: Healthy genes are introduced into somatic cells to treat acquired disorders.

questions.text: Define vector. Write any two examples.
questions.answer: Vector carries foreign DNA; examples: plasmids and bacteriophages.

questions.text: Explain traditional use of biotechnology.
questions.answer: Based on fermentation using microbes to produce curd, wine, cheese and bread.

questions.text: Define biotechnology and state its basic principles.
questions.answer: Use of biological systems for products based on genetic engineering and sterile conditions.

questions.text: What is gene cloning? Explain tools used for it.
questions.answer: Isolation and amplification of DNA using enzymes, vectors and host cells.

questions.text: Explain types of enzymes used in biotechnology.
questions.answer: Restriction enzymes, ligases, polymerases and alkaline phosphatase.

questions.text: What is recognition sequence?
questions.answer: Specific palindromic DNA sequence recognized by restriction enzymes.

questions.text: Define biotechnology. How is it used in production of human insulin?
questions.answer: Biotechnology uses rDNA to insert insulin gene into bacteria for large-scale production.

questions.text: What is PCR? Explain different steps involved in it.
questions.answer: PCR amplifies DNA using denaturation, annealing and extension with Taq polymerase.

questions.text: Explain terms passenger DNA, chimeric DNA, transformed cell and restriction site.
questions.answer: Passenger DNA is desired gene; chimeric DNA is recombinant DNA; transformed cell uptakes rDNA; restriction site is enzyme cutting site.

questions.text: Define biotechnology. Give any three applications of it.
questions.answer: Applications include plant, medical, microbial and environmental biotechnology.

questions.text: Which are the different adverse effects of biotechnology on human health and environment?
questions.answer: Allergies, unknown health effects, resistant pests, resistant weeds and ecological imbalance.

questions.text: Explain biopatent and biopiracy with examples.
questions.answer: Biopatent protects innovations; biopiracy exploits traditional knowledge like turmeric and neem.

questions.text: Which enzyme is used to cut DNA at specific sites?
questions.answer: Restriction endonuclease

questions.text: The vector commonly used in genetic engineering is:
questions.answer: Plasmid

questions.text: Define biotechnology.
questions.answer: Biotechnology is the application of biological systems, organisms or derivatives to develop useful products and processes.

questions.text: What is recombinant DNA?
questions.answer: Recombinant DNA is DNA formed by combining DNA segments from two different sources.

questions.text: Explain the role of plasmids in genetic engineering.
questions.answer: Plasmids act as vectors to transfer foreign DNA into host cells for replication and expression.

questions.text: Explain polymerase chain reaction (PCR).
questions.answer: PCR is a technique used to amplify specific DNA sequences using primers, DNA polymerase and thermal cycling.

questions.text: State applications of biotechnology in medicine.
questions.answer: Production of insulin, vaccines, antibiotics, gene therapy and diagnostic techniques.

questions.text: Describe the steps involved in recombinant DNA technology.
questions.answer: Isolation of DNA, restriction digestion, ligation, transformation, selection and expression of recombinant DNA.

questions.text: Explain applications of biotechnology in agriculture.
questions.answer: Development of GM crops, pest resistance, improved yield and nutritional quality.

questions.text: Biotechnology is considered a multidisciplinary science.
questions.answer: Because it integrates biology with chemistry, physics, engineering and computer science.

chapters.title: Organisms and Populations
chapters.description: Study of ecological levels, abiotic factors, adaptations, population attributes, population interactions, and growth models.
topics: Population Interactions (Competition, Predation, Parasitism, Commensalism, Mutualism)
learningObjectives: Understand how organisms interact with their environment.
Explain adaptations to various abiotic factors.
Analyze population attributes such as size, density, and age structure.
Differentiate population interactions and their ecological significance.
Interpret population growth curves and survivorship patterns.

questions.text: The study of interaction between organisms and their environment is called:
questions.answer: Ecology

questions.text: Define habitat.
questions.answer: Habitat is the natural living place of an organism where it obtains food, shelter, and reproduces.

questions.text: What is acclimatization? Give an example.
questions.answer: Acclimatization is the reversible adjustment of an organism to a change in its environment. Example: Humans adjusting to high altitudes.

questions.text: Differentiate between natality and mortality.
questions.answer: Natality is the birth rate of a population, whereas mortality is the death rate.

questions.text: The logistic growth curve is:
questions.answer: S-shaped

questions.text: Explain mutualism with an example.
questions.answer: Mutualism is an interaction where both species benefit. Example: Lichens consist of algae and fungi living together.

questions.text: What are age pyramids? Name their types.
questions.answer: Age pyramids show the age distribution of a population. Types: Expanding, stable, and declining.

questions.text: Describe the exponential growth model.
questions.answer: In exponential growth, resources are unlimited and population grows at its maximum rate, forming a J-shaped curve. The growth rate is proportional to the existing population, represented by the equation dN/dt = rN.

questions.text: Explain predation and its ecological importance.
questions.answer: Predation is the interaction where one organism (predator) kills and consumes another (prey). It maintains population balance, drives evolution through natural selection, and regulates energy flow in ecosystems.

questions.text: Discuss adaptations of organisms to extreme environments.
questions.answer: Adaptations include morphological (thick fur in polar animals), physiological (heat tolerance in desert plants), and behavioral (burrowing in rodents). These enable survival under extreme temperature, salinity, pressure, or light conditions.

questions.text: An association of individuals of different species living in the same habitat and having functional interactions is called
questions.answer: biotic community

questions.text: Community is defined as
questions.answer: interacting populations

questions.text: Regional and local variations within each biome lead to the formation of variety of
questions.answer: habitats

questions.text: Maximum absorption of rainfall water is done by
questions.answer: tropical evergreen forest

questions.text: The cattle egret and grazing cattle in close association is a classic example of
questions.answer: commensalism

questions.text: The ecological niche of population is a
options: set of conditions and resources that it uses
questions.answer: set of conditions and resources that it uses

questions.text: Tropical dense forests are due to
questions.answer: high rainfall and warm temperature

questions.text: Polar bears show hibernation during
questions.answer: winter

questions.text: In logistic growth curve lag phase shows
questions.answer: initial stage of growth

questions.text: The number of deaths under ideal conditions is known as
questions.answer: absolute mortality

questions.text: Define absolute mortality.
questions.answer: Number of deaths under ideal conditions with no environmental resistance.

questions.text: What is population ecology?
questions.answer: Branch of ecology dealing with population dynamics, genetics and evolution.

questions.text: Define habitat niche.
questions.answer: Physical space occupied by organisms.

questions.text: What is ESS?
questions.answer: Evolutionary Stable Strategy where males and females are in 1:1 ratio.

questions.text: Define habitat.
questions.answer: Area where a species lives and interacts with other factors.

questions.text: What Allen's rule indicates?
questions.answer: Animals in cold climates have shorter extremities to reduce heat loss.

questions.text: Differentiate between habitat and niche.
questions.answer: Habitat is physical place of living, niche is functional role and position in ecosystem.

questions.text: Define adaptation with two examples.
questions.answer: Adaptation is an attribute enabling survival; e.g. thick cuticle in desert plants, streamlined body in fishes.

questions.text: What is mortality?
questions.answer: Death rate of a population.

questions.text: Define population interactions.
questions.answer: Interactions among organisms of same or different species living together.

questions.text: Define niche with its types.
questions.answer: Niche is functional role of species. Types: spatial niche, trophic niche, multidimensional niche.

questions.text: Explain mutualism with example.
questions.answer: Both species benefit; e.g. lichen association of algae and fungus.

questions.text: Explain characteristics of population.
questions.answer: Population density, natality, mortality and age structure.

questions.text: Explain population interactions with examples.
questions.answer: Includes mutualism, competition, parasitism, predation, commensalism.

questions.text: Define population growth. Explain different types of age pyramids.
questions.answer: Population growth is increase in number of individuals. Age pyramids: expanding, stable and declining.

questions.text: Explain biotic and abiotic factors involved in ecology.
questions.answer: Biotic include producers, consumers, decomposers; abiotic include temperature, water, light and soil.

questions.text: Explain different types of population growth models.
questions.answer: Exponential growth occurs under unlimited resources; logistic growth occurs under limited resources.

questions.text: The relationship where one organism benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited is called:
questions.answer: Commensalism

questions.text: Exponential population growth is represented by:
questions.answer: J-shaped curve

questions.text: Define population density.
questions.answer: Population density is the number of individuals of a species per unit area or volume at a given time.

questions.text: What is mutualism?
questions.answer: Mutualism is an interaction where both participating species benefit from each other.

questions.text: Explain logistic population growth.
questions.answer: Logistic growth shows initial exponential growth followed by stabilization at carrying capacity, forming an S-shaped curve.

questions.text: Explain predator-prey relationship with an example.
questions.answer: In predator-prey interaction, predator feeds on prey, regulating population size; e.g., lion and deer.

questions.text: Explain adaptations in desert plants.
questions.answer: Desert plants show thick cuticle, reduced leaves, deep roots and CAM pathway to reduce water loss.

questions.text: Describe population interactions in an ecosystem.
questions.answer: Interactions include mutualism, commensalism, parasitism, predation and competition.

questions.text: Explain population growth curves with suitable diagrams.
questions.answer: Exponential growth shows J-curve; logistic growth shows S-curve due to carrying capacity.

questions.text: Carrying capacity regulates population size.
questions.answer: Because it represents maximum population an environment can sustain with available resources.

chapters.title: Ecosystems and Energy Flow
chapters.description: Study of ecosystem structure, biotic and abiotic components, food chains and food webs, ecological pyramids, productivity, energy flow, and nutrient cycles.
learningObjectives: Understand the structure and components of ecosystems.
Differentiate between food chains and food webs.
Interpret ecological pyramids and energy flow models.
Explain primary and secondary productivity.
Understand the importance of nutrient cycles.

questions.text: The primary source of energy in an ecosystem is:
questions.answer: Sunlight

questions.text: Define ecosystem.
questions.answer: An ecosystem is a functional unit consisting of living organisms interacting with each other and with the physical environment.

questions.text: What is a food web?
questions.answer: A food web is a network of interconnected food chains that shows multiple feeding relationships in an ecosystem.

questions.text: Explain Gross Primary Productivity (GPP).
questions.answer: GPP is the total amount of energy captured by producers through photosynthesis in a given time.

questions.text: Ecological pyramids represent:
questions.answer: Number, biomass, or energy

questions.text: What is decomposition?
questions.answer: Decomposition is the breakdown of organic matter by microorganisms, releasing nutrients back into the environment.

questions.text: State the 10% law of energy transfer.
questions.answer: According to the 10% law, only about 10% of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next; the rest is lost as heat.

questions.text: Describe the nitrogen cycle in an ecosystem.
questions.answer: The nitrogen cycle includes nitrogen fixation (conversion of N₂ to ammonia), nitrification (ammonia to nitrates), assimilation by plants, ammonification (decomposition releasing ammonia), and denitrification (conversion of nitrates back to N₂). This cycle maintains soil fertility.

questions.text: Explain the flow of energy in an ecosystem.
questions.answer: Energy flows unidirectionally from the sun to producers and then to consumers and decomposers. At each trophic level, most energy is lost as heat, making the energy pyramid always upright.

questions.text: Discuss differences between food chains and food webs.
questions.answer: A food chain shows a single linear pathway of energy flow. A food web consists of multiple interconnected chains, offering greater stability to the ecosystem by providing alternative feeding routes.

questions.text: Lichens taking roots on bare rocks are an example of
questions.answer: pioneer species

questions.text: Growth of new grasses and shrubs on a patch of forest burnt down by forest fire is an example of
questions.answer: secondary succession

questions.text: All types of ecological succession whether on land or in water always reaches
questions.answer: climax community

questions.text: Succession occurring in wet areas is called
questions.answer: hydrarch

questions.text: Succession occurring in dry areas is known as
questions.answer: xerarch

questions.text: Which of the following is a pioneer species on rocks?
questions.answer: crustose lichens

questions.text: The stable, final stage of succession is called
questions.answer: climax community

questions.text: Succession that starts on bare rocks is known as
questions.answer: primary succession

questions.text: Succession that begins where soil is already present is
questions.answer: secondary succession

questions.text: The entire sequence of communities in succession is called
questions.answer: sere

questions.text: What is sere?
questions.answer: The entire sequence of communities that change successively in a given area.

questions.text: Define ecological succession.
questions.answer: Gradual and predictable changes in species composition of a given area.

questions.text: What is climax community?
questions.answer: Final stable stage of succession that remains unchanged for a long period.

questions.text: Name the pioneer species in aquatic habitat.
questions.answer: Phytoplanktons

questions.text: Which succession is faster: primary or secondary?
questions.answer: Secondary succession

questions.text: Name one pioneer species on rocks.
questions.answer: Crustose lichens

questions.text: What is nudation?
questions.answer: Formation of a bare area due to destruction of existing vegetation.

questions.text: Name the types of succession based on nature of habitat.
questions.answer: Hydrarch succession and Xerarch succession.

questions.text: Why is primary succession slower than secondary succession?
questions.answer: Because soil formation is required in primary succession which takes a very long time.

questions.text: What are pioneer species?
questions.answer: Species that first invade a bare area and initiate succession.

questions.text: Give two examples of pioneer species.
questions.answer: Crustose lichens and phytoplanktons.

questions.text: Define primary succession.
questions.answer: Succession that starts on bare area where no life existed earlier.

questions.text: Explain primary succession.
questions.answer: It begins on bare rocks or new land, involves pioneer species, soil formation and ends in climax community.

questions.text: Explain secondary succession.
questions.answer: Occurs in areas where soil is already present after disturbance like fire or flood.

questions.text: Explain the following sequence of succession after a forest fire.
questions.answer: Grasses → shrubs → woodland → forest stage.

questions.text: What is hydrarch succession?
questions.answer: Succession that starts in aquatic habitat and progresses towards mesic conditions.

questions.text: What is xerarch succession?
questions.answer: Succession that begins in dry habitat and progresses towards mesic conditions.

questions.text: Explain the progress of ecological succession in a newly formed volcanic island.
questions.answer: Primary succession starts with lichens, followed by mosses, herbs, shrubs and finally climax forest.

questions.text: Describe stages of secondary succession after forest fire.
questions.answer: Grasses grow first, followed by shrubs, woodland stage and finally climax forest community.

questions.text: Differentiate between primary and secondary succession.
questions.answer: Primary succession starts on bare area and is slow; secondary succession starts where soil exists and is faster.

questions.text: The primary producers in an ecosystem are:
questions.answer: Green plants

questions.text: The ten percent law of energy transfer was proposed by:
questions.answer: Lindeman

questions.text: Define ecosystem.
questions.answer: An ecosystem is a functional unit where living organisms interact with each other and with their physical environment.

questions.text: What are decomposers?
questions.answer: Decomposers are organisms like bacteria and fungi that break down dead organic matter into simpler substances.

questions.text: Explain food chain with an example.
questions.answer: A food chain shows transfer of energy from producers to consumers, e.g., grass → deer → lion.

questions.text: Explain food web.
questions.answer: A food web is a network of interconnected food chains showing complex feeding relationships.

questions.text: Explain ecological pyramids.
questions.answer: Ecological pyramids represent number, biomass or energy at each trophic level.

questions.text: Describe energy flow in an ecosystem.
questions.answer: Energy flows unidirectionally from sun to producers and then to consumers with loss at each trophic level.

questions.text: Explain nutrient cycling in an ecosystem.
questions.answer: Nutrients circulate through biotic and abiotic components via biogeochemical cycles like carbon and nitrogen cycles.

questions.text: Energy pyramid is always upright.
questions.answer: Because energy decreases at successive trophic levels due to loss as heat.

chapters.title: Biodiversity, Conservation and Environmental Issues
chapters.description: Study of biodiversity levels, importance of biodiversity, threats to biodiversity, conservation strategies, pollution, global warming, ozone depletion, and sustainable development.
learningObjectives: Understand biodiversity at genetic, species, and ecosystem levels.
Recognize the importance and value of biodiversity.
Identify major threats such as habitat loss, poaching, pollution, and climate change.
Differentiate between in-situ and ex-situ conservation.
Understand environmental issues and the need for sustainable development.

questions.text: Biosphere reserves, national parks, and wildlife sanctuaries are examples of:
questions.answer: In-situ conservation

questions.text: Define biodiversity.
questions.answer: Biodiversity refers to the variety of life forms at genetic, species, and ecosystem levels.

questions.text: State two major threats to biodiversity.
questions.answer: Habitat loss and fragmentation, and poaching of wildlife are major threats to biodiversity.

questions.text: What is global warming? Mention one cause.
questions.answer: Global warming is the rise in Earth's average temperature due to increased greenhouse gases such as CO₂.

questions.text: Ozone depletion is mainly caused by:
questions.answer: CFCs

questions.text: Explain ex-situ conservation with an example.
questions.answer: Ex-situ conservation involves protecting species outside their natural habitats. Example: Botanical gardens and seed banks.

questions.text: What is eutrophication?
questions.answer: Eutrophication is nutrient enrichment of water bodies causing excessive algal growth, depletion of oxygen, and damage to aquatic life.

questions.text: Describe the major types of biodiversity.
questions.answer: Types include: 1. **Genetic diversity** – variation in genes within a species. 2. **Species diversity** – variety of species within a region. 3. **Ecosystem diversity** – diversity of ecosystems such as forests, deserts, wetlands. These levels reflect complexity and stability of life on Earth.

questions.text: Explain how climate change affects biodiversity.
questions.answer: Climate change alters temperature and rainfall patterns, causing habitat shifts, species migration, coral bleaching, extinction of sensitive species, and disruption of ecological interactions like pollination and migration.

questions.text: Discuss sustainable development and its importance.
questions.answer: Sustainable development meets present needs without compromising future generations by balancing economic growth, environmental protection, and social well-being. It promotes conservation of resources, renewable energy use, and pollution control.

questions.text: Dodo bird, stellar sea cow and passenger pigeon are few examples of extinction due to _____.
questions.answer: over exploitation

questions.text: Select the odd example with respect to types of conservation strategies.
questions.answer: Crocodile bank of Chennai

questions.text: India boasts a handsome share of _____ % of total biodiversity wealth of the earth.
Which of the following is an example of in-situ conservation?
questions.answer: Sacred groves

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a cause of biodiversity loss?
questions.answer: Afforestation

questions.text: Introduction of Nile perch in Lake Victoria caused extinction of
questions.answer: cichlid fish

questions.text: The convention on biological diversity was held at
questions.answer: Rio de Janeiro

questions.text: Hot spots of biodiversity are regions with
questions.answer: high endemism and threat

questions.text: What is Hello Forest?
questions.answer: A 24-hour toll free helpline number (1926) for plantation, protection and mass awareness.

questions.text: Name the Japanese method of plantation adopted by our government.
questions.answer: Miyawaki method

questions.text: Variations in reserpine concentration in Rauwolfia vomitoria indicate which level of biodiversity?
questions.answer: Genetic diversity

questions.text: What does IUCN stand for?
questions.answer: International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources

questions.text: What is NBA?
questions.answer: National Biodiversity Authority

questions.text: What is alien species invasion?
questions.answer: Introduction of non-native species that harm local species and ecosystems.

questions.text: Name one invasive plant species in India.
questions.answer: Parthenium

questions.text: Write full forms of IUCN and NBA.
questions.answer: IUCN – International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources; NBA – National Biodiversity Authority.

questions.text: State any two causes of biodiversity loss.
questions.answer: Habitat loss and over exploitation.

questions.text: What is in-situ conservation?
questions.answer: Conservation of species in their natural habitat.

questions.text: What is ex-situ conservation?
questions.answer: Conservation of species outside their natural habitat.

questions.text: Name any two biodiversity hotspots in India.
questions.answer: Western Ghats and Eastern Himalayas.

questions.text: Explain alien species invasion with one example.
questions.answer: Alien species introduced intentionally or accidentally can harm native species; e.g. Nile perch in Lake Victoria.

questions.text: Explain causes of biodiversity losses.
questions.answer: Habitat loss, over exploitation, alien species invasion and co-extinction.

questions.text: Explain genetic diversity with example.
questions.answer: Variations within species; e.g. reserpine content in Rauwolfia.

questions.text: Explain IUCN categories.
questions.answer: Includes Extinct, Endangered, Vulnerable, Near Threatened and Least Concern.

questions.text: Describe reasons for conservation of biodiversity.
questions.answer: Reasons include narrowly utilitarian, broadly utilitarian and ethical reasons.

questions.text: Describe measures to achieve Mission Harit Maharashtra.
questions.answer: Includes Hello Forest helpline, My Plants app, mass plantation drives and Miyawaki method.

questions.text: Explain in-situ and ex-situ conservation with examples.
questions.answer: In-situ: national parks and sanctuaries; Ex-situ: zoos, botanical gardens and seed banks.

questions.text: The variety of life forms found in a particular habitat is called:
questions.answer: Biodiversity

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of ex-situ conservation?
questions.answer: Botanical garden

questions.text: Define biodiversity hotspot.
questions.answer: A biodiversity hotspot is a region with high species richness and a high degree of endemism that is under threat.

questions.text: What is in-situ conservation?
questions.answer: In-situ conservation is the protection of species in their natural habitats.

questions.text: Explain causes of loss of biodiversity.
questions.answer: Habitat loss, overexploitation, invasive species, pollution and climate change cause loss of biodiversity.

questions.text: Explain the importance of biodiversity.
questions.answer: Biodiversity provides ecological stability, resources for food and medicine, and supports ecosystem services.

questions.text: Explain greenhouse effect.
questions.answer: Greenhouse effect is warming of Earth due to trapping of heat by greenhouse gases like CO₂ and methane.

questions.text: Describe measures for conservation of biodiversity.
questions.answer: Conservation includes in-situ and ex-situ methods, habitat protection, legal measures and public awareness.

questions.text: Explain environmental issues caused by human activities.
questions.answer: Human activities cause pollution, deforestation, global warming and ozone depletion.

questions.text: Conservation of biodiversity is essential.
questions.answer: Because biodiversity maintains ecological balance and ensures sustainable development.
