questions.text: Name the alloy formed from copper and tin.
questions.answer: Bronze

questions.text: Name the catalyst used in Fischer–Tropsch process.
questions.answer: Cobalt–thorium alloy

questions.text: Name the catalyst used for hydrogenation of ethene to ethane.
questions.answer: Finely divided nickel

questions.text: Why salts of Sc3+ and Ti4+ are colourless?
questions.answer: They have empty d-orbitals, so d–d transitions are not possible

questions.text: Write electronic configuration of europium and gadolinium.
questions.answer: Eu: [Xe] 4f7 6s2; Gd: [Xe] 4f7 5d1 6s2

questions.text: Distinguish between lanthanoids and actinoids.
questions.answer: Lanthanoids involve 4f orbitals; actinoids involve 5f orbitals

questions.text: Why Mn2+ is more stable than Mn3+?
questions.answer: Mn2+ has half-filled 3d5 configuration

questions.text: Explain cast iron and wrought iron.
questions.answer: Cast iron is hard with ~4% carbon; wrought iron is soft with <0.2% carbon

questions.text: What are causes of lanthanoid contraction?
questions.answer: Poor shielding of 4f electrons and increasing nuclear charge

questions.text: Give similarities and differences in 3d, 4d and 5d series.
questions.answer: All are lustrous, dense metals; higher series stabilize higher oxidation states

questions.text: Discuss position of d-block elements, lanthanoids and actinoids in periodic table.
questions.answer: d-block in groups 3–12; lanthanoids and actinoids placed separately at bottom

questions.text: Calculate magnetic moment of thorium (Z=90).
What are interstitial compounds? Write properties.
questions.answer: Formed by small atoms in lattice; hard, high melting, conductive

questions.text: What are ferrous and non-ferrous alloys? Give uses.
questions.answer: Ferrous contain iron; non-ferrous do not; used in construction and machinery

questions.text: Why ground state electronic configurations of gadolinium and lutetium are different from expected?
questions.answer: Due to comparable energies of 4f and 5d orbitals leading to extra stability

questions.text: Explain trends in atomic radii, oxidation states and colour of transition metals.
questions.answer: Radii decrease across series; oxidation states vary; colour due to d–d transitions

questions.text: Which of the following elements shows variable oxidation states?
questions.answer: Iron

questions.text: The general electronic configuration of transition elements is:
questions.answer: (n−1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns¹⁻²

questions.text: Define transition element.
questions.answer: Transition elements are elements having partially filled d-orbitals in their atoms or common oxidation states.

questions.text: What are inner transition elements?
questions.answer: Inner transition elements are f-block elements including lanthanides and actinides.

questions.text: Why do transition elements show coloured compounds?
questions.answer: Due to d–d electronic transitions in partially filled d-orbitals.

questions.text: Explain catalytic property of transition metals.
questions.answer: Transition metals act as catalysts due to their variable oxidation states and ability to form complexes.

questions.text: What is lanthanide contraction?
questions.answer: Lanthanide contraction is the gradual decrease in atomic and ionic radii of lanthanides with increasing atomic number.

questions.text: Explain general characteristics of transition elements.
questions.answer: Transition elements show variable oxidation states, coloured compounds, catalytic activity, complex formation and magnetic properties.

questions.text: Describe properties and uses of lanthanides.
questions.answer: Lanthanides show similar properties, high reactivity and are used in alloys, catalysts and phosphors.

questions.text: Explain actinides and their radioactive nature.
questions.answer: Actinides are f-block elements that are mostly radioactive due to unstable nuclei.

questions.text: Transition metals form complexes.
questions.answer: Because of availability of vacant d-orbitals to accept electron pairs from ligands.

questions.text: Zinc is not considered a transition element.
questions.answer: Because zinc has completely filled d-orbitals in its atoms and common oxidation states.

chapters.title: Coordination Compounds
chapters.description: Werner's theory, nomenclature, isomerism, valence bond theory, crystal field theory, stability and applications of coordination compounds.
topics: Basic Terms: Ligand, Coordination Number, Coordination Sphere
learningObjectives: Use IUPAC rules to name coordination compounds.
Classify ligands and determine coordination number.
Identify and explain different kinds of isomerism in complexes.
Apply VBT and CFT to predict geometry and magnetic properties.
Explain stability and uses of coordination compounds.

questions.text: In the complex [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃, the coordination number of Co is:
Define ligand and give one example each of monodentate and bidentate ligand.
questions.answer: Ligand is an ion or molecule capable of donating a pair of electrons to central metal atom/ion. Monodentate: Cl⁻; Bidentate: ethane-1,2-diamine (en).

questions.text: Write IUPAC name of [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻.
questions.answer: Hexacyanidoferrate(II) ion.

questions.text: Which type of isomerism is shown by [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]Cl and [Co(NH₃)₄ClCl₂]?
questions.answer: Ionization isomerism

questions.text: Explain geometrical isomerism in square planar complex [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂].
questions.answer: In square planar [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂], ligands can be arranged as cis (two Cl⁻ adjacent) and trans (two Cl⁻ opposite). These isomers differ in physical and chemical properties; cis is more reactive and used as anticancer drug (cis-platin).

questions.text: What is effective atomic number (EAN)? State its significance.
questions.answer: EAN is the total number of electrons present around the central metal ion including those donated by ligands. Complexes with EAN equal to nearest noble gas configuration are often more stable.

questions.text: A complex with d²sp³ hybridization has which geometry?
questions.answer: Octahedral (inner orbital)

questions.text: Explain high-spin and low-spin complexes with reference to crystal field splitting.
questions.answer: In octahedral field, Δo may be small or large. For weak-field ligands (small Δo), electrons occupy higher energy t2g and eg orbitals singly, giving more unpaired electrons (high-spin complex). For strong-field ligands (large Δo), electrons pair in lower t2g orbitals before occupying eg, giving fewer unpaired electrons (low-spin complex).

questions.text: Give any two applications of coordination compounds in daily life or industry.
questions.answer: Used in metallurgy for extraction (e.g., cyanide complexes in gold extraction), as catalysts (e.g., Wilkinson's catalyst), in medicine (e.g., cis-platin), and as complexometric indicators (EDTA in water hardness estimation).

questions.text: Calculate the oxidation state of cobalt in the complex [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂.
questions.answer: Let oxidation state of Co be x. NH₃ is neutral, Cl⁻ ligand is −1, two counter Cl⁻ are −2: x + (−1) + 0 = +2 (overall charge of complex cation). So x = +3.

questions.text: Amongst the following, the ambidentate ligand is
questions.answer: thiocyanate ion

questions.text: The charge on metal ion in [Fe(CN)6]4− is
The effective atomic number of cobalt in [Co(NH3)6]3+ is
The IUPAC name of Na3[AlF6] is
questions.answer: sodium hexafluoroaluminate(III)

questions.text: Hybridization of cobalt in [Co(NH3)6]3+ is
questions.answer: d2sp3

questions.text: The geometry of [CoF6]3− complex ion is
questions.answer: octahedral

questions.text: The pair [Co(NH3)5(SO4)]Br and [Co(NH3)5Br]SO4 exhibits
questions.answer: ionisation isomerism

questions.text: Write coordination number of Fe3+ in [Fe(C2O4)3]3−.
Write chemical composition of carnallite.
questions.answer: KCl·MgCl2·6H2O

questions.text: Write oxidation number of iron in [Fe(CO)5].
Calculate EAN of iron in [Fe(CN)6]4−.
Name the type of isomerism shown by [Co(NH3)5(NO2)]2+ and [Co(NH3)5(ONO)]2+.
questions.answer: Linkage isomerism

questions.text: Write IUPAC name of [Fe(CN)6]4−.
questions.answer: Hexacyanoferrate(II) ion

questions.text: Explain homoleptic and heteroleptic complexes.
questions.answer: Homoleptic complexes have only one type of ligand; heteroleptic complexes have more than one type of ligand.

questions.text: Write four postulates of Werner's theory.
questions.answer: Metals show primary and secondary valencies; primary are ionisable, secondary are non-ionisable; secondary valency equals coordination number; secondary valencies have fixed spatial arrangement.

questions.text: Write one example each of bidentate and ambidentate ligand.
questions.answer: Bidentate: oxalate ion; Ambidentate: thiocyanate ion

questions.text: Distinguish between double salt and coordination compound.
questions.answer: Double salts dissociate completely in water; coordination compounds retain identity in solution.

questions.text: Define coordination isomers and hydrate isomers.
questions.answer: Coordination isomers involve exchange of ligands between cationic and anionic complexes; hydrate isomers involve exchange of water molecules.

questions.text: Write two applications of coordination compounds.
questions.answer: Used in medicines like cisplatin and in estimation of hardness of water using EDTA.

questions.text: Classify ligands with one example of each.
questions.answer: Monodentate: Cl−; Bidentate: ethylenediamine; Hexadentate: EDTA; Ambidentate: NO2−

questions.text: Define coordination number and anionic sphere complex. Draw optical isomers of [Co(en)3]3+.
questions.answer: Coordination number is number of donor atoms attached; anionic sphere complex has negatively charged coordination sphere.

questions.text: Calculate EAN of [Fe(CN)6]3− and explain significance of EAN.
questions.answer: EAN = 35; it indicates stability of complex.

questions.text: Define ligand and explain magnetic properties of [Ni(CN)4]2−.
questions.answer: Ligands donate electron pairs; [Ni(CN)4]2− is diamagnetic due to dsp2 hybridization.

questions.text: Write oxidation state and coordination number of [Co(NH3)4Cl2]+. Calculate EAN of iron in [Fe(CN)6]4−. Write IUPAC name of [Zn(NH3)4]2+.
questions.answer: Oxidation state of Co is +3; coordination number is 6; EAN of Fe is 36; name is tetraamminezinc(II) ion.

questions.text: Explain why [Co(NH3)6]3+ is low spin and write geometry and number of unpaired electrons.
questions.answer: NH3 is strong field ligand causing pairing; geometry is octahedral; unpaired electrons = 0.

questions.text: For [CoF6]3− write hybridization, number of unpaired electrons, geometry and magnetic property.
questions.answer: Hybridization sp3d2; unpaired electrons 4; geometry octahedral; paramagnetic.

questions.text: The coordination number of cobalt in [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 is:
Which of the following is a bidentate ligand?
questions.answer: C2O4²−

questions.text: Define coordination compound.
questions.answer: A coordination compound is a compound containing a central metal atom or ion surrounded by ligands linked through coordinate bonds.

questions.text: What is ligand?
questions.answer: A ligand is an ion or molecule that donates a pair of electrons to the central metal atom or ion to form a coordinate bond.

questions.text: Define coordination number.
questions.answer: Coordination number is the number of ligands directly attached to the central metal atom or ion.

questions.text: What is chelation?
questions.answer: Chelation is the formation of ring structures when a polydentate ligand binds to a central metal ion.

questions.text: Explain ionisation isomerism with an example.
questions.answer: Ionisation isomerism occurs when compounds produce different ions in solution, e.g., [Co(NH3)5Br]SO4 and [Co(NH3)5SO4]Br.

questions.text: Explain geometrical isomerism in coordination compounds.
questions.answer: Geometrical isomerism arises due to different spatial arrangements of ligands around the central metal ion.

questions.text: Explain Werner's theory of coordination compounds.
questions.answer: Werner proposed primary and secondary valencies explaining bonding, structure and properties of coordination compounds.

questions.text: Describe different types of isomerism in coordination compounds.
questions.answer: Isomerism includes structural (ionisation, hydrate) and stereoisomerism (geometrical, optical).

questions.text: Coordination compounds show optical isomerism.
questions.answer: Due to asymmetric arrangement of ligands around the central metal ion.

questions.text: Chelated complexes are more stable than non-chelated complexes.
questions.answer: Because chelation forms ring structures which increase stability.

chapters.title: Halogen Derivatives
chapters.description: Classification, nomenclature, methods of preparation and reactions of haloalkanes and haloarenes, mechanism of nucleophilic substitution and elimination reactions.
topics: Classification and Nomenclature of Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
learningObjectives: Write IUPAC names and classify haloalkanes and haloarenes.
Describe methods of preparation and properties of halogen derivatives.
Differentiate between SN1 and SN2 mechanisms.
Explain elimination reactions and Saytzeff rule.
Discuss uses and environmental hazards of important polyhalogen compounds.

questions.text: Which of the following is a primary haloalkane?
questions.answer: 1-bromopropane

questions.text: Write IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(Br)–CH₂–CH₃.
questions.answer: 2-bromobutane.

questions.text: What is Walden inversion?
questions.answer: In SN2 reactions at a chiral carbon, the configuration inverts due to backside attack of nucleophile; this is called Walden inversion.

questions.text: SN1 reactions are favoured by:
options: Primary halides in polar protic solvents
Tertiary halides in polar protic solvents
Primary halides in polar aprotic solvents
questions.answer: Tertiary halides in polar protic solvents

questions.text: State Saytzeff's rule with an example.
questions.answer: In dehydrohalogenation of haloalkanes, the major alkene formed is the one with greater number of alkyl substituents on doubly bonded carbon atoms. Example: 2-bromobutane gives mainly 2-butene.

questions.text: Explain the electrophilic substitution reactions of chlorobenzene.
questions.answer: Chlorobenzene undergoes substitution such as nitration, sulphonation and halogenation. Cl is deactivating but o,p-directing. Reaction conditions are harsher than benzene due to −I effect of Cl.

questions.text: Which of these is a polyhalogen compound used as a refrigerant?
questions.answer: Freon-12

questions.text: Why are aryl halides less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution than alkyl halides?
questions.answer: Due to partial double bond character of C–X bond because of resonance and because the carbon in ring is sp²-hybridized and holds halogen more strongly.

questions.text: Differentiate between SN1 and SN2 mechanisms (any three points).
questions.answer: SN1: two-step, carbocation intermediate, first order, favoured by tertiary halides and polar protic solvents, racemization at chiral centre. SN2: one-step, backside attack, second order, favoured by primary halides and polar aprotic solvents, Walden inversion.

questions.text: A chiral haloalkane undergoes SN1 reaction. If the initial optical rotation is +20°, what will be the observed rotation if complete racemization occurs?
questions.answer: For complete racemization, equal amounts of enantiomers are formed; net optical rotation becomes 0°.

questions.text: The type of monohalogen derivative in which a halogen atom is bonded to sp3 hybridized carbon atom next to carbon–carbon double bond is
questions.answer: allylic halide

questions.text: Aromatic electrophilic substitution with iodine can be carried out using
questions.answer: HNO3

questions.text: For the isomeric dichlorobenzenes, melting point of _____ is higher
questions.answer: para isomer

questions.text: Optical activity of a molecule is associated with
questions.answer: 3-D structure of a molecule

questions.text: Propane nitrile can be prepared by heating
questions.answer: ethyl bromide with alcoholic KCN

questions.text: The following will react faster by SN1 mechanism
questions.answer: 2-chloro-2-methylpropane

questions.text: Major product of the reaction CH3CH2MgBr + NH3 is
questions.answer: CH3CH3

questions.text: Write IUPAC name of C6H5CH2Br.
questions.answer: Bromophenylmethane

questions.text: Write the major product when 1-methylcyclohexene reacts with HBr.
questions.answer: 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexene

questions.text: Write decreasing order of boiling point of bromomethane, chloroform, dibromomethane and bromoform.
questions.answer: bromoform > dibromomethane > chloroform > bromomethane

questions.text: Name reagent used to convert alkyl halide into ester.
questions.answer: Silver carboxylate

questions.text: Which halide undergoes dehydrohalogenation most easily?
questions.answer: Tertiary alkyl halide

questions.text: Name reaction of aryl halide with sodium in dry ether.
questions.answer: Fittig reaction

questions.text: Why aryl halides are less reactive than alkyl halides towards nucleophilic substitution?
questions.answer: Due to resonance stabilization and partial double bond character of C–X bond

questions.text: Explain Wurtz–Fittig reaction.
questions.answer: Reaction of aryl halide with alkyl halide and sodium in dry ether gives alkylbenzene

questions.text: Explain optical activity of 2-chlorobutane.
questions.answer: It has chiral carbon atom leading to non-superimposable mirror images

questions.text: Distinguish between SN1 and SN2 reactions.
questions.answer: SN1 is unimolecular with carbocation intermediate; SN2 is bimolecular with backside attack

questions.text: Why alkyl halides are insoluble in water?
questions.answer: Strong alkyl–alkyl attraction and weak alkyl–water attraction

questions.text: Explain why primary benzylic halide shows higher SN1 reactivity.
questions.answer: Due to resonance-stabilized benzylic carbocation

questions.text: Explain factors affecting SN1 and SN2 reactions.
questions.answer: Nature of substrate, nucleophile strength and solvent polarity

questions.text: Explain aqueous alkaline hydrolysis of tert-butyl bromide.
questions.answer: It follows SN1 mechanism forming tert-butanol via carbocation intermediate

questions.text: How are the following conversions carried out: Propene to 1-iodopropane, Propene to 2-nitropropane.
questions.answer: Via peroxide effect followed by NaI; via addition of HBr then AgNO2

questions.text: What is Grignard reagent? Why is it prepared in dry ether?
questions.answer: RMgX; moisture destroys Grignard reagent

questions.text: Write equations for preparation of ethyl chloride using HCl, ethene and thionyl chloride. Which method is preferred?
questions.answer: Preparation using thionyl chloride is preferred due to gaseous by-products

questions.text: What is dehydrohalogenation? State Saytzeff rule and explain products formed from 2-chloro-2-methylbutane.
questions.answer: Elimination of HX; Saytzeff rule gives more substituted alkene as major product

questions.text: Identify the type of halides and explain reactivity towards aqueous alkaline hydrolysis.
questions.answer: Aryl halides are less reactive; alkyl halides undergo hydrolysis readily

questions.text: Which of the following is a secondary alkyl halide?
questions.answer: CH3CHClCH3

questions.text: Which reagent is used to convert alcohol into alkyl chloride?
questions.answer: PCl5

questions.text: Define alkyl halide.
questions.answer: Alkyl halides are organic compounds in which one or more hydrogen atoms of an alkane are replaced by halogen atoms.

questions.text: What is Wurtz reaction?
questions.answer: Wurtz reaction involves coupling of alkyl halides with sodium metal in dry ether to form higher alkanes.

questions.text: Explain SN1 reaction.
questions.answer: SN1 reaction is a nucleophilic substitution reaction that proceeds via carbocation intermediate and follows first order kinetics.

questions.text: Explain SN2 reaction.
questions.answer: SN2 reaction is a bimolecular nucleophilic substitution reaction occurring in a single step with inversion of configuration.

questions.text: Why tertiary alkyl halides undergo SN1 reaction?
questions.answer: Because tertiary carbocations are more stable due to inductive and hyperconjugation effects.

questions.text: Arrange alkyl halides in increasing order of reactivity towards SN2 reaction.
questions.answer: Tertiary < Secondary < Primary < Methyl.

questions.text: Explain preparation, properties and uses of chloroform.
questions.answer: Chloroform is prepared by chlorination of methane; it is a colourless liquid used as solvent and anesthetic (earlier).

questions.text: Explain preparation and uses of iodoform.
questions.answer: Iodoform is prepared by reaction of ethanol with iodine in presence of alkali and used as antiseptic.

questions.text: Alkyl iodides are more reactive than alkyl chlorides.
questions.answer: Because C–I bond is weaker than C–Cl bond.

questions.text: Polar solvents favour SN1 reaction.
questions.answer: Because they stabilize carbocation intermediate.

chapters.title: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
chapters.description: Nomenclature, preparation, physical and chemical properties of alcohols, phenols and ethers; acidity of alcohols and phenols; Williamson ether synthesis.
learningObjectives: Name and classify alcohols, phenols and ethers.
Describe methods of preparation of these compounds.
Explain acidity of phenols and compare with alcohols.
Discuss important reactions such as dehydration, oxidation and electrophilic substitution.
Explain Williamson synthesis and cleavage of ethers.

questions.text: Which of the following will show highest boiling point?
questions.answer: Ethanol

questions.text: Give IUPAC name of (CH₃)₃C–OH.
questions.answer: 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

questions.text: Explain why phenol is more acidic than ethanol.
questions.answer: Phenoxide ion formed after deprotonation is resonance-stabilized, whereas ethoxide ion is not; this makes phenol more acidic.

questions.text: Dehydration of ethanol with conc. H₂SO₄ at 443 K gives mainly:
questions.answer: Ethene

questions.text: Write equation for Williamson synthesis of ethoxybenzene (phenetole).
questions.answer: C₂H₅Br + C₆H₅O⁻Na⁺ → C₆H₅–O–C₂H₅ + NaBr.

questions.text: Describe electrophilic substitution reactions of phenol.
questions.answer: Phenol undergoes nitration, halogenation and sulphonation more readily than benzene due to +M effect of –OH. It is o,p-directing: nitration gives o- and p-nitrophenols; bromination gives 2,4,6-tribromophenol in absence of solvent.

questions.text: Which reagent is used to distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols?
questions.answer: Lucas reagent

questions.text: What happens when anisole reacts with HI?
questions.answer: Anisole undergoes cleavage to give phenol and iodomethane: C₆H₅–O–CH₃ + HI → C₆H₅–OH + CH₃I.

questions.text: Explain oxidation reactions of primary and secondary alcohols.
questions.answer: Primary alcohols oxidize to aldehydes and further to acids (e.g., ethanol → ethanal → ethanoic acid). Secondary alcohols oxidize to ketones (e.g., isopropanol → acetone). Tertiary alcohols resist oxidation under mild conditions.

questions.text: 0.92 g of ethanol is completely burned. Calculate moles of CO₂ formed. (Molar mass of ethanol = 46 g mol⁻¹).
questions.answer: Moles of ethanol = 0.92/46 = 0.02 mol. Combustion: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O. Moles of CO₂ = 2 × 0.02 = 0.04 mol.

questions.text: In carbinol system of nomenclature, tert-butyl alcohol is named as
questions.answer: trimethyl carbinol

questions.text: Which of the following pair of reagent is used for conversion of carboxylic acid to alcohol?
questions.answer: LiAlH4/H3O+

questions.text: Reaction between Grignard reagent and aldehyde other than formaldehyde leads to formation of
questions.answer: secondary

questions.text: Oxidation of ethyl alcohol using K2Cr2O7/dil. H2SO4 leads to formation of
questions.answer: acetic acid

questions.text: When vapours of tert-butyl alcohol are passed over hot copper, it gives
questions.answer: isobutylene

questions.text: Reaction between hot conc. HI and anisole gives
questions.answer: phenol and methyl iodide

questions.text: The reagents used to convert phenol to 2,4,6-tribromophenol is
questions.answer: Br2/H2O

questions.text: Why phenols give deep coloration with neutral ferric chloride?
questions.answer: Due to formation of ferric phenoxide

questions.text: Write IUPAC name of crotonyl alcohol.
questions.answer: But-2-en-1-ol

questions.text: Name the major product of hydroboration–oxidation of propene.
questions.answer: Propan-1-ol

questions.text: Write reaction to get aspirin from salicylic acid.
questions.answer: Salicylic acid reacts with acetic anhydride to form aspirin

questions.text: What is the major product when anisole reacts with HI at 398 K?
questions.answer: Phenol

questions.text: What is the action of atmospheric oxygen on ethers?
questions.answer: Ethers form peroxides

questions.text: Name the reaction used to convert phenol to salicylaldehyde.
questions.answer: Reimer–Tiemann reaction

questions.text: What is the action of H2/Ni and LiAlH4/H3O+ on pent-3-enal?
questions.answer: H2/Ni reduces both C=C and –CHO; LiAlH4 reduces only –CHO group

questions.text: Write the reactions involved in preparation of phenol from benzene sulfonic acid.
questions.answer: Benzene sulfonic acid → sodium phenoxide → phenol

questions.text: Write Kolbe's reaction.
questions.answer: Sodium phenoxide reacts with CO2 at 398 K followed by acidification to give salicylic acid

questions.text: Name reagents used to convert phenol into picric acid and p-benzoquinone.
questions.answer: Conc. HNO3/H2SO4 and chromic anhydride respectively

questions.text: Write chemical equation of acetyl chloride with ethanol.
questions.answer: Ethanol reacts with acetyl chloride to form ethyl ethanoate

questions.text: Explain why alkoxy group is ring activating and ortho/para directing.
questions.answer: Due to +R effect increasing electron density at ortho and para positions

questions.text: Explain action of dilute HNO3, conc. H2SO4 and Br2/CS2 on phenol.
questions.answer: Dil. HNO3 gives o- and p-nitrophenol; conc. H2SO4 gives phenol sulfonic acid; Br2/CS2 gives o- and p-bromophenol

questions.text: Explain Lucas test to distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols.
questions.answer: Based on turbidity formation time with Lucas reagent

questions.text: How will you bring about conversion of isopropyl alcohol to acetone?
questions.answer: By oxidation using Cu/573 K or chromic anhydride

questions.text: Explain Dow process.
questions.answer: Chlorobenzene is converted to phenol using NaOH at high temperature and pressure

questions.text: Write preparation of ethanol from methyl magnesium iodide.
questions.answer: Methyl magnesium iodide reacts with formaldehyde followed by hydrolysis to give ethanol

questions.text: Write preparation of phenol from aniline.
questions.answer: Aniline → benzene diazonium chloride → phenol by hydrolysis

questions.text: Write chemical reactions to convert phenol into salicylaldehyde. What happens if CCl4 is used instead of CHCl3?
questions.answer: Phenol reacts with CHCl3/NaOH to give salicylaldehyde; with CCl4 gives salicylic acid

questions.text: An organic compound gives hydrogen with sodium metal and forms aldehyde on oxidation. Identify compound and justify.
questions.answer: Ethanol; reacts with Na to give H2 and oxidizes to acetaldehyde

questions.text: How will you prepare diethyl ether by dehydration of alcohol? State limitations and reactions with dil. H2SO4 and PCl5.
questions.answer: Diethyl ether is prepared by dehydration of ethanol at 413 K; limitations include formation of alkene at higher temperature

questions.text: Which of the following alcohols gives Lucas test immediately?
questions.answer: Propan-2-ol

questions.text: Phenol is more acidic than alcohol because:
questions.answer: Phenoxide ion is resonance stabilized

questions.text: Define alcohol.
questions.answer: Alcohols are organic compounds in which hydroxyl group (–OH) is attached to a saturated carbon atom.

questions.text: What are phenols?
questions.answer: Phenols are organic compounds in which hydroxyl group is directly attached to an aromatic ring.

questions.text: Explain acidic nature of phenol.
questions.answer: Phenol is acidic due to resonance stabilization of phenoxide ion formed after loss of proton.

questions.text: What is Williamson ether synthesis?
questions.answer: Williamson ether synthesis is the preparation of ethers by reaction of alkyl halide with sodium alkoxide.

questions.text: Why phenol does not give Lucas test?
questions.answer: Because phenol does not form stable carbocation due to aromatic ring.

questions.text: Arrange alcohols in increasing order of acidity.
questions.answer: Tertiary < Secondary < Primary alcohols.

questions.text: Explain preparation, properties and uses of ethanol.
questions.answer: Ethanol is prepared by fermentation; it shows hydrogen bonding and is used as solvent, fuel and antiseptic.

questions.text: Explain preparation and reactions of phenol.
questions.answer: Phenol is prepared from chlorobenzene; it undergoes electrophilic substitution reactions.

questions.text: Phenol reacts with sodium hydroxide but alcohol does not.
questions.answer: Because phenol is acidic enough to react with NaOH while alcohol is not.

questions.text: Ethers are less reactive than alcohols.
questions.answer: Because ethers do not have active hydrogen and are less polar.

chapters.title: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic acids
chapters.description: Nomenclature, preparation and reactions of aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids; nucleophilic addition, oxidation–reduction and strength of acids.
topics: Nomenclature and Structure of Carbonyl Group
Preparation and Properties of Carboxylic Acids
learningObjectives: Write IUPAC names and structures of aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids.
Explain nucleophilic addition reactions of carbonyl compounds.
Compare reactivity of aldehydes and ketones.
Describe methods of preparation and reactions of carboxylic acids.
Explain factors affecting acidity of carboxylic acids.

questions.text: The functional group present in aldehydes is:
questions.answer: –CHO

questions.text: Give IUPAC name of CH₃–CO–CH₃.
questions.answer: Propan-2-one (acetone).

questions.text: State any two differences between aldehydes and ketones.
questions.answer: Aldehydes have –CHO group at end of chain while ketones have >C=O within chain; aldehydes are generally more reactive and are easily oxidized to acids, whereas ketones resist oxidation.

questions.text: Benedict's solution is used to distinguish:
questions.answer: Aldehydes and ketones

questions.text: Write the reaction of acetaldehyde with hydrogen cyanide.
questions.answer: CH₃–CHO + HCN → CH₃–CH(OH)–CN (cyanohydrin).

questions.text: Explain the mechanism of nucleophilic addition to the carbonyl group.
questions.answer: First, nucleophile attacks electrophilic carbon of C=O, forming a tetrahedral intermediate. Then protonation of oxygen (or deprotonation of nucleophile) occurs to give addition product. Polarization of C=O makes carbon susceptible to nucleophilic attack.

questions.text: The reaction of carboxylic acid with alcohol in presence of conc. H₂SO₄ is called:
questions.answer: Esterification

questions.text: Why are carboxylic acids stronger acids than alcohols?
questions.answer: Carboxylate ion is resonance-stabilized with negative charge delocalized over two oxygen atoms, whereas alkoxide ion is not; this stabilizes conjugate base and increases acidity.

questions.text: Explain Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction.
questions.answer: HVZ reaction is α-halogenation of carboxylic acids. Carboxylic acid is converted to its acyl halide with PCl₃/Cl₂, then halogen substitutes α-hydrogen, followed by hydrolysis to give α-halo acid.

questions.text: 0.1 mol of acetic acid is neutralized by NaOH releasing 5.7 kJ heat. Calculate molar enthalpy of neutralization.
questions.answer: ΔHneutralization = −5.7 kJ / 0.1 mol = −57 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.text: Which of the following is the product of reaction of ethanenitrile with Grignard reagent followed by acid hydrolysis?
questions.answer: A ketone

questions.text: Which reaction is used to synthesize straight chain alkyl substituted benzenes?
questions.answer: Etard reaction

questions.text: Ketones cannot be converted into carboxylic acid using
questions.answer: CrO3

questions.text: The correct order of acidic strength is
questions.answer: Fluoroacetic > chloroacetic > acetic

questions.text: Addition of sodium bisulphite to ethanal is an example of
questions.answer: Nucleophilic addition

questions.text: The following compounds give positive Fehling's test
questions.answer: Butanal

questions.text: The reducing agent which cannot reduce –COOH group is
questions.answer: NaBH4

questions.text: Write IUPAC name of phthalaldehyde.
questions.answer: Benzene-1,2-dicarbaldehyde

questions.text: What is substituted imine called?
questions.answer: Schiff's base

questions.text: Write the product obtained when ketones react with 1,2-diol in presence of dry HCl.
questions.answer: Cyclic ketal

questions.text: Name the reaction in which aldehydes undergo disproportionation.
questions.answer: Cannizzaro reaction

questions.text: What is the product formed when carboxylic acid is heated with P2O5?
questions.answer: Acid anhydride

questions.text: Which aldehyde does not give aldol condensation?
questions.answer: Formaldehyde

questions.text: Write one use of Tollens' reagent.
questions.answer: To distinguish aldehydes from ketones

questions.text: Classify aliphatic ketones with suitable examples.
questions.answer: Simple ketones have identical alkyl groups; mixed ketones have different alkyl groups.

questions.text: What is the action of Grignard reagent on benzonitrile?
questions.answer: Forms ketone after acid hydrolysis

questions.text: Why carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than ethers?
questions.answer: Due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding and dimer formation

questions.text: Write Cannizzaro reaction with example.
questions.answer: Aldehydes without α-hydrogen undergo disproportionation in presence of strong alkali

questions.text: Write reaction of propanal with hydroxylamine.
questions.answer: Propanal forms oxime derivative

questions.text: How is acid amide prepared from acid chloride?
questions.answer: By reacting acid chloride with ammonia

questions.text: Explain aldol condensation reaction.
questions.answer: Aldehydes or ketones with α-hydrogen form β-hydroxy aldehydes or ketones in presence of base

questions.text: Write reactions for conversion of benzene to benzaldehyde.
questions.answer: By Gattermann–Koch reaction

questions.text: Explain haloform reaction with example.
questions.answer: Methyl ketones give haloform in presence of halogen and base

questions.text: How will you distinguish acetaldehyde from acetone?
questions.answer: By Tollens' test or Fehling's solution test

questions.text: Write chemical reactions to convert acetic acid to ethanol.
questions.answer: By reduction using LiAlH4

questions.text: Explain acidity of carboxylic acids.
questions.answer: Due to resonance stabilization of carboxylate ion

questions.text: Draw structure of salicylaldehyde and explain acidic nature of carboxylic acids.
questions.answer: Carboxylate ion is resonance stabilized making carboxylic acids acidic

questions.text: Explain reactions of aldehydes with Tollens' reagent and Fehling's solution.
questions.answer: Aldehydes reduce Tollens' reagent forming silver mirror and Fehling's solution forming red precipitate

questions.text: Complete the following sequence of reactions and identify products.
questions.answer: Grignard reagent forms alcohols and carboxylic acids after hydrolysis

questions.text: Which functional group is present in aldehydes?
questions.answer: –CHO

questions.text: Which of the following does not give Tollens' test?
questions.answer: Acetone

questions.text: Define aldehydes.
questions.answer: Aldehydes are organic compounds containing the functional group –CHO.

questions.text: What are ketones?
questions.answer: Ketones are organic compounds containing carbonyl group (–CO–) bonded to two carbon atoms.

questions.text: Explain nucleophilic addition reaction of aldehydes.
questions.answer: Aldehydes undergo nucleophilic addition due to polar C=O bond, where nucleophile attacks carbonyl carbon.

questions.text: Distinguish between aldehydes and ketones.
questions.answer: Aldehydes have –CHO group and are easily oxidised; ketones have –CO– group and resist oxidation.

questions.text: Why aldehydes are more reactive than ketones?
questions.answer: Because aldehydes have less steric hindrance and stronger positive charge on carbonyl carbon.

questions.text: Give chemical test to distinguish aldehyde and ketone.
questions.answer: Tollens' test gives silver mirror with aldehydes but not with ketones.

questions.text: Explain preparation and reactions of formaldehyde.
questions.answer: Formaldehyde is prepared by oxidation of methanol and shows nucleophilic addition and oxidation reactions.

questions.text: Explain preparation and properties of acetic acid.
questions.answer: Acetic acid is prepared by oxidation of ethanol; it shows acidic reactions and esterification.

questions.text: Carboxylic acids are stronger acids than phenols.
questions.answer: Because carboxylate ion is more stabilized by resonance than phenoxide ion.

questions.text: Ketones do not give Tollens' test.
questions.answer: Because ketones are not easily oxidised.

chapters.title: Amines
chapters.description: Classification, nomenclature, methods of preparation, basic character, reactions and identification of primary, secondary and tertiary amines.
topics: Basicity of Amines and Factors Affecting It
Aromatic Diazonium Salts and Their Reactions
Distinction between Primary, Secondary and Tertiary Amines
learningObjectives: Classify and name aliphatic and aromatic amines.
Describe various methods of preparation of amines.
Explain basic nature of amines and compare strengths.
Discuss important reactions including diazotization and coupling.
Use chemical tests to distinguish different classes of amines.

questions.text: Which of the following is a secondary amine?
questions.answer: (CH₃)₂NH

questions.text: Write IUPAC name of aniline.
questions.answer: Benzenamine.

questions.text: State carbylamine reaction.
questions.answer: Primary amines on heating with chloroform and alcoholic KOH form isocyanides (carbylamines) with foul smell; used as a test for primary amines.

questions.text: Which amine is most basic in aqueous solution?
questions.answer: (C₂H₅)₂NH

questions.text: What is diazotization? Write equation for diazotization of aniline.
questions.answer: Conversion of primary aromatic amine into diazonium salt with nitrous acid at low temperature. C₆H₅NH₂ + HNO₂ + HCl → C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻ + 2H₂O.

questions.text: Explain why aniline is less basic than ethylamine.
questions.answer: In aniline, lone pair on nitrogen is delocalized into benzene ring by resonance, reducing availability for protonation. In ethylamine, lone pair is localized and +I effect of ethyl group increases electron density, making it more basic.

questions.text: Which reagent is used to distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary amines?
questions.answer: HNO₂

questions.text: What is coupling reaction of diazonium salts?
questions.answer: Aromatic diazonium salts react with phenols or aromatic amines to form azo compounds with –N=N– linkage, often coloured dyes.

questions.text: Explain Gabriel phthalimide synthesis for preparation of primary amines.
questions.answer: Phthalimide reacts with alcoholic KOH to form potassium salt, which undergoes nucleophilic substitution with alkyl halide to form N-alkyl phthalimide. Hydrolysis of this gives primary amine and phthalic acid.

questions.text: 0.93 g of an amine neutralizes 0.1 mol of HCl. Determine molar mass of the amine assuming it is monobasic.
questions.answer: If it neutralizes 0.1 mol HCl, moles of amine = 0.1 mol. Molar mass = 0.93 / 0.1 = 9.3 g mol⁻¹ (hypothetical example for calculation practice).

questions.text: The following amine is the product of Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.
questions.answer: Primary aliphatic amine

questions.text: Mendius reaction is used to convert
questions.answer: alkyl cyanide into amine

questions.text: The strongest base amongst the following is
questions.answer: N,N-Dimethylmethanamine

questions.text: The reaction in which diazonium salt is used
questions.answer: Sandmeyer reaction

questions.text: The type of isopropylamine is a
questions.answer: primary amine

questions.text: Aniline on reaction with bromine water produces
questions.answer: 2,4,6-Tribromoaniline

questions.text: Tertiary amines have lowest boiling points because
options: they do not possess intermolecular H-bonding
questions.answer: they do not possess intermolecular H-bonding

questions.text: Name the process of breaking C–X bond by ammonia in preparation of amines.
questions.answer: Ammonolysis

questions.text: Write the name of reaction in which aromatic primary amines produce offensive smell.
questions.answer: Carbylamine reaction

questions.text: Which gas is evolved when a primary amine reacts with nitrous acid?
questions.answer: Nitrogen gas

questions.text: Write the order of reactivity of alkyl halides with ammonia.
questions.answer: R–I > R–Br > R–Cl

questions.text: Name Hinsberg's reagent.
questions.answer: Benzenesulphonyl chloride

questions.text: Why N,N-dimethylaniline does not react with acetyl chloride?
questions.answer: It has no replaceable hydrogen on nitrogen

questions.text: Explain basic nature of amines.
questions.answer: Amines are basic due to presence of a lone pair of electrons on nitrogen atom.

questions.text: Write the reaction of methyl chloride with ammonia.
questions.answer: CH3Cl + NH3 → CH3NH2

questions.text: Explain carbylamine reaction.
questions.answer: Primary amines on heating with chloroform and alcoholic KOH give foul-smelling isocyanides.

questions.text: Write IUPAC names of p-toluidine and trimethylamine.
questions.answer: 4-Methylaniline and N,N-dimethylmethanamine

questions.text: What is the action of nitrous acid on aniline?
questions.answer: Aniline forms benzene diazonium chloride.

questions.text: Write one method to convert alkyl cyanide into alkylamine.
questions.answer: Reduction using Na/C2H5OH or LiAlH4.

questions.text: Distinguish between primary, secondary and tertiary amines using Hinsberg's test.
questions.answer: Primary forms soluble sulphonamide, secondary forms insoluble sulphonamide, tertiary does not react.

questions.text: Explain Hoffmann's exhaustive alkylation.
questions.answer: Alkylation of amines with excess alkyl halide forms quaternary ammonium salt.

questions.text: Explain nitration of aniline.
questions.answer: Direct nitration gives o-, m- and p-nitroaniline due to protonation of –NH2 group.

questions.text: Explain classification of amines based on functional group.
questions.answer: Amines are classified as primary, secondary and tertiary depending on number of alkyl groups attached to nitrogen.

questions.text: Explain Sandmeyer reaction.
questions.answer: Aryl diazonium salts react with CuCl/CuBr to form aryl halides.

questions.text: Write reactions for preparation of ethanamine using Gabriel phthalimide synthesis. Why aniline cannot be prepared by this method?
questions.answer: Gabriel synthesis gives primary aliphatic amines; aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution.

questions.text: Explain basicity of amines with suitable examples.
questions.answer: Basicity depends on +I effect, solvation and resonance effects.

questions.text: Explain Hoffmann elimination reaction with suitable example.
questions.answer: Quaternary ammonium hydroxides on heating give least substituted alkene.

questions.text: Which of the following is a primary amine?
questions.answer: CH3NH2

questions.text: Aniline on diazotisation gives:
questions.answer: Benzene diazonium chloride

questions.text: Define amines.
questions.answer: Amines are organic compounds derived from ammonia by replacement of one or more hydrogen atoms by alkyl or aryl groups.

questions.text: What are aromatic amines?
questions.answer: Aromatic amines are amines in which amino group is directly attached to an aromatic ring.

questions.text: Explain basic nature of amines.
questions.answer: Amines are basic due to availability of lone pair of electrons on nitrogen atom which can accept a proton.

questions.text: Arrange amines in increasing order of basic strength.
questions.answer: Aromatic amines < Primary aliphatic < Secondary aliphatic < Tertiary aliphatic.

questions.text: Why aniline is less basic than aliphatic amines?
questions.answer: Because lone pair on nitrogen is delocalised into benzene ring by resonance.

questions.text: Explain Hoffmann bromamide reaction.
questions.answer: In Hoffmann bromamide reaction, amide is converted to amine with one carbon less using bromine and alkali.

questions.text: Explain preparation and reactions of aniline.
questions.answer: Aniline is prepared by reduction of nitrobenzene and undergoes diazotisation and electrophilic substitution reactions.

questions.text: Explain diazotisation and coupling reactions.
questions.answer: Diazotisation converts aromatic amine into diazonium salt which undergoes coupling to form azo dyes.

questions.text: Aniline is ortho-para directing in electrophilic substitution reactions.
questions.answer: Because –NH2 group activates benzene ring and directs incoming electrophile to ortho and para positions.

questions.text: Diazonium salts are prepared at low temperature.
questions.answer: Because diazonium salts are unstable at higher temperatures.

chapters.title: Biomolecules
chapters.description: Carbohydrates, amino acids, proteins, vitamins and nucleic acids – their classification, structure and biological importance.
learningObjectives: Classify carbohydrates and represent monosaccharides using Fischer and Haworth projections.
Explain structure of amino acids and formation of peptides.
Describe different levels of protein structure.
Differentiate between DNA and RNA in structure and function.
Explain role of vitamins and enzymes in biological systems.

questions.text: Glucose is an example of:
questions.answer: Monosaccharide

questions.text: What is an essential amino acid?
questions.answer: Amino acid that cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be supplied through diet is called essential amino acid.

questions.text: Define peptide bond.
questions.answer: Peptide bond is an amide linkage formed between –COOH group of one amino acid and –NH₂ group of another with elimination of water (–CO–NH–).

questions.text: Which of the following is a storage polysaccharide in animals?
questions.answer: Glycogen

questions.text: Explain primary, secondary and tertiary structure of proteins.
questions.answer: Primary: linear sequence of amino acids. Secondary: regular folding into α-helix or β-pleated sheet due to hydrogen bonding. Tertiary: further folding into specific 3D shape stabilized by H-bonds, disulphide bonds, hydrophobic interactions and ionic interactions.

questions.text: Name the vitamin whose deficiency causes scurvy and give its chemical name.
questions.answer: Vitamin C; chemical name ascorbic acid.

questions.text: The sugar present in RNA is:
questions.answer: Ribose

questions.text: Differentiate between DNA and RNA (any three points).
questions.answer: DNA has deoxyribose sugar, RNA has ribose. DNA contains bases A, G, C, T while RNA has A, G, C, U. DNA is double stranded helix, RNA usually single stranded. DNA is genetic material; RNA involved in protein synthesis.

questions.text: What is an enzyme? Mention any one characteristic.
questions.answer: Enzymes are biocatalysts which speed up biochemical reactions. They are highly specific for substrate and work under mild conditions.

questions.text: If a tripeptide is made from three different amino acids A, B and C, how many different sequences are possible?
questions.answer: Number of permutations of 3 different amino acids = 3! = 6 sequences.

questions.text: Glucose on oxidation with dilute nitric acid gives
questions.answer: saccharic acid

questions.text: The glycosidic linkage in maltose is formed between
options: C-1 of α-D-glucose and C-4 of α-D-glucose
C-1 of β-D-glucose and C-4 of β-D-glucose
C-1 of α-D-glucose and C-2 of α-D-fructose
C-1 of β-D-glucose and C-1 of β-D-glucose
questions.answer: C-1 of α-D-glucose and C-4 of α-D-glucose

questions.text: The optically inactive α-amino acid among the following is
questions.answer: glycine

questions.text: The sugar moiety of nucleotide unit in RNA is
questions.answer: D-ribose

questions.text: The chemical nature of peptide bond in proteins is
questions.answer: secondary amide

questions.text: Which of the following structure of DNA carries genetic information?
questions.answer: double helical structure

questions.text: In the process of denaturation, there is NO change in the structure of following protein
questions.answer: primary

questions.text: Write the name of polysaccharide used for commercial preparation of glucose.
questions.answer: Starch

questions.text: Write the name of the base present in DNA but not found in RNA.
questions.answer: Thymine

questions.text: Write the number of chiral carbon atoms present in fructose.
Sugar present in DNA is
questions.answer: 2-deoxy-D-ribose

questions.text: Name the unit to which glucose units are linked to form sucrose.
questions.answer: Fructose

questions.text: Write the structure type of alanine present in aqueous solution.
questions.answer: Zwitter ion

questions.text: Write the formula of peptide bond.
questions.answer: -CO-NH-

questions.text: Define peptide bond.
questions.answer: The bond that connects α-amino acids to each other is called peptide bond.

questions.text: Write types of proteins depending upon molecular shape.
questions.answer: Globular proteins and fibrous proteins

questions.text: Define nucleotide.
questions.answer: Repeating monomers in unbranched polymers of nucleic acids are called nucleotides.

questions.text: What is denaturation of proteins?
questions.answer: Disruption of secondary, tertiary or quaternary structure of proteins without breaking peptide bonds.

questions.text: Write two industrial applications of enzyme catalysis.
questions.answer: Manufacture of glucose from starch; manufacture of detergents using proteases

questions.text: Write two differences between DNA and RNA.
questions.answer: DNA contains deoxyribose and thymine; RNA contains ribose and uracil

questions.text: Classify carbohydrates with one example of each.
questions.answer: Monosaccharide: glucose; disaccharide: sucrose; polysaccharide: starch

questions.text: Write the names of globular proteins.
questions.answer: Albumin, insulin

questions.text: Explain classification of carbohydrates with examples.
questions.answer: Carbohydrates are classified as monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides based on hydrolysis.

questions.text: Explain D and L configuration in sugars.
questions.answer: Configuration depends on the position of OH group on the chiral carbon farthest from carbonyl carbon.

questions.text: Explain structure of proteins.
questions.answer: Proteins have primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary structures.

questions.text: Explain primary structure of proteins.
questions.answer: It is the sequence of amino acids linked by peptide bonds.

questions.text: Explain globular and fibrous proteins with examples.
questions.answer: Globular proteins are spherical and soluble; fibrous proteins are thread-like and insoluble.

questions.text: Explain Haworth projection of carbohydrates.
questions.answer: It represents cyclic structure of sugars showing orientation of substituents above or below the plane.

questions.text: Define carbohydrates. Classify carbohydrates with suitable examples.
questions.answer: Carbohydrates are polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones or substances that yield them on hydrolysis.

questions.text: How is glucose prepared on commercial scale?
questions.answer: Glucose is prepared by hydrolysis of starch with dilute sulphuric acid at high temperature and pressure.

questions.text: Which of the following is a reducing sugar?
questions.answer: Glucose

questions.text: The linkage present in proteins is:
questions.answer: Peptide

questions.text: Define carbohydrates.
questions.answer: Carbohydrates are polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones or substances that yield them on hydrolysis.

questions.text: What are amino acids?
questions.answer: Amino acids are organic compounds containing both amino (–NH2) and carboxyl (–COOH) groups.

questions.text: Explain denaturation of proteins.
questions.answer: Denaturation is the loss of biological activity of proteins due to change in structure caused by heat, pH or chemicals.

questions.text: Distinguish between glucose and fructose.
questions.answer: Glucose is an aldohexose while fructose is a ketohexose.

questions.text: Why sucrose is a non-reducing sugar?
questions.answer: Because both aldehyde and ketone groups are involved in glycosidic bond formation.

questions.text: What is zwitter ion?
questions.answer: Zwitter ion is a dipolar ion having both positive and negative charges in the same molecule.

questions.text: Explain classification of carbohydrates with examples.
questions.answer: Carbohydrates are classified as monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides with suitable examples.

questions.text: Explain structure and functions of proteins.
questions.answer: Proteins are polymers of amino acids linked by peptide bonds and perform structural and catalytic functions.

questions.text: Proteins are optically active.
questions.answer: Because they contain chiral carbon atoms in amino acids.

questions.text: Starch gives blue colour with iodine.
questions.answer: Because iodine molecules get trapped in helical structure of starch.

chapters.title: Introduction to Polymer Chemistry
chapters.description: Classification of polymers, addition and condensation polymerization, natural and synthetic polymers, properties and uses of important polymers and biodegradable polymers.
topics: Types Based on Source and Structure
learningObjectives: Classify polymers on different bases such as source, structure and mode of polymerization.
Differentiate between addition and condensation polymerization.
Explain preparation and properties of important polymers like PVC, teflon, nylon and bakelite.
Describe vulcanization of rubber and its advantages.
Discuss significance of biodegradable polymers.

questions.text: The polymer of tetrafluoroethene is known as:
questions.answer: Teflon

questions.text: Define monomer and give one example.
questions.answer: Monomer is a small molecule that combines with similar molecules to form a polymer; e.g., ethene is monomer of polyethene.

questions.text: Differentiate between thermoplastics and thermosetting plastics.
questions.answer: Thermoplastics soften on heating and can be reshaped; thermosetting plastics harden permanently on heating and cannot be remoulded.

questions.text: Which of the following is a condensation polymer?
questions.answer: Nylon-6,6

questions.text: Explain vulcanization of rubber.
questions.answer: Natural rubber is heated with sulphur and accelerators. Sulphur forms cross-links between polyisoprene chains, increasing elasticity, tensile strength and resistance to temperature changes.

questions.text: What is a copolymer? Give one example.
questions.answer: Polymer formed from two or more different monomers is copolymer; e.g., Buna-S from butadiene and styrene.

questions.text: Which of the following is a biodegradable polymer?
questions.answer: PHBV

questions.text: State any two disadvantages of synthetic polymers.
questions.answer: They are often non-biodegradable causing environmental pollution; burning them may release toxic gases.

questions.text: Describe the preparation and uses of bakelite.
questions.answer: Bakelite is formed by condensation polymerization of phenol and formaldehyde in presence of acid or base catalyst, followed by cross-linking. It is a thermosetting plastic used in electrical switches, plugs, handles of utensils etc.

questions.text: If the average degree of polymerization of a polymer sample is 1000 and molecular mass of its monomer is 28 g mol⁻¹, calculate the approximate molecular mass of the polymer.
questions.answer: Molecular mass of polymer ≈ 1000 × 28 = 2.8 × 10⁴ g mol⁻¹.

questions.text: Synthetic polymer among the following is
questions.answer: nylon

questions.text: Addition polymer among the following is
questions.answer: polyethylene

questions.text: Monomer of Buna-S is
questions.answer: butadiene + styrene

questions.text: Which of the following is biodegradable polymer?
questions.answer: PHBV

questions.text: Ziegler–Natta catalyst contains
questions.answer: TiCl4 + Al(C2H5)3

questions.text: Dacron is a copolymer of
questions.answer: ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid

questions.text: Nylon-6,6 is a
questions.answer: condensation polymer

questions.text: Write the number of carbon atoms present in monomer of nylon-6.
Name the catalyst used for preparation of high density polyethylene.
questions.answer: Ziegler–Natta catalyst

questions.text: Write monomer of natural rubber.
questions.answer: Isoprene

questions.text: Name biodegradable polymer formed from two amino acids.
questions.answer: Nylon-2-nylon-6

questions.text: What is vulcanization?
questions.answer: Process of introducing cross-links in rubber

questions.text: Write one use of LDPE.
questions.answer: Packaging films

questions.text: Name polymer used for making non-stick cookware.
questions.answer: Teflon

questions.text: Define polymer.
questions.answer: High molecular mass compounds formed by repetition of simple molecules called monomers.

questions.text: What are thermoplastic polymers?
questions.answer: Polymers that soften on heating and harden on cooling repeatedly.

questions.text: Write preparation of LDPE.
questions.answer: By free radical polymerization of ethylene under high pressure and temperature.

questions.text: Explain copolymers with example.
questions.answer: Polymers formed from two or more different monomers, e.g. Buna-S.

questions.text: What is vulcanized rubber?
questions.answer: Rubber treated with sulfur to increase strength and elasticity.

questions.text: Write two uses of HDPE.
questions.answer: Pipes and containers

questions.text: Classify polymers on the basis of origin.
questions.answer: Natural, semi-synthetic and synthetic polymers.

questions.text: Write monomers of nylon-6,6.
questions.answer: Hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid.

questions.text: What are elastomers?
questions.answer: Polymers with elastic properties like rubber.

questions.text: Differentiate between addition and condensation polymers.
questions.answer: Addition polymers form without by-product; condensation polymers form with elimination of small molecules.

questions.text: Explain preparation and uses of HDPE.
questions.answer: Prepared using Ziegler–Natta catalyst; used for pipes and containers.

questions.text: Explain vulcanization of rubber.
questions.answer: Sulfur cross-links are introduced to improve elasticity and strength.

questions.text: Explain free radical polymerization mechanism.
questions.answer: It involves initiation, propagation and termination steps.

questions.text: Write properties of nylon-6,6.
questions.answer: High tensile strength, abrasion resistance and toughness.

questions.text: Explain thermosetting polymers with examples.
questions.answer: Rigid polymers that cannot be remoulded, e.g. bakelite.

questions.text: Write preparation, properties and uses of nylon-6,6.
questions.answer: Prepared by condensation of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid; strong fibres used in textiles.

questions.text: Explain preparation of polythene by free radical polymerization.
questions.answer: Ethylene polymerizes under high pressure using peroxide initiator.

questions.text: Which of the following is a natural polymer?
questions.answer: Cellulose

questions.text: The polymer obtained from ethene is:
questions.answer: Polythene

questions.text: Define polymer.
questions.answer: Polymer is a high molecular mass compound formed by repetition of small units called monomers.

questions.text: What is monomer?
questions.answer: Monomer is a small molecule that combines repeatedly to form a polymer.

questions.text: Explain addition polymerisation.
questions.answer: Addition polymerisation involves successive addition of monomers without elimination of small molecules.

questions.text: Explain condensation polymerisation.
questions.answer: Condensation polymerisation involves elimination of small molecules like water or HCl during polymer formation.

questions.text: What are thermoplastics?
questions.answer: Thermoplastics are polymers that soften on heating and harden on cooling repeatedly.

questions.text: What are thermosetting polymers?
questions.answer: Thermosetting polymers are polymers that become permanently hard on heating.

questions.text: Explain preparation, properties and uses of nylon-6,6.
questions.answer: Nylon-6,6 is prepared by condensation of hexamethylene diamine and adipic acid and is used in fibres and ropes.

questions.text: Explain preparation and uses of Bakelite.
questions.answer: Bakelite is prepared by condensation of phenol and formaldehyde and is used in electrical switches.

questions.text: Polythene is an addition polymer.
questions.answer: Because it is formed by addition of ethene monomers without elimination of small molecules.

questions.text: Thermosetting plastics cannot be recycled.
questions.answer: Because they have cross-linked structure and cannot be remoulded on heating.

chapters.title: Green Chemistry and Nanochemistry
chapters.description: Principles of green chemistry, sustainable development, introduction to nanoscience and nanomaterials, methods of synthesis and applications.
topics: Concept and Need of Green Chemistry
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and importance of green chemistry.
State and illustrate twelve principles of green chemistry.
Describe atom economy and its calculation.
Explain basic methods for synthesis of nanomaterials.
Discuss unique properties and applications of nanomaterials with awareness of safety aspects.

questions.text: Green chemistry aims primarily at:
options: Minimizing use and generation of hazardous substances
questions.answer: Minimizing use and generation of hazardous substances

questions.text: What is atom economy?
questions.answer: Atom economy is the percentage of reactant atoms that are incorporated into the desired product; it is calculated as (molar mass of desired product / sum of molar masses of all reactants) × 100.

questions.text: Name any two green solvents.
questions.answer: Water, supercritical CO₂, ionic liquids (any two).

questions.text: Which of the following is a bottom-up approach in nanomaterial synthesis?
questions.answer: Sol–gel method

questions.text: Write any four principles of green chemistry and explain them briefly.
questions.answer: Examples: (i) Prevention: better to prevent waste than treat it. (ii) Atom economy: design processes maximizing incorporation of materials into product. (iii) Use of safer solvents and auxiliaries. (iv) Energy efficiency: conduct reactions at ambient temperature and pressure when possible.

questions.text: What are nanomaterials? Give typical size range.
questions.answer: Materials with at least one dimension in the nanometer range, typically 1–100 nm, are called nanomaterials.

questions.text: Unique properties of nanomaterials are mainly due to:

questions.question: Read the extract and complete the activities given below:
questions.passageText: Punctually at midday he opened his bag and spread out his professional equipment, which consisted of a dozen cowrie shells, a square piece of cloth with obscure mystic charts on it, a notebook, and a bundle of Palmyra writing. His forehead was resplendent (glorious) with sacred ash and vermilion, and his eyes sparkled with a sharp abnormal gleam (shine) which was really an outcome of a continual searching look for customers, but which his simple clients took to be a prophetic light and felt comforted. The power of his eyes was considerably enhanced by their position placed as they were between the painted forehead and the dark whiskers (mustaches) which streamed down his cheeks: even a half-wit's eyes would sparkle in such a setting. To crown the effect he wound a saffron-coloured turban around his head. This colour scheme never failed. People were attracted to him as bees are attracted to cosmos or dahlia stalks. He sat under the boughs of a spreading tamarind tree which flanked a path running through the Town Hall Park. It was a remarkable place in many ways. A surging crowd was always moving up and down this narrow road from morning till night. A variety of trades and occupations was represented all along its way : medicine sellers, sellers of stolen hardware and junk, magicians, and above all, an auctioneer of cheap cloth, who created enough din all day to attract the whole town. Next to him in vociferousness came a vendor of fried groundnut, who gave his ware a fancy name each day, calling it “Bombay Ice Cream” one day and on the next “Delhi Almond,” and on the third “Raja's Delicacy,” and so on and so forth, and people flocked to him. A considerable portion of this crowd dallied before the astrologer too. The astrologer transacted his business by the light of a flare which crackled and smoked up above the groundnut heap nearby. Half the enchantment of the place was due to the fact that it did not have the benefit of municipal lighting. The place was lit up by shop lights. One or two had hissing gaslights, some had naked flares stuck on poles, some were lit up by old cycle lamps, and one or two, like the astrologer, managed without lights of their own. It was a bewildering crisscross of light rays and moving shadows. This suited the astrologer very well, for the simple reason that he had not in the least intended to be an astrologer when he began life; and he knew no more of what was going to happen to others than he knew what was going to happen to himself next minute. He was as much a stranger to the stars as were his innocent customers. Yet he said things which pleased and astonished everyone: that was more a matter of study, practice, and shrewd guesswork. All the same, it was as much an honest man's labour as any other, and he deserved the wages he carried home at the end of a day.

questions.question: Read the extract and complete the activities given below:
questions.passageText: The young lift-man in a City office who threw a passenger out of his lift the other morning and was fined for the offence was undoubtedly in the wrong. It was a question of “Please.” The complainant entering the lift, said, “Top.” The lift-man demanded “Top-please,” and this concession being refused he not only declined to comply with the instruction, but hurled the passenger out of the lift. This, of course was carrying a comment on manner too far. Discourtesy is not a legal offence, and it does not excuse assault and battery. If a burglar breaks into my house and I knock him down, the law will acquit me, and if I am physically assaulted, it will permit me to retaliate with reasonable violence. It does this because the burglar and my assailant have broken quite definite commands of the law. But no legal system could attempt to legislate against bad manners or could sanction the use of violence against something which it does not itself recognize as a legally punishable offence. And our sympathy with the liftman, we must admit that the law is reasonable. It would never do if we were at liberty to box people's ears because we did not like their behaviour, or the tone of their voices, or the scowl on their faces. Our fists would never be idle, and the gutters of the city would run with blood all day. I may be as uncivil as I may please and the law will protect me against violent retaliation. I may be haughty or boorish and there is no penalty to pay except the penalty of being written down an ill mannered fellow. The law does not compel me to say “Please” or to attune my voice to other people's sensibilities any more than it says that I shall not wax my moustache or dye my hair or wear ringlets down my back. It does not recognize the laceration of our feelings as a case for compensation. There is no allowance for moral and intellectual damages in these matters.

questions.passageText: Soapy left his bench and strolled out of the square and across the level sea of asphalt, where Broadway and Fifth Avenue flow together. Up Broadway he turned, and stopped at a luxurious cafe. Soapy had confidence in himself from the lowest button of his vest upward. He was shaven, and his coat was trim and his neat, black bow had been presented to him by a lady missionary on Thanksgiving Day. If only he could reach a table in the restaurant unsuspected, success would be his. The portion of him that would show above the table would raise no doubt in the waiter's mind. A roasted mallard duck, thought Soapy, would be about the thing with a bottle of wine and then some cheese, a cup of coffee and a cigar. One dollar for the cigar would be enough. The total would not be so high as to call forth any extreme of revenge from the cafe management; and yet the meat would leave him filled and happy for the journey to his winter island. But as Soapy set foot inside the restaurant door, the head-waiter's eye fell upon his tattered trousers and decadent shoes. Strong and ready hands turned him about and conveyed him in silence and haste to the side-walk and averted the ignoble fate of the menaced mallard. Soapy turned off Broadway. It seemed that his route to the coveted island was not to be an easy one. Some other way of entering the limbo must be devised. At a corner of Sixth Avenue electric lights and cunningly displayed wares behind plate glass made a shop window attractive. Soapy took a stone and dashed it through the glass. People came running round the corner, a policeman in the lead. Soapy stood still with his hands in his pockets, and smiled at the sight of brass buttons. “Where's the man that done that?” inquired the officer agitatedly. “Don't you think that I might have had something to do with it?” said Soapy, with a friendly voice, as one greets good fortune. The policeman refused to accept Soapy even as a clue. Men who smash windows do not remain to chat with the police. They take to their heels. The policeman saw a man half-way down the block running to catch a car. With drawn club he joined in the pursuit. Soapy, with disgust in his heart, drifted along, twice unsuccessful.

questions.passageText:
So a huge amount of data is collected. Let me give you an idea of how huge the data might be. Big Data can be petabytes or exabytes of data consisting of billions to trillions of records of millions of people- all from different sources, for example web, sales, customer contact centre, social media, mobile data and so on. The data available to industries and companies is enormously increasing in volume, variation, velocity, veracity and value. Such a Big Data is easy to obtain but so massive that it challenges the current computing technologies and hence Big Data analytics is used to give insights that were previously incomprehensible. Big Data analytics is the complex process of examining large and varied data sets or Big Data to uncover information- such as hidden patterns, unknown correlations, market trends and customer preferences. With such a huge data available with the industries they can have innumerable advantages hence all the industries are trying to reap the maximum 5 benefit from it. Many industries have advanced by miles from their competitors. It's not the amount of data that is important but what the organizations do with the data is what matters. 
Uses of Big Data 
1. Location Tracking: Big Data has been useful in identifying and tracking the exact location of a place. Your GPS and Google Maps make use of Big Data. With geographic positioning and radio frequency identification sensors we get the real-time data about traffic, congestion on a particular route, information if the route is closed or if it is a one-way route, understanding accident prone areas etc. You can plan your own route according to the travel time and the transportation of goods. If you have ordered something online you can track the location of your goods in transit, you can also track the condition of the goods. This has immensely helped the logistics companies to reduce risks in transport, improve speed and reliability in delivery.

questions.passageText:
The eight-and-a-half-hour-long day inside the hide was a fruitful as the Jambha tree standing tall on the edge of Umbarzara. Before wrapping up my day at this natural waterhole, I took entries of the avifauna in my field work. Since I was alone, I rushed to Pitezari village where I was stationed. I camouflaged the hide, took my essentials, and came out of the hide and stretched out to my heart's content. I lifted my camera bag and took the familiar trial to Pitezari. Negotiating the webbed leaves of Teakwood and Moha trees, trying to make minimal sound, I was treading cautiously among the wood. Walking alone in a jungle needs more alertness than walking with a companion. I was alone here like a fox. Following the trial silently, watching with wide-open eyes, my ears were grasping a variety of sound stunned me... 
'Khyak! Khyak! KhyakoSS Khyak!' 
It was a Langur alarm call. The leader of the gang of Langurs was sitting on the tall tree making alarm calls out of fear. Rest of the Langur brigade continued raising the alarm calls. The network of alarm calls was expanding its range as the petrified Langurs speeded to the trees near and far and secured their places on treetops. All this upheaval was created by only one animal's presence- a Leopard. Many animals make alarm calls when they see a predator- Tiger or a Leopard nearby. The Langur is more reliable when it comes to finding clues about the presence of the apex predators in the jungle. The mighty elusive Leopard of Umbarzara was out of his liar. He was on the prowl. The stealthily moving figure in spotted gold- black cloak was spied by these Langurs. Even the small ones from the legion of Langurs were giving alarm calls. 
'Chyak! Chyak!' 
I stayed put. Gauged the leader Langur's target sight and scanned the area visually. Took some steps. Stopped again. A fresh scat was lying before me on the trail. The bluish-purple flies were hovering over it. I was sure that the Leopard was somewhere near. The distant alarm call of four-horned antelope was adding to the chaos.

questions.passageText:
I scored 100% marks in Mathematics in almost all the examinations that I appeared for from my 1st standard until IIT, barring only a few times. I stood 16th in the SSC Board (at that time, this examination was for the whole of Maharashtra, including Nagpur) and I stood 1st in the University in all subjects put together. Those days, you could get an admission into IIT without the entrance test (JEE) if you had secured the 1st rank in the University. Therefore, I did not have to appear for the entrance test to get the admission into IIT, but nobody in Solapur told me about it, for I doubt if anybody in Solapur even knew about this rule. Therefore, I appeared for the entrance examination, and I secured a very good rank in the same. I was quite happy getting into IIT, but my joy was short lived. At Solapur I had not seen any building which was more than three storeyed. Mumbai however was full of skyscrapers. At IIT, most of the students and professors used to converse in English whereas my English was very poor. I had my entire education in Marathi. My spoken English was quite pathetic. Not only did I have a very weak vocabulary, but, my pronunciation also was terrible and my construction of English sentences very awkward to say the least. Due to all this, I was feeling quite lonely and terrified in Mumbai in general and IIT in particular. I had developed an inferiority complex and wanted to run away from IIT and even Mumbai. 
One day, I was sitting at my mess table in the hostel sipping tea when a senior guy came and sat on the chair adjacent to me. He was a convent educated guy with fairly sophisticated English- at least spoken or colloquial English. He was a bit arrogant and wanted to pull my leg. He tried to engage in some conversation with me and started pointing out errors in just about every sentence or everything that I said. After about 5 minutes he walked away after insulting me. 
I felt extremely humiliated and upset. As it is, I was feeling quite depressed and diffident and this incident was the last straw. I was almost broken. I felt out of place there and literally wanted to run away to Solapur that very moment. However, it was only my self-esteem which stopped me. Suddenly, a feeling of determination and strength came over me and gripped me. Despite hailing from Solapur, if I could be a rank holder in the school, college and IIT with many awards in Mathematics, there must be something right with me. Why should I give up? And that too for a silly and small thing like English? I was not to give up anymore, and I was determined to fight back.

Theme: The poem highlights loneliness, emotional alienation, and the struggles of a middle-class working father.
Poetic devices: Simile, imagery, metaphor and symbolism are effectively used. For example, 'like a word dropped from a long sentence' is a striking simile.
Special features: Realistic urban imagery, free verse form, and deep emotional appeal make the poem powerful.
Opinion: The poem sensitively presents the silent suffering of a father and evokes empathy in the reader.
