CSS selectors, positioning, float and display
Basics of website hosting and domain
learningObjectives: Use advanced HTML5 input types for user-friendly forms.
Apply validation-related attributes like required, pattern, min and max.
Use meta tags to describe a web page for search engines and browsers.
Design consistent layouts using CSS selectors, positioning and float.
Embed audio, video, image maps and iframes in web pages.
Explain the basic process of hosting a website with a custom domain.

questions.text: Which HTML5 input type is most suitable for selecting a value between 0 and 100 using a slider?
questions.answer: range

questions.text: Write any two HTML5 input types that help in validating contact details and explain their use in one line each.
questions.answer: Examples: type="email" for validating e-mail address format; type="tel" for entering a telephone number, often with a pattern attribute.

questions.text: Which attribute of the <input> tag forces the user to fill a value before submitting the form?
questions.answer: required

questions.text: What is the purpose of the placeholder attribute in an input element? Give one example.
questions.answer: placeholder displays a light, temporary hint inside the input field to show what the user should enter. Example: <input type="text" placeholder="Enter your full name">.

questions.text: Differentiate between inline CSS and external CSS (two points).
questions.answer: Inline CSS: written inside the style attribute of an HTML tag, affects only that element and mixes style with structure. External CSS: written in a separate .css file linked using <link>, can style many pages and keeps content and style separate.

questions.text: Explain the four CSS position values: static, relative, absolute and fixed with a suitable use case for each.
questions.answer: Static: default flow, element positioned as normal; used for most text blocks. Relative: element is shifted relative to its normal position using top/left etc., useful for small adjustments. Absolute: element is removed from normal flow and positioned relative to the nearest positioned ancestor or page; used for tooltips or badges. Fixed: element is positioned relative to the browser window and does not move while scrolling; used for sticky headers or floating buttons.

questions.text: Which HTML5 tag is used to embed video with native controls?
questions.answer: <video>

questions.text: What is an image map? Name the two main tags used to create a client-side image map in HTML5.
questions.answer: An image map is an image with different clickable areas (hotspots), each linking to a different URL. It mainly uses and tags together with .

questions.text: Describe the basic steps involved in hosting a small website for free using a service like 000webhost and a free domain provider.
questions.answer: Steps: (1) Sign up on a free hosting site such as 000webhost and create a new site, which allocates free web space and a temporary subdomain. (2) Upload all website files (HTML, CSS, images, etc.) via file manager, ensuring the home page is named index.html. (3) Register a free domain (e.g., .tk or .ml) from a provider like Freenom. (4) Park the domain on the hosting account and update nameservers at the domain provider to point to the hosting provider (e.g., ns01.000webhost.com, ns02.000webhost.com). (5) Wait for DNS propagation and then access the site using the custom domain.

questions.text: Write HTML5 code to embed an audio file named "intro.mp3" with controls.
questions.answer:
Example: <audio controls>
  <source src="intro.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
  Your browser does not support the audio element.
</audio>

chapters.title: Introduction to SEO (Search Engine Optimization)
chapters.description: Basics of search engines and SEO, on-page and off-page SEO, white-hat and black-hat techniques, page-structure optimisation and best practices for titles, meta descriptions, headings, images and URLs.
topics: Page structure and HTML best practices
Title, meta description and heading tags
Alt text for images and semantic HTML
Basic link building and social bookmarking
Role of keywords and content quality
learningObjectives: Define SEO and explain why websites need optimisation.
Differentiate between on-page SEO and off-page SEO.
Identify white-hat and black-hat SEO practices with examples.
Apply basic on-page SEO elements such as title, meta description and headings.
Explain the importance of meaningful URLs, internal linking and alt attributes.

questions.text: SEO mainly helps a website to:
options: Improve ranking in search engine results
questions.answer: Improve ranking in search engine results

questions.text: What is meant by On-Page SEO? Give two examples of On-Page factors.
questions.answer: On-Page SEO refers to optimisation techniques applied directly on the website pages. Examples: optimising title tags and meta descriptions, using proper heading tags, improving page content and keyword placement, adding alt attributes to images.

questions.text: Define Off-Page SEO and mention any two common Off-Page activities.
questions.answer: Off-Page SEO includes optimisation activities performed outside the website to improve its authority and popularity, such as link building and social bookmarking. Common activities: getting backlinks from other relevant websites, directory submissions, social media sharing.

questions.text: Which of the following is a White-Hat SEO technique?
options: Showing different content to search engines and users (cloaking)
questions.answer: Creating high-quality, original content

questions.text: Using invisible text stuffed with keywords on a page is an example of:
questions.answer: Black-Hat SEO

questions.text: What is a meta description? State the recommended length range for it.
questions.answer: A meta description is a short summary of a web page's content, placed in a <meta name="description"> tag and often shown in search results under the title. It is usually recommended to keep it between about 70 and 160 characters including spaces.

questions.text: Explain how the following elements affect SEO: (i) Title tag, (ii) Heading tags, (iii) Alt attribute of images.
questions.answer: Title tag: Appears as the clickable headline in search results; including main keywords and a clear description helps both ranking and click-through rate. Heading tags (H1–H6): Provide structure to the content; search engines use them to understand page hierarchy and important topics. Alt attribute: Describes images in text form; improves accessibility and helps search engines understand image content, contributing to relevancy for certain keywords.

questions.text: What is keyword stuffing and why should it be avoided?
questions.answer: Keyword stuffing is the practice of excessively repeating keywords in content, meta tags or alt texts only to manipulate search rankings. It should be avoided because it reduces readability, violates search engine guidelines and can lead to penalties or lower ranking.

questions.text: A meta description currently has 210 characters including spaces. If the recommended maximum is 160 characters, by how many characters must it be reduced?
questions.answer: It must be reduced by 210 − 160 = 50 characters.

questions.text: List any five good practices to follow while optimising a page structure for SEO.
questions.answer: Good practices: (1) Use <!doctype html> and valid semantic HTML. (2) Provide a unique, descriptive title tag for each page. (3) Write a concise, meaningful meta description. (4) Use heading tags in order (H1, H2, etc.) to structure content. (5) Provide alt attributes for images. (6) Use clean, human-readable URLs. (7) Avoid duplicate content and ensure fast loading pages.

chapters.title: Advanced JavaScript
chapters.description: Looping constructs, arrays, functions, events and DOM manipulation in JavaScript for creating interactive and dynamic web pages.
learningObjectives: Use different loop structures to perform repetitive tasks.
Declare and manipulate one-dimensional arrays in JavaScript.
Write and call functions with parameters and return values.
Use events to interact with user actions like click and keypress.
Access and modify HTML elements through the DOM for validation.

questions.text: Which JavaScript loop will always execute its body at least once?
questions.answer: do-while

questions.text: Write the syntax of a for loop in JavaScript.
questions.answer: Basic syntax: for (initialisation; condition; increment/decrement) { // statements }

questions.text: What is an array in JavaScript? Write a statement to declare an array of 3 city names.
questions.answer: An array is a special variable that can hold multiple values under a single name, accessed by index. Example: var cities = ["Mumbai", "Pune", "Nagpur"];

questions.text: Which method is used to add a new element at the end of a JavaScript array?
questions.answer: push()

questions.text: Define a function in JavaScript named sum that takes two parameters a and b and returns their addition.
questions.answer: Example: function sum(a, b) { return a + b; }

questions.text: Write a JavaScript program using a loop to display the multiplication table of 7 from 7 × 1 to 7 × 10 in the browser window.
What is the purpose of the document.getElementById() method? Give one example.
questions.answer: It returns the HTML element whose id attribute matches the given string, allowing us to read or change its properties. Example: document.getElementById("msg").innerHTML = "Welcome";

questions.text: Which event is triggered when a user clicks a button?
questions.answer: onclick

questions.text: Write JavaScript code to validate that a text box with id="age" contains a value between 18 and 60. If it is invalid, show an alert message.
Differentiate between break and continue statements used inside loops.
questions.answer: break immediately terminates the loop and control moves to the statement after the loop. continue skips the remaining statements in the current iteration and moves to the next iteration of the loop.

chapters.title: Emerging Technologies (IoT, Cloud Computing, AI, 5G)
chapters.description: Overview of modern and emerging technologies including Internet of Things (IoT), Cloud Computing, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and 5G networks, with applications and benefits.
topics: Basics of Artificial Intelligence and examples
5G features and advantages over previous generations
Applications of IoT, Cloud, AI and 5G in daily life
learningObjectives: Explain the concept of IoT with suitable examples.
Differentiate between IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.
Describe how AI is used in common applications.
State key features and benefits of 5G networks.
Discuss advantages and challenges of emerging technologies.

questions.text: IoT stands for:
questions.answer: Internet of Things

questions.text: Give any two examples of IoT devices used in daily life.
questions.answer: Examples: smart lights controllable via mobile app, smart thermostat, fitness band, internet-connected CCTV camera, smart refrigerator.

questions.text: Define cloud computing in one or two lines.
questions.answer: Cloud computing is a model of delivering computing resources such as servers, storage, databases and software over the internet on demand, often on a pay-as-you-go basis.

questions.text: Which cloud service model provides only virtualised hardware resources such as servers and storage?
questions.answer: IaaS

questions.text: Differentiate between public cloud and private cloud.
questions.answer: Public cloud is owned by a third-party provider and shared among many customers over the internet; it is cost-effective and scalable. Private cloud is dedicated to a single organisation, offering more control and security but at higher cost.

questions.text: What is Artificial Intelligence? Mention one real-life application.
questions.answer: Artificial Intelligence is the ability of machines or software to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence such as learning, reasoning or decision-making. Example: voice assistants like Siri/Alexa, recommendation systems on shopping sites, or spam filters in email.

questions.text: Which of the following is a key feature of 5G networks?
options: Massive device connectivity and high speed
questions.answer: Massive device connectivity and high speed

questions.text: Explain any three advantages of using cloud computing for a small business.
questions.answer: Advantages: (1) Cost saving – no need to buy and maintain expensive hardware; pay as per usage. (2) Scalability – resources can be increased or decreased quickly as demand changes. (3) Accessibility – employees can access applications and data from anywhere via the internet. (4) Automatic updates and backup managed by provider, reducing maintenance work.

questions.text: Mention any two security or privacy concerns related to IoT.
questions.answer: Examples: weakly protected devices can be hacked, leading to misuse of cameras or sensors; collection of large amounts of personal data about users' habits; risk of unauthorised remote control of devices.

questions.text: How can AI and IoT together improve healthcare? Explain with any three points.
questions.answer: AI and IoT can improve healthcare by: (1) Using wearable IoT devices that continuously monitor vital signs and send data to AI systems for early detection of anomalies. (2) Enabling remote patient monitoring, where AI analyses data and alerts doctors if intervention is needed. (3) Helping in hospital management with smart beds and equipment tracking, while AI predicts patient inflow and optimises resource usage.

chapters.title: Server-Side Scripting (PHP)
chapters.description: Basics of server-side scripting using PHP, including syntax, variables, operators, control structures, forms handling and simple database connectivity concepts.
topics: Introduction to PHP and its features
Concept of connecting PHP with a database (overview)
learningObjectives: Differentiate between client-side and server-side scripting.
Write basic PHP scripts using variables and operators.
Use conditional statements and loops in PHP.
Collect and process form data using PHP.
Explain at a basic level how PHP connects to a database.

questions.text: PHP code is executed:
options: On the server before sending HTML to the client
questions.answer: On the server before sending HTML to the client

questions.text: Write the PHP opening and closing tags.
questions.answer: Opening tag: <?php  Closing tag: ?>

questions.text: Write a PHP statement to store value 10 in a variable x and display it using echo.
questions.answer: Example: <?php $x = 10; echo $x; ?>

questions.text: Which superglobal array is used to collect form data sent with the HTTP POST method?
questions.answer: $_POST

questions.text: Differentiate between client-side scripting and server-side scripting with one example each.
questions.answer: Client-side scripting runs in the user's browser, mainly used for validation and interactivity; example: JavaScript form validation. Server-side scripting runs on the web server and generates dynamic pages; example: PHP script that fetches data from a database and displays it.

questions.text: Write a PHP script that accepts two numbers from a form (fields: num1 and num2, method="post") and displays their sum.

questions.answer: Output will be 25 because the ** operator is exponentiation, so 5 squared is 25.

questions.text: Which function is commonly used in PHP to connect to a MySQL database (procedural style)?
questions.answer: mysqli_connect()

(i) mysqli_connect(...) establishes a connection to the MySQL server running on localhost using username 'root', empty password and selects database 'school'. (ii) mysqli_query($con, $sql) sends the SQL query stored in $sql to the server using the connection $con and stores the result (e.g., rows selected). (iii) mysqli_close($con) closes the database connection and frees server resources.

questions.text: Why is server-side validation necessary even if client-side validation is implemented using JavaScript?
questions.answer: Because client-side validation can be bypassed or disabled by users; server-side validation ensures data is checked on the server before processing or storing it, which protects security and data integrity.

chapters.title: E-Commerce and E-Governance
chapters.description: Concepts, types and benefits of e-commerce and e-governance, including online payment methods, security concerns and major Indian initiatives.
topics: Types of e-commerce (B2B, B2C, C2C, etc.)
Online payment methods (cards, net banking, wallets, UPI)
Types of e-governance interactions (G2C, G2B, G2G)
Examples of e-governance services in India
learningObjectives: Define e-commerce and describe its main types.
Explain common online payment methods and their benefits.
Discuss security and privacy issues in e-transactions.
Define e-governance and describe its objectives.
List important examples of e-governance services in India.

questions.text: Buying a mobile phone from an online shopping website like Amazon is an example of:
questions.answer: B2C

questions.text: What is e-commerce?
questions.answer: E-commerce (electronic commerce) is the buying and selling of goods and services and the transfer of money or data over electronic networks like the internet.

questions.text: State any two advantages of e-commerce for customers.
questions.answer: Advantages: ability to shop 24×7 from anywhere; wider choice of products and price comparison; home delivery and time saving; access to user reviews.

questions.text: Which of the following is a popular real-time payment system widely used in India for e-commerce and person-to-person transfers?
questions.answer: UPI

questions.text: Name any two security measures that websites use to protect online transactions.
questions.answer: Examples: HTTPS (SSL/TLS encryption) to secure communication; strong authentication methods like OTP; use of secure payment gateways; two-factor authentication.

questions.text: Explain B2B and C2C types of e-commerce with suitable examples.
questions.answer: B2B (Business-to-Business): electronic transactions between businesses, such as a manufacturer selling components online to another company; example: a company ordering raw material through an online supplier portal. C2C (Consumer-to-Consumer): transactions between individual consumers, usually via a third-party platform; example: a person selling a second-hand mobile phone on OLX or a similar marketplace.

questions.text: E-Governance mainly aims to:
options: Use computers only in private companies
Deliver government services to citizens using ICT
questions.answer: Deliver government services to citizens using ICT

questions.text: What do you mean by G2C in e-governance? Give one example.
questions.answer: G2C (Government-to-Citizen) refers to electronic interactions where the government provides services or information directly to citizens, such as online payment of electricity bills or applying for a PAN/Aadhaar card through a portal.

questions.text: Discuss any three benefits of e-governance for citizens and government.
questions.answer: Benefits: (1) Increased transparency as information and processes are visible online, reducing corruption. (2) Convenience and time saving for citizens who can access services 24×7 without visiting offices. (3) Faster processing and better record keeping for government departments. (4) Reduced paperwork and cost, and improved communication between departments.

questions.text: Mention any two risks or challenges associated with e-commerce.
questions.answer: Examples: risk of online fraud and misuse of card details; privacy issues due to misuse of personal data; delivery delays or receiving wrong/damaged products; dependence on internet connectivity.

chapters.title: Mathematical Logic
chapters.description: Statements, truth values, logical connectives, truth tables, statement patterns, tautology, contradiction, contingency, quantifiers, duals, negation of compound statements, converse, inverse, contrapositive and applications to switching circuits.
learningObjectives: Identify logical statements and determine their truth values.
Use logical connectives to form compound statements and build truth tables.
Classify statement patterns as tautology, contradiction or contingency.
Work with quantifiers, duals and negations of compound statements.
Interpret and design simple switching circuits using logic.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a statement in the sense of mathematical logic?
options: The Earth revolves around the Sun.

questions.text: Define a simple statement and a compound statement with one example of each.
questions.answer: A simple statement cannot be broken into smaller statements, e.g. "$5$ is odd". A compound statement is formed by combining two or more simple statements using logical connectives, e.g. "$5$ is odd $\land$ $6$ is even".

questions.text: The connective in the compound statement "$p \lor q$" is represented symbolically by:
questions.answer: $\lor$

questions.text: Write the truth table for the disjunction $p \lor q$.
questions.answer:
Truth table:
$p$ $q$ | $p \lor q$
T T | T
T F | T
F T | T
F F | F

questions.text: Construct the truth table for $(\sim\!p \land q) \to p$.
questions.answer:
Truth table:
$p$ $q$ | $\sim\!p$ | $\sim\!p \land q$ | $(\sim\!p \land q) 	o p$
T T | F | F | T
T F | F | F | T
F T | T | T | F
F F | T | F | T

questions.text: State whether the statement pattern $p \lor \sim\!p$ is a tautology, contradiction or contingency.
questions.answer: $p \lor \sim\!p$ is a tautology because it is true for all truth values of $p$.

questions.text: Write the converse and contrapositive of: "If $n$ is even then $n^2$ is even".
questions.answer: Converse: If $n^2$ is even then $n$ is even. Contrapositive: If $n^2$ is not even then $n$ is not even.

questions.text: Write the dual of the statement pattern $(p \land q) \lor r$.
questions.answer: The dual is $(p \lor q) \land r$.

questions.text: Negate the statement: "All real numbers are rational" using quantifiers.
questions.answer: Negation: $\exists x \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $x$ is not rational.

questions.text: Two switches $S_1$ and $S_2$ are connected in series to glow a lamp $L$. Represent this as a logical expression and write the switching table.
questions.answer:
Let $p$: $S_1$ is ON, $q$: $S_2$ is ON. Logical expression: $p \land q$.
Truth table:
$p$ $q$ | $p \land q$
1 1 | 1
1 0 | 0
0 1 | 0
0 0 | 0

questions.text: Which of the following is not a statement?
options: 2 is the only even prime number
questions.answer: Come here

questions.text: If $p$ is any statement then $(p \lor \sim\!p)$ is a:
questions.answer: Tautology

questions.text: If $p \to q$ then $(\sim\!q \to \sim\!p)$ is called:
questions.answer: Contrapositive

questions.text: A biconditional statement is the conjunction of two _____ statements.
questions.answer: Conditional

questions.text: The negation of $(p \land q) \to (r \lor \sim\!p)$ is:
questions.answer: $p \land q \land \sim\!r$

questions.text: The statement $p \land \sim\!p$ is:
questions.answer: Contradiction

questions.text: Which statement is always true?
questions.answer: $p \lor \sim\!p$

questions.text: The negation of $p \to q$ is:
questions.answer: $p \land \sim\!q$

questions.text: Which of the following is a contradiction?
questions.answer: $p \land \sim\!p$

questions.text: Find the negation of $10 + 20 = 30$.
State the truth value of: $\sqrt{3}$ is not an irrational number.
questions.answer: False

questions.text: Write the negation of $p \to q$.
questions.answer: $p \land \sim\!q$

questions.text: State the truth value of $(p \lor \sim\!p)$.
questions.answer: True

questions.text: State the truth value of $(p \land \sim\!p)$.
questions.answer: False

questions.text: Is $p \leftrightarrow p$ a tautology?
questions.answer: Yes

questions.text: If statements $p$ and $q$ are true and $r$ and $s$ are false, find the truth value of $\sim\!p \land (q \lor \sim\!r)$.
questions.answer: False

questions.text: Write the following compound statement symbolically: Nagpur is in Maharashtra and Chennai is in Tamil Nadu.
questions.answer: $p \land q$

questions.text: Write the converse of the statement: If a function is differentiable, then it is continuous.
questions.answer: If a function is continuous, then it is differentiable.

questions.text: Write the contrapositive of the statement: If a function is differentiable, then it is continuous.
questions.answer: If a function is not continuous, then it is not differentiable.

questions.text: Write the negation of the statement: An angle is a right angle if and only if it is of measure $90^\circ$.
questions.answer: An angle is a right angle and it is not of measure $90^\circ$, or an angle is not a right angle and it is of measure $90^\circ$.

questions.text: Write the following statement in symbolic form: Milk is white if and only if the sky is not blue.
questions.answer: $p \leftrightarrow \sim\!q$

questions.text: Write the following statement in symbolic form: If Qutub Minar is in Delhi then Taj Mahal is in Agra.
questions.answer: $p \to q$

questions.text: Write the following statement in symbolic form: Even though it is not cloudy, it is still raining.
questions.answer: $\sim\!p \land q$

questions.text: Examine whether the statement pattern $(p \land \sim\!q) \to (\sim\!p \land \sim\!q)$ is a tautology, contradiction or contingency.
questions.answer: Contingency

questions.text: Write the dual of the statement: 13 is a prime number and India is a democratic country.
questions.answer: 13 is a prime number or India is a democratic country.

questions.text: Using truth table, prove that $\sim\!p \land q \equiv (p \lor q) \land \sim\!p$.
questions.answer: Both expressions have identical truth values for all possible combinations of $p$ and $q$; hence they are logically equivalent.

questions.text: Examine whether the statement pattern $[p \to (\sim\!q \lor r)] \leftrightarrow \sim\!p \to (q \to r)]$ is a tautology, contradiction or contingency.
questions.answer: Contingency

questions.text: Using truth table prove that $p \lor (q \land r) \equiv (p \lor q) \land (p \lor r)$.
questions.answer: Both sides give identical truth values for all combinations of $p$, $q$, and $r$; hence they are equivalent.

questions.text: Without using truth table, show that $(p \lor q) \land (\sim\!p \lor \sim\!q) \equiv (p \lor \sim\!q) \land (\sim\!p \lor q)$.
questions.answer: Both expressions reduce to the same logical form using De Morgan's laws and distributive properties.

questions.text: Prepare a truth table for the statement $(p \land q) \lor \sim\!r$.
questions.answer: The truth table shows the statement is false only when $p$ and $q$ are false and $r$ is true; otherwise it is true.

questions.text: Which of the following statement is true?
options: If Pune is in Maharashtra, then Hyderabad is in Kerala
It is false that $12$ is not divisible by $3$
The square of any odd integer is even
questions.answer: It is false that $12$ is not divisible by $3$

questions.text: Which of the following statements is a compound statement?
questions.answer: 2 is prime and 3 is odd

questions.text: The negation of the statement “It is raining” is:
questions.answer: It is not raining

questions.text: If $p$ is true and $q$ is false, then $p \land q$ is:
questions.answer: False

questions.text: Define a statement.
questions.answer: A statement is a declarative sentence which is either true or false but not both.

questions.text: What is a simple statement?
questions.answer: A simple statement is a statement that cannot be broken into smaller statements.

questions.text: Write the negation of the statement: “All integers are rational numbers.”
questions.answer: There exists at least one integer which is not a rational number.

questions.text: Find the truth value of $p \lor q$, if $p$ is false and $q$ is true.
questions.answer: True

questions.text: Construct the truth table for $p \to q$.
questions.answer: The implication $p \to q$ is false only when $p$ is true and $q$ is false; otherwise it is true.

questions.text: Verify De Morgan's law: $\sim\!p \land q) \equiv (\sim\!p \lor \sim\!q)$.
questions.answer: By constructing truth tables for both sides, the truth values are identical for all combinations of $p$ and $q$.

questions.text: Check whether the statement $p \leftrightarrow q$ is a tautology or not.
questions.answer: By constructing the truth table, $p \leftrightarrow q$ is true only when $p$ and $q$ have the same truth values; hence it is not a tautology.

chapters.title: Matrices
chapters.description: Types of matrices, equality and order, algebra of matrices, transpose, determinant of a square matrix, adjoint and inverse, and solution of system of linear equations using matrices.
topics: Row, column, zero, identity and diagonal matrices
Adjoint and inverse of a matrix
Solving linear equations using inverse matrix
learningObjectives: Identify different types of matrices and their orders.
Perform algebraic operations on matrices.
Find determinants and inverses of square matrices where possible.
Use matrices to solve small systems of linear equations.
Understand basic properties like associativity and non-commutativity of multiplication.

questions.text: If $A$ is a $2 \times 3$ matrix and $B$ is a $3 \times 4$ matrix, then the order of $AB$ is:
questions.answer: $2 \times 4$

questions.text: Define a square matrix and a diagonal matrix with one example each.
questions.answer: A square matrix has equal number of rows and columns, e.g. $\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\3 & 4\end{bmatrix}$. A diagonal matrix is a square matrix with all non-diagonal elements zero, e.g. $\begin{bmatrix}5 & 0\\0 & 7\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.text: If $A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\3 & 4\end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 0\\1 & 5\end{bmatrix}$, find $AB$.
questions.answer: $AB = \begin{bmatrix}4 & 10\\10 & 20\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.text: State whether matrix multiplication is commutative. Justify with a small example.
questions.answer: Matrix multiplication is not commutative, i.e. $AB \ne BA$. Example: $A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0\\0 & 0\end{bmatrix}$, $B=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1\\0 & 0\end{bmatrix}$, then $AB \ne BA$.

questions.text: Find the determinant of the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix}3 & 2\\5 & 4\end{bmatrix}$.
For $A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\3 & 4\end{bmatrix}$, find $\operatorname{adj}(A)$ and hence $A^{-1}$.
questions.answer: $|A|=-2$, $\operatorname{adj}(A)=\begin{bmatrix}4 & -3\\-2 & 1\end{bmatrix}$, so $A^{-1}=\frac{-1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}4 & -3\\-2 & 1\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.text: Write the system of equations $2x + 3y = 5$, $4x - y = 1$ in matrix form $AX = B$.
questions.answer: $A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3\\4 & -1\end{bmatrix}$, $X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}$, $B=\begin{bmatrix}5\\1\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.text: Solve the system $2x + 3y = 5$, $4x - y = 1$ using matrices.
questions.answer: Using inverse method, $x=\frac{4}{7}$ and $y=\frac{9}{7}$.

questions.text: What is the transpose of a matrix? Find $\left(\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 3\\0 & 4 & 5\end{bmatrix}\right)^T$.
questions.answer: Transpose is obtained by interchanging rows and columns. Result is $\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0\\-2 & 4\\3 & 5\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.text: If $A$ is a $3 \times 3$ matrix and $|A| = 0$, then which of the following is true?
options: A is singular and not invertible
questions.answer: A is singular and not invertible

questions.answer: Upper triangular matrix

questions.answer: Solved using matrix method

questions.answer: $2\times2$

questions.text: Which of the following matrices is symmetric?
Define a zero matrix.
questions.answer: A matrix in which all elements are zero is called a zero matrix.

questions.text: What is a square matrix?
questions.answer: A matrix having equal number of rows and columns is called a square matrix.

questions.text: Find the transpose of the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{bmatrix}$.
questions.answer: $A^{T}=\begin{bmatrix}1&3\\2&4\end{bmatrix}$

questions.text: Show that the sum of a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix is neither symmetric nor skew-symmetric in general.
questions.answer: Let $A$ be symmetric ($A^{T}=A$) and $B$ be skew-symmetric ($B^{T}=-B$). Then $(A+B)^{T}=A^{T}+B^{T}=A-B\neq A+B$ and $(A+B)^{T}\neq -(A+B)$. Hence the sum is neither symmetric nor skew-symmetric in general.

questions.text: If $A$ is a square matrix, show that $(A^{T})^{T}=A$.
questions.answer: Transpose of the transpose of a matrix gives the original matrix, hence $(A^{T})^{T}=A$.

questions.text: Find matrix $X$ if $A+X=B$, where $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}5&6\\7&8\end{bmatrix}$.
questions.answer: $X=B-A=\begin{bmatrix}4&4\\4&4\end{bmatrix}$

questions.text: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{bmatrix}$, find $A^{2}$.
questions.answer: $A^{2}=\begin{bmatrix}5&3\\3&2\end{bmatrix}$

questions.text: Prove that the product of two symmetric matrices need not be symmetric.
questions.answer: Take symmetric matrices $A$ and $B$ such that $AB\neq BA$. Then $(AB)^{T}=B^{T}A^{T}=BA\neq AB$. Hence the product of two symmetric matrices need not be symmetric.

chapters.title: Trigonometric Functions
chapters.description: Trigonometric equations and their solutions, principle and general solutions, solution of triangles using sine, cosine and projection rules, area of triangle, and basic properties of inverse trigonometric functions.

Area of triangle by trigonometric formulae

learningObjectives: Solve standard trigonometric equations for principal and general solutions.
Apply sine, cosine and projection rules to solve a triangle.
Use trigonometric formulae for the area of a triangle.
Understand basic definitions and ranges of inverse trigonometric functions.

questions.text: Solve the equation $\sin x = \frac{1}{2}$ for $0^{\circ} \le x < 360^{\circ}$.
questions.answer: $\sin x = \frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow x = 30^{\circ},\ 150^{\circ}$

questions.text: Find the general solution of $\cos x = 0$.
questions.answer: $\cos x = 0 \Rightarrow x = \frac{(2n+1)\pi}{2},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}$

questions.text: For a triangle $ABC$, the sine rule is:
questions.answer: $\dfrac{a}{\sin A} = \dfrac{b}{\sin B} = \dfrac{c}{\sin C}$

questions.text: In $\triangle ABC$, $a=7$ cm, $b=8$ cm and $\angle C = 120^{\circ}$. Find side $c$ using cosine rule.
questions.answer: $c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C = 49 + 64 - 112(-\tfrac{1}{2}) = 169 \Rightarrow c = 13\text{ cm}$

questions.text: The sides of a triangle are $5$ cm, $6$ cm and $7$ cm. Find its area using the formula $\tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$.
questions.answer: $\cos C = \tfrac{1}{5},\ \sin C = \tfrac{2\sqrt{6}}{5}$. Area $= \tfrac{1}{2} \cdot 5 \cdot 6 \cdot \tfrac{2\sqrt{6}}{5} = 6\sqrt{6}\text{ cm}^2$

questions.text: State the projection rule relating side $a$ and angles $B$ and $C$ of a triangle $ABC$.
questions.answer: Projection rule: $a = b\cos C + c\cos B$

questions.answer: Range of $\tan^{-1}x$ is $(-\tfrac{\pi}{2},\ \tfrac{\pi}{2})$

questions.text: If $\triangle ABC$ has sides $a=10$ cm, $b=12$ cm and included angle $C=45^{\circ}$, find its area.
questions.answer: Area $= \tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C = 60 \cdot \tfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = 30\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}^2$

questions.answer: Let $\sin x = t$. Then $(2t-1)(t-1)=0$. Hence $x=30^{\circ},\ 90^{\circ},\ 150^{\circ}$

chapters.title: Pair of Straight Lines
chapters.description: Combined equation of two lines, pair of lines passing through origin, angle between lines, condition for parallel and perpendicular lines, and general second degree equation representing pair of lines.
topics: Pair of lines through origin: ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0
Condition for lines to be perpendicular or coincident
General second degree equation and its homogeneous part
Point of intersection of two lines
learningObjectives: Write combined equation of a pair of straight lines in a plane.
Determine angle between lines and conditions for parallelism and perpendicularity.
Find point of intersection of two lines.
Identify when a second degree equation represents a pair of lines.

questions.text: The pair of lines represented by $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0$ are perpendicular if:
Find the combined equation of the pair of lines passing through the origin and making angles $30^\circ$ and $120^\circ$ with the positive $x$-axis.
questions.answer: Slopes are $m_1=\tan30^\circ=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$ and $m_2=\tan120^\circ=-\sqrt3$. Hence, $(y-\tfrac{x}{\sqrt3})(y+\sqrt3x)=0$ or equivalently $y^2-\tfrac{2}{\sqrt3}xy-x^2=0$.

questions.text: Find the point of intersection of the lines $2x+3y-5=0$ and $x-y+1=0$.
questions.answer: Solving simultaneously gives $x=\tfrac{2}{5},\;y=\tfrac{7}{5}$. Hence the point of intersection is $(\tfrac{2}{5},\tfrac{7}{5})$.

questions.text: Find the angle between the lines represented by $3x^2-10xy+3y^2=0$.
questions.answer: Here $a=3,\;2h=-10\Rightarrow h=-5,\;b=3$. Using $\tan\theta=\dfrac{2\sqrt{h^2-ab}}{a+b}$, we get $\tan\theta=\tfrac{4}{3}$. Hence $\theta=\tan^{-1}(\tfrac{4}{3})$.

questions.text: The general second degree equation $ax^2+2hxy+by^2+2gx+2fy+c=0$ represents a pair of straight lines if:
options: the homogeneous part represents a pair of straight lines
questions.answer: the homogeneous part represents a pair of straight lines

questions.text: Write the condition for $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$ to represent a pair of real and distinct straight lines.
questions.answer: The condition is $h^2>ab$.

questions.text: Resolve $6x^2-xy-y^2=0$ into two linear factors.
questions.answer: Comparing with $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$, we get $a=6,\;h=-\tfrac12,\;b=-1$. Slopes satisfy $6-hm-bm^2=0\Rightarrow m^2+m-6=0$. Hence $m=2,-3$. The lines are $y=2x$ and $y=-3x$. Therefore $(y-2x)(y+3x)=0$.

questions.text: Find the combined equation of the lines $x+y-2=0$ and $2x-3y+5=0$.
questions.answer: The combined equation is $(x+y-2)(2x-3y+5)=0$.

questions.text: If two non-vertical lines have slopes $m_1$ and $m_2$, they are perpendicular when:
Examine whether the lines represented by $x^2-4xy-5y^2=0$ are perpendicular.
questions.answer: Here $a=1,\;h=-2,\;b=-5$. Since $a+b\neq0$, the lines are not perpendicular. Solving for slopes gives $m=\tfrac15$ and $m=-1$, whose product is $-\tfrac15\neq-1$. Hence the lines are not perpendicular.

questions.text: The combined equation of two lines through the origin making angles $45^\circ$ and $135^\circ$ with the $x$-axis is:
The separate equations of the lines represented by $3x^2-2\sqrt3xy-3y^2=0$ are:
questions.answer: $x-\sqrt3y=0$ and $\sqrt3x+y=0$

questions.text: The equation $4x^2+4xy+y^2=0$ represents:
questions.answer: real and coincident lines

questions.text: If the lines represented by $kx^2-3xy+6y^2=0$ are perpendicular, then $k$ equals:
The condition for $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$ to represent perpendicular lines is:
The angle between the lines $x^2-y^2=0$ is:
questions.answer: $90^\circ$

questions.text: The equation representing coincident lines is:
The pair of lines represented by $x^2+y^2=0$ are:
questions.answer: Imaginary

questions.text: Write the general equation of a pair of lines passing through the origin.
State the condition for coincident lines represented by $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$.
State the condition for imaginary lines represented by $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$.
State the condition for real and distinct lines represented by $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$.
When are the pair of lines represented by $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$ perpendicular?
Find the angle between the lines represented by $x^2-5xy+y^2=0$.
questions.answer: Here $a=1,\;2h=-5\Rightarrow h=-\tfrac52,\;b=1$. Using $\tan\theta=\dfrac{2\sqrt{h^2-ab}}{a+b}$, we get $\tan\theta=\dfrac{3}{1}$. Hence $\theta=\tan^{-1}(3)$.

questions.text: Find the condition for $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$ to represent parallel lines.
questions.answer: For a pair of lines through the origin, parallel lines are coincident. Hence the condition is $h^2=ab$.

questions.text: Find the slopes of the lines represented by $x^2-y^2=0$.
questions.answer: Factorising, $(x-y)(x+y)=0$. Hence slopes are $m=1$ and $m=-1$.

questions.text: Show that $x^2+2xy+y^2=0$ represents coincident lines.
questions.answer: Here $a=1,\;h=1,\;b=1$. Since $h^2=ab$, the lines are coincident.

questions.text: Find the angle between the lines represented by $3x^2-10xy+3y^2=0$.
questions.answer: Here $a=3,\;h=-5,\;b=3$. Using $\tan\theta=\dfrac{2\sqrt{h^2-ab}}{a+b}$, we get $\tan\theta=\tfrac{4}{3}$. Hence $\theta=\tan^{-1}(\tfrac{4}{3})$.

questions.text: Find the pair of lines represented by $6x^2-7xy+2y^2=0$.
questions.answer: Comparing with $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$, we get $a=6,\;h=-\tfrac72,\;b=2$. Slopes satisfy $6-hm-bm^2=0\Rightarrow 2m^2+7m-12=0$. Hence $m=\tfrac32,-4$. The lines are $y=\tfrac32x$ and $y=-4x$.

questions.text: Find the angle between the lines represented by $x^2+4xy+y^2=0$.
questions.answer: Here $a=1,\;h=2,\;b=1$. Since $h^2>ab$, lines are real. Using $\tan\theta=\dfrac{2\sqrt{h^2-ab}}{a+b}$, we get $\tan\theta=\sqrt3$. Hence $\theta=60^\circ$.

questions.text: Find the condition for the pair of lines represented by $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$ to be perpendicular.
questions.answer: For the pair of lines $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$ to be perpendicular, the condition is $a+b=0$.

questions.text: Show that the equation $x^2+y^2+2x+2y=0$ represents imaginary lines.
questions.answer: Comparing with $ax^2+2hxy+by^2+2gx+2fy+c=0$, we have $a=1,\;h=0,\;b=1$. Since $h^2<ab$, the equation represents imaginary lines.

questions.text: Find the angle between the pair of lines represented by $2x^2-5xy+2y^2=0$.
questions.answer: Here $a=2,\;2h=-5\Rightarrow h=-\tfrac{5}{2},\;b=2$. Using $\tan\theta=\dfrac{2\sqrt{h^2-ab}}{a+b}$, we get $\tan\theta=\dfrac{3}{2}$. Hence the angle between the lines is $\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\tfrac{3}{2}\right)$.

questions.text: Find the pair of straight lines represented by $3x^2+10xy+3y^2=0$.
questions.answer: Comparing with $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$, we get $a=3,\;h=5,\;b=3$. Slopes satisfy $3+10m+3m^2=0\Rightarrow (m+3)(3m+1)=0$. Hence $m=-3$ and $m=-\tfrac{1}{3}$. The pair of lines are $y=-3x$ and $y=-\tfrac{1}{3}x$.

questions.text: Show that the pair of lines represented by $x^2-6xy+y^2=0$ are perpendicular.
questions.answer: Here $a=1,\;2h=-6\Rightarrow h=-3,\;b=1$. Since $a+b=2\neq0$, slopes are found from $1-6m+m^2=0\Rightarrow m=3,\;\tfrac{1}{3}$. Product of slopes is $1$, hence the lines are not perpendicular. (Thus, the given pair is NOT perpendicular.)

questions.text: Find the angle between the lines represented by $4x^2-4xy+y^2=0$.
questions.answer: Here $a=4,\;2h=-4\Rightarrow h=-2,\;b=1$. Using $\tan\theta=\dfrac{2\sqrt{h^2-ab}}{a+b}$, we get $\tan\theta=\dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{5}$. Hence the angle is $\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\tfrac{2\sqrt3}{5}\right)$.

questions.text: The general equation of a pair of straight lines passing through the origin is:
Find the angle between the pair of lines represented by $x^2-y^2=0$.
questions.answer: Factoring gives $(x-y)(x+y)=0$, i.e. $y=x$ and $y=-x$. These lines are perpendicular, so the angle is $90^\circ$.

questions.text: Prove that the equation $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$ represents two straight lines through the origin.
questions.answer: Rewriting as $b\left(y-m_1x\right)\left(y-m_2x\right)=0$, where $m_1,m_2$ are roots of $bm^2+2hm+a=0$, shows that the equation represents two straight lines through the origin.

chapters.title: Vectors

questions.text: Define scalar and vector with one example of each.
questions.answer: A scalar quantity has magnitude only, e.g. mass 5 kg. A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction, e.g. force 10 N acting east.

questions.text: If $\vec a = 3\hat i - 4\hat j$, find $|\vec a|$.
If $\vec a = 2\hat i + 3\hat j - \hat k$ and $\vec b = \hat i - 2\hat j + 4\hat k$, find $\vec a + \vec b$.
questions.answer: $\vec a + \vec b = (2+1)\hat i + (3-2)\hat j + (-1+4)\hat k = 3\hat i + \hat j + 3\hat k.$

questions.text: Find the dot product of $\vec a = 2\hat i - 3\hat j + \hat k$ and $\vec b = \hat i + 4\hat j - 2\hat k$ and hence find the angle between them.
questions.answer:
$\vec a\cdot\vec b = 2(1) + (-3)(4) + 1(-2) = -12.
|\vec a|=\sqrt{14},\ |\vec b|=\sqrt{21}.
\cos	heta = \dfrac{-12}{\sqrt{14}\sqrt{21}} = -\dfrac{12}{7\sqrt6}.
	heta = \cos^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{12}{7\sqrt6}ight).$

questions.text: If $\vec a = \hat i + 2\hat j$ and $\vec b = 3\hat i - 4\hat j$, find $|\vec a \times \vec b|$ and interpret it geometrically.
questions.answer: $\vec a \times \vec b = (1\cdot(-4) - 2\cdot3)\hat k = -10\hat k.\n|\vec a \times \vec b| = 10.$\nIt represents the area of the parallelogram formed by $\vec a$ and $\vec b$.

questions.text: Find the area of the triangle whose vertices have position vectors $\vec a$, $\vec b$, $\vec c$.
questions.answer: Area of triangle $= \dfrac12 |(\vec b - \vec a) \times (\vec c - \vec a)|.$

questions.text: Evaluate the scalar triple product $[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]$ for $\vec a = \hat i$, $\vec b = 2\hat j$, $\vec c = 3\hat k$ and interpret it.
questions.answer: $[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c] = \begin{vmatrix}1&0&0\\0&2&0\\0&0&3\end{vmatrix}=6.$\nIt represents the volume of the parallelepiped formed, hence volume = 6 cubic units.

questions.text: State the condition for vectors $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ to be perpendicular.
questions.answer: Vectors $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are perpendicular if $\vec a \cdot \vec b = 0$.

questions.text: Find the position vector of the point dividing the line joining A(1,2,3) and B(5,4,−1) internally in the ratio 1:3.
questions.answer: Using section formula: $\vec{OP} = \dfrac{3\vec{OA} + \vec{OB}}{4} = (2,\tfrac52,2).$

questions.text: If $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are parallel non-zero vectors, then $\vec a \times \vec b$ equals
questions.answer: Zero vector

$(\hat i + \hat j - \hat k) \cdot (\hat i - \hat j + \hat k) =$
The angle $\theta$ between two non-zero vectors $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ is given by
questions.answer: $\cos\theta=\dfrac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec a||\vec b|}$

questions.text: If the sum of two unit vectors is also a unit vector, then the magnitude of their difference is
questions.answer: $\sqrt3$

questions.text: If $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ are direction angles of a line and $\alpha=60^\circ,\ \beta=45^\circ$, then $\gamma$ equals
questions.answer: $30^\circ$

questions.answer: Unit vector along the line

questions.text: The value of $|c|$ that satisfies $|c\vec u| = 3$, where $\vec u = \hat i + 2\hat j + 3\hat k$, is
questions.answer: $\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{14}}$

questions.text: The value of $\hat i\cdot(\hat j\times\hat k) + \hat j\cdot(\hat i\times\hat k) + \hat k\cdot(\hat i\times\hat j)$ is
The vectors $\hat j + \hat k$ and $3\hat i - \hat j + 4\hat k$ are sides $AB$ and $AC$ of $\triangle ABC$. The length of the median through A is
questions.answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{34}}{2}$

questions.text: Find the magnitude of a vector with initial point (1, −3, 4) and terminal point (1, 0, −1).
Find the coordinates of the point which is three units behind the YZ-plane, four units to the right of the XZ-plane and five units above the XY-plane.
Check whether $\overrightarrow{CD}$ is parallel to $\overrightarrow{AB}$, where A(2,3), B(-1,5), C(-1,1), D(-7,5).
questions.answer: Yes, $\overrightarrow{CD} \parallel \overrightarrow{AB}$.

questions.text: Find a unit vector in the opposite direction of $\vec u$, where $\vec u = 8\hat i + 3\hat j - \hat k$.
questions.answer: $-\dfrac{8\hat i + 3\hat j - \hat k}{\sqrt{74}}$

questions.text: The non-zero vectors $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are not collinear. Find $\lambda$ and $\mu$ if $\vec a + 3\vec b = 2\lambda \vec a - \mu \vec b$.
questions.answer: $\lambda = \dfrac12, \ \mu = -3$

questions.text: If $\vec a = 4\hat i + 3\hat k$ and $\vec b = -2\hat i + \hat j + 5\hat k$, find $2\vec a + 5\vec b$.
questions.answer: $-2\hat i + 5\hat j + 31\hat k$

Find $\vec a \cdot (\vec b \times \vec c)$, if $\vec a = 3\hat i - \hat j + 4\hat k$, $\vec b = 2\hat i + 3\hat j - \hat k$, $\vec c = -5\hat i + 2\hat j + 3\hat k$.
If a line makes angles $90^\circ$, $60^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ with the positive directions of X, Y and Z axes respectively, find its direction cosines.
questions.answer: $(0, \tfrac12, \tfrac{\sqrt3}{2})$

questions.text: The vector $\vec a$ is directed due north and $|\vec a| = 24$. The vector $\vec b$ is directed due west and $|\vec b| = 7$. Find $|\vec a + \vec b|$.
Show that the points P(4,5,2), Q(3,2,4) and R(5,8,0) are collinear.
questions.answer: Vectors $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ and $\overrightarrow{PR}$ are proportional, hence the points are collinear.

questions.text: If a vector has direction angles $45^\circ$ and $60^\circ$, find the third direction angle.
questions.answer: $45^\circ$ or $135^\circ$

questions.text: If $\vec c = 3\vec a - 2\vec b$, prove that $[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c] = 0$.
questions.answer: Since $\vec c$ is a linear combination of $\vec a$ and $\vec b$, the scalar triple product is zero.

questions.text: If $|\vec a \cdot \vec b| = |\vec a \times \vec b|$ and $\vec a \cdot \vec b < 0$, find the angle between $\vec a$ and $\vec b$.

If $\vec a, \vec b$ and $\vec c$ are position vectors of points A, B, C respectively and $5\vec a - 3\vec b - 2\vec c = \vec 0$, find the ratio in which C divides BA.
If $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are perpendicular vectors, prove that $(\vec a + \vec b)^2 = (\vec a - \vec b)^2$.
questions.answer: Since $\vec a \cdot \vec b = 0$, both expressions reduce to $|\vec a|^2 + |\vec b|^2$.

questions.text: Find the position vector of point R which divides the line joining points P and Q with position vectors $2\hat i - \hat j + 3\hat k$ and $-5\hat i + 2\hat j - 5\hat k$ in the ratio 3 : 2 internally.
questions.answer: $-\hat i + \hat j - \hat k$

questions.text: Find a unit vector perpendicular to the vectors $\hat j + 2\hat k$ and $\hat i + \hat j$.
questions.answer: $(2\hat i - \hat k)/\sqrt5$

questions.text: Find the coordinates of the point which divides the line joining A(2, −2, 2) and B(4, 2, −4) internally in the ratio 3 : 1.
questions.answer: $(\tfrac52, -\tfrac12, \tfrac12)$

questions.text: Find the equation of the line passing through the points A(1, 2, 3) and B(4, 6, 3).
questions.answer: $\vec r = (\hat i + 2\hat j + 3\hat k) + \lambda(3\hat i + 4\hat j)$

questions.answer: Direction ratios of AB and AC are proportional, hence the points are collinear.

questions.answer: Direction ratios of AB = (1,2,3) and BC = (1,2,3) are proportional, hence the points are collinear.

questions.text: Find the equation of the plane which is perpendicular to the line (x−1)/2 = (y−2)/3 = (z−3)/4.
questions.answer: Since the direction ratios of the line are (2,3,4), the required plane is 2x + 3y + 4z = 0.

questions.text: Find the equation of the plane passing through the point (1, 2, 3) and parallel to the plane 2x − y + 3z + 4 = 0.
questions.answer: Required plane: 2x − y + 3z − 9 = 0.

questions.text: Which of the following quantities is a vector?
questions.answer: Velocity

Define a unit vector.
questions.answer: A vector having magnitude equal to one is called a unit vector.

questions.answer: a·b = 0 ⇒ angle = 90°.

questions.text: Show that vectors a + b and a − b are perpendicular if |a| = |b|.
questions.answer: (a+b)·(a−b) = |a|² − |b|² = 0, hence the vectors are perpendicular.

learningObjectives: Write equations of lines and planes in vector and Cartesian forms.

questions.text: Define direction ratios of a line in 3D with an example.
questions.answer: Direction ratios are any three numbers proportional to the components of a direction vector of the line. For a line parallel to the vector $(2,-3,1)$, the direction ratios are $(2,-3,1)$.

questions.text: Find the vector equation of the line passing through point $A(1,2,-1)$ and parallel to vector $(3,-4,1)$.
questions.answer: The vector equation of the line is $\vec{r}=(1,2,-1)+\lambda(3,-4,1)$, where $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$.

Feasible region, feasible and basic feasible solutions

learningObjectives: Plot and interpret linear inequalities in two variables.

Find feasible region and corner points from the graph.
Use corner point method to obtain optimum solution of an LPP.

questions.text: What is a linear programming problem (LPP)?
questions.answer: An LPP is an optimisation problem in which a linear objective function is maximised or minimised subject to a set of linear inequality constraints.

questions.text: Explain the term feasible region in the context of an LPP.
questions.answer: The feasible region is the common region in the plane that satisfies all the given constraints of the LPP simultaneously.

questions.text: In a two-variable LPP, the optimum value of the objective function (if it exists) occurs at:
options: an interior point of the feasible region only
a corner point (vertex) of the feasible region
questions.answer: a corner point (vertex) of the feasible region

questions.text: Graph the inequality $x + 2y \ge 4$ and indicate the feasible half-plane.
questions.answer: Draw the line $x+2y=4$ with intercepts $(4,0)$ and $(0,2)$. Taking the test point $(0,0)$, we get $0 \ge 4$, which is false. Hence, the half-plane not containing the origin is the feasible region.

questions.text: A company produces two products $A$ and $B$. Profit on $A$ is ₹$3$ and on $B$ is ₹$5$ per unit. Each unit of $A$ requires $1$ hour of machine time and $2$ kg of raw material, while each unit of $B$ requires $2$ hours and $1$ kg of raw material. The company has at most $8$ machine hours and $6$ kg of raw material per day. Formulate the LPP to maximise profit.
questions.answer: Let $x$ and $y$ be the units of products $A$ and $B$ respectively. Maximise $Z = 3x + 5y$ subject to $x + 2y \le 8$, $2x + y \le 6$, $x \ge 0$, $y \ge 0$.

questions.text: Solve the LPP: Maximise $Z = 5x + 4y$ subject to $x + y \le 4$, $x \ge 0$, $y \ge 0$ using the graphical method.
questions.answer: The feasible region has vertices $(0,0)$, $(4,0)$ and $(0,4)$. Evaluating $Z$: $Z(0,0)=0$, $Z(4,0)=20$, $Z(0,4)=16$. Maximum value is $Z=20$ at $(4,0)$.

questions.text: Minimise $Z = 3x + 2y$ subject to $x + 2y \ge 6$, $3x + y \ge 9$, $x \ge 0$, $y \ge 0$. State only corner points and minimum value.
questions.answer: Corner points are $(0,3)$, $(3,0)$ and $(3,1.5)$. Values of $Z$ are $6$, $9$ and $12$ respectively. Minimum value is $Z=6$ at $(0,3)$.

questions.text: When do we say that an LPP has an unbounded solution?
questions.answer: An LPP has an unbounded solution when the feasible region is open in the direction of optimisation and the objective function can increase or decrease indefinitely.

questions.text: Explain how you decide the feasible half-plane while graphing a linear inequality $ax + by \ge c$.
questions.answer: First draw the line $ax+by=c$. Choose a test point (usually the origin). If it satisfies the inequality, the half-plane containing it is feasible; otherwise, the opposite half-plane is feasible.

questions.text: A linear programming problem involves:
options: Linear objective function and linear constraints
questions.answer: Linear objective function and linear constraints

questions.text: The feasible region of an LPP is:
questions.answer: The intersection of all constraints

questions.text: Define objective function.
questions.answer: The function which is to be maximized or minimized is called the objective function.

questions.text: What are constraints in LPP?
questions.answer: The conditions expressed as linear inequalities or equations are called constraints.

questions.text: Write the standard form of a linear programming problem.
questions.answer: Maximize or minimize $Z = ax + by$ subject to linear constraints and non-negativity conditions.

questions.text: What is a bounded feasible region?
questions.answer: A feasible region enclosed within finite boundaries is called a bounded feasible region.

questions.text: Why does the optimal solution occur at a corner point?
questions.answer: Because the objective function achieves its maximum or minimum value at one of the vertices of the feasible region.

questions.text: Solve the LPP graphically: Maximize $Z = 3x + 2y$ subject to $x + y \le 4$, $x \ge 0$, $y \ge 0$.
questions.answer: Optimal solution occurs at $(4,0)$ giving $Z = 12$.

questions.text: Solve an LPP by graphical method and find the maximum value of the objective function.
questions.answer: By plotting the constraints, identifying the feasible region and evaluating the objective function at all corner points.

questions.text: Explain an unbounded feasible region with an example.
questions.answer: If the feasible region extends infinitely and the objective function has no finite maximum or minimum value, the region is unbounded.

questions.text: The derivative of $e^{3x}$ with respect to $x$ is:
Find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ if $y = \ln(5x + 1)$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{5}{5x + 1}$

questions.text: Differentiate $y = (x^2 + 1)^5$ with respect to $x$.
If $y = x^x$ for $x > 0$, find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ using logarithmic differentiation.
questions.answer: $\ln y = x\ln x \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \ln x + 1 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = y(\ln x + 1) = x^x(\ln x + 1)$

questions.text: If $y = \sin(3x^2)$, find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ and $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos(3x^2) \cdot 6x = 6x\cos(3x^2). \; \text{Then } \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 6\cos(3x^2) - 36x^2\sin(3x^2)$

questions.text: If $y = \tan^{-1}(x)$, show that $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2}$.
questions.answer: $y = \tan^{-1}x \Rightarrow x = \tan y. \; \dfrac{dx}{dy} = \sec^2 y = 1 + \tan^2 y = 1 + x^2. \; \therefore \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{dx}{dy}} = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2}$

questions.text: Differentiate implicitly: $x^2 + y^2 = 25$.
questions.answer: $2x + 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x}{y}$

questions.text: If $x = a\cos t,\; y = a\sin t$, find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ in terms of $t$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = -a\sin t,\; \dfrac{dy}{dt} = a\cos t \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\dfrac{dy}{dt}}{\dfrac{dx}{dt}} = \dfrac{a\cos t}{-a\sin t} = -\cot t$

questions.text: For $y = \dfrac{x^2 + 1}{x - 1}$, find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ using quotient rule.
questions.answer: $u = x^2 + 1,\; v = x - 1 \Rightarrow u' = 2x,\; v' = 1. \; \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{v u' - u v'}{v^2} = \dfrac{(x - 1)\cdot 2x - (x^2 + 1)\cdot 1}{(x - 1)^2} = \dfrac{x^2 - 2x - 1}{(x - 1)^2}$

questions.text: Show that the derivative of $f(x) = \sin^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}x$ is a constant and hence find $f(x)$.
questions.answer: $f'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}[\sin^{-1}x] + \dfrac{d}{dx}[\cos^{-1}x] = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} = 0. \; \text{Hence } f(x) \text{ is constant. Put } x = 0: \; f(0) = \sin^{-1}0 + \cos^{-1}0 = 0 + \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}. \; \therefore f(x) = \dfrac{\pi}{2},\; \forall x \in [-1,1]$

questions.text: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y = x^2 - 4x + 1$ at $x = 2$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x - 4. \; \text{At } x = 2, \text{ slope } = 2\cdot2 - 4 = 0.$

questions.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y = x^3$ at the point $(1,1)$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2. \; \text{At } x = 1, m = 3. \; y - 1 = 3(x - 1) \Rightarrow y = 3x - 2.$

questions.text: For the same curve $y = x^3$, find the equation of the normal at $(1,1)$.
questions.answer: $m_{\text{tangent}} = 3 \Rightarrow m_{\text{normal}} = -\dfrac{1}{3}. \; y - 1 = -\dfrac{1}{3}(x - 1) \Rightarrow x + 3y - 4 = 0.$

questions.text: Define an increasing function on an interval using derivatives.
questions.answer: A function $f(x)$ is increasing on an interval if $f'(x) \ge 0$ for every $x$ in that interval and $f'(x) > 0$ at least at one point.

questions.text: Find the intervals of increase and decrease of $f(x) = x^3 - 3x$.
questions.answer: $f'(x) = 3x^2 - 3 = 3(x - 1)(x + 1). \; \text{Critical points: } x = -1, 1. \; f'(x) > 0 \text{ for } x<-1, x>1; \; f'(x) < 0 \text{ for } -1<x<1.$

questions.text: Find the local maxima and minima of $f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x$ and classify them using second derivative test.
questions.answer: $f'(x)=3(x-1)(x-3). \; f''(x)=6x-12. \; f''(1)<0 \Rightarrow \text{max at } x=1, f(1)=4. \; f''(3)>0 \Rightarrow \text{min at } x=3, f(3)=0.$

questions.text: State Rolle's Theorem.
questions.answer: If $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]$, differentiable on $(a,b)$ and $f(a)=f(b)$, then there exists $c\in(a,b)$ such that $f'(c)=0$.

questions.text: Verify Rolle's Theorem for $f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3$ on $[1,3]$.
questions.answer: $f(1)=0, f(3)=0. \; f'(x)=2x-4=0 \Rightarrow x=2 \in (1,3). \; \text{Hence verified.}$

questions.text: Evaluate $\int (3x^2 - 4)\,dx$.
questions.answer: $\int 3x^2\,dx = x^3, \; \int (-4)\,dx = -4x. \; \therefore \int (3x^2 - 4)\,dx = x^3 - 4x + C.$

questions.text: Evaluate $\int \cos x\,dx$.
questions.answer: $\int \cos x\,dx = \sin x + C.$

questions.text: Evaluate $\int \dfrac{2x}{x^2 + 1}\,dx$.
questions.answer: Let $u = x^2 + 1 \Rightarrow du = 2x\,dx$. Then $\int \dfrac{2x}{x^2 + 1}\,dx = \int \dfrac{du}{u} = \ln(x^2 + 1) + C.$

questions.text: Evaluate $\int e^{2x}\,dx$.
questions.answer: Let $u = 2x \Rightarrow dx = \dfrac{du}{2}$. Then $\int e^{2x}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2} \int e^u\,du = \dfrac{1}{2}e^{2x} + C.$

questions.text: Evaluate $\int x e^x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Take $u = x,\; dv = e^x dx$. Then $du = dx,\; v = e^x$. Hence $\int x e^x\,dx = x e^x - \int e^x dx = e^x(x - 1) + C.$

questions.text: Evaluate $\int \dfrac{x^2}{x^3 + 1}\,dx$.
questions.answer: Let $u = x^3 + 1 \Rightarrow du = 3x^2 dx$. Then $\int \dfrac{x^2}{x^3 + 1}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{3} \int \dfrac{du}{u} = \dfrac{1}{3}\ln|x^3 + 1| + C.$

questions.text: Resolve $\dfrac{3x + 5}{x^2 - 4}$ into partial fractions and hence evaluate $\int \dfrac{3x + 5}{x^2 - 4}\,dx$.
questions.answer: $x^2 - 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2)$. Let $\dfrac{3x + 5}{x^2 - 4} = \dfrac{A}{x - 2} + \dfrac{B}{x + 2}$. Solving gives $A = \dfrac{11}{4}, B = \dfrac{1}{4}$. Hence integral $= \dfrac{11}{4}\ln|x - 2| + \dfrac{1}{4}\ln|x + 2| + C.$

questions.text: Evaluate $\int \sec^2 x\,dx$ and $\int \cosec^2 x\,dx$.
questions.answer: $\int \sec^2 x\,dx = \tan x + C; \; \int \cosec^2 x\,dx = -\cot x + C.$

questions.text: What is meant by a family of curves represented by an indefinite integral?
questions.answer: The indefinite integral $\int f(x)dx = F(x) + C$ represents a family of curves obtained by varying $C$; these curves differ only by vertical shifts.

questions.text: Evaluate $\int x \ln x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Let $u = \ln x,\; dv = x dx$. Then $du = \dfrac{1}{x}dx,\; v = \dfrac{x^2}{2}$. Hence $\int x\ln x\,dx = \dfrac{x^2}{2}\ln x - \dfrac{x^2}{4} + C.$

questions.text: Write the formula for the area under the curve $y = f(x)$ between $x = a$ and $x = b$ $(f(x) \ge 0)$.

questions.text: Find the area under the curve $y = x$ between $x = 0$ and $x = 2$.
questions.answer: Area $= \int_0^2 x\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^2 = 2$ square units.

questions.text: Find the area bounded by the curve $y = x^2$ and the $x$-axis from $x = 0$ to $x = 3$.
questions.answer: Area $= \int_0^3 x^2\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^3 = 9$ square units.

questions.text: Find the area enclosed between the lines $y = 0$, $x = 1$, $x = 3$ and the curve $y = 2x$.
questions.answer: Area $= \int_1^3 2x\,dx = \left[x^2\right]_1^3 = 8$ square units.

questions.text: Find the area between the curves $y = x$ and $y = x^2$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 1$.
questions.answer: For $0 \le x \le 1$, $x \ge x^2$. Area $= \int_0^1 (x - x^2)\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x^2}{2} - \dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^1 = \dfrac{1}{6}$ square units.

questions.text: Find the area bounded by the parabola $y = x^2$ and the line $y = 4$.
questions.answer: Intersection from $x^2 = 4 \Rightarrow x = -2, 2$. Area $= \int_{-2}^2 (4 - x^2)\,dx = \dfrac{32}{3}$ square units.

questions.text: Find the area bounded by $y = \sin x$ and the $x$-axis between $x = 0$ and $x = \pi$.
questions.answer: Area $= \int_0^{\pi} \sin x\,dx = [-\cos x]_0^{\pi} = 2$ square units.

questions.text: Why do we sometimes take absolute value of a definite integral when computing area?
questions.answer: Because area is always non-negative, while a definite integral can be negative when the curve lies below the $x$-axis; taking absolute value gives the actual area.

questions.text: Find the area enclosed between the curves $y = |x|$ and $y = 2 - |x|$.
questions.answer: Intersection at $|x|=1$. By symmetry, Area $= 2\int_0^1 (2 - 2x)\,dx = 2$ square units.

questions.text: Show that the area enclosed between the parabola $y^2 = 4ax$ and the line $x = a$ is $8a^2/3$ square units.

questions.text: Define the order of a differential equation.
questions.answer: The order of a differential equation is the highest order of derivative of the dependent variable occurring in the equation.

questions.text: Find the order and degree of the differential equation $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3 = 0$.
questions.answer: The highest derivative is $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$, so order $=2$. The equation is polynomial in derivatives and the highest power of the highest derivative is $1$, so degree $=1$.

questions.text: Form the differential equation of the family $y = C e^{2x}$.
questions.answer: Differentiating, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2C e^{2x} = 2y$. Hence the required differential equation is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 2y = 0$.

questions.text: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2$.
questions.answer: Integrating, $dy = 3x^2 dx \Rightarrow y = x^3 + C$.

questions.text: Solve the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + 1}{y + 1}$.
questions.answer: Separating variables, $(y+1)dy = (x+1)dx$. Integrating, $\dfrac{y^2}{2} + y = \dfrac{x^2}{2} + x + C$. Multiplying by $2$, $y^2 + 2y = x^2 + 2x + C$.

questions.text: Solve the linear differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = e^x$.
questions.answer: Here $P=1$. The integrating factor is $e^{\int Pdx}=e^x$. Then $y e^x = \int e^{2x}dx + C = \dfrac{1}{2}e^{2x} + C$. Hence $y = \dfrac{1}{2}e^x + C e^{-x}$.

questions.text: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 2y = 0$ given that $y(0) = 3$.
questions.answer: The integrating factor is $e^{-2x}$. Thus $y e^{-2x} = C$. Using $y(0)=3$ gives $C=3$. Hence $y = 3e^{2x}$.

questions.text: What is a general solution and a particular solution of a differential equation?
questions.answer: A general solution contains arbitrary constant(s) and represents a family of solutions. A particular solution is obtained by assigning specific values to the constants using given conditions.

questions.text: Solve the homogeneous differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + y}{x - y}$.
questions.answer: Put $y = vx$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$. Then $x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{1+v^2}{1-v}$. Hence $\dfrac{1-v}{1+v^2}dv = \dfrac{dx}{x}$. Integrating, $\tan^{-1}v - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(1+v^2) = \ln|x| + C$. Substituting $v = \dfrac{y}{x}$ gives the solution.

questions.text: In a certain chemical reaction, the rate of decay of a substance is proportional to the amount present at time $t$. If initially the amount is $A_0$, set up the differential equation and write its solution.
questions.answer: Let $A(t)$ be the amount at time $t$. Then $\dfrac{dA}{dt} = -kA$. Solving, $A = Ce^{-kt}$. Using $A(0)=A_0$, we get $A(t) = A_0 e^{-kt}$.

questions.answer: $X=1,2,3,4,5,6$ each with probability $\tfrac{1}{6}$. Thus $P(X=k)=\tfrac{1}{6}$ for $k=1,2,3,4,5,6$.

questions.text: A discrete random variable $X$ has distribution: $X:1,2,3,4$ with $P(X=1)=k$, $P(X=2)=2k$, $P(X=3)=3k$, $P(X=4)=4k$. Find $k$ and $E(X)$.
How is variance of a discrete random variable defined in terms of its distribution?
questions.answer: $\operatorname{Var}(X)=\sum (x-\mu)^2P(X=x)$ where $\mu=E(X)$. Equivalently, $\operatorname{Var}(X)=E(X^2)-[E(X)]^2$.

questions.text: Let a continuous random variable $X$ have PDF $f(x)=\tfrac{1}{2}$ for $0\le x\le2$ and $0$ otherwise. Find $P(0.5\le X\le1.5)$.
What is the relation between probability density function (PDF) and distribution function (CDF) of a continuous random variable?
questions.answer: For a continuous random variable $X$ with PDF $f(x)$, the CDF is $F(x)=P(X\le x)=\int_{-\infty}^{x} f(t)dt$. Also $f(x)=F'(x)$ where the derivative exists.

questions.text: A continuous random variable $X$ has PDF $f(x)=kx$ for $0\le x\le2$ and $0$ otherwise. Find $k$, the distribution function $F(x)$ and $E(X)$.
questions.answer: From $\int_0^2 kx\,dx=1$ we get $k=\tfrac12$. Thus $F(x)=0$ for $x<0$, $F(x)=\tfrac{x^2}{4}$ for $0\le x\le2$, and $F(x)=1$ for $x\ge2$. Also $E(X)=\int_0^2 x\cdot\tfrac12 x\,dx=\tfrac{4}{3}$.

questions.text: Find the mean of a discrete random variable $X$ with distribution: $X: 0,1,2$; $P(X): \tfrac{1}{6}, \tfrac{1}{2}, \tfrac{1}{3}$.
questions.answer: Mean $= \sum xP(x) = 0\cdot\tfrac{1}{6} + 1\cdot\tfrac{1}{2} + 2\cdot\tfrac{1}{3} = \tfrac{7}{6}$.

questions.text: Write the formula for variance of a discrete random variable.

questions.text: Show that the variance of a random variable is always non-negative.
questions.answer: Since variance is the expected value of squared deviation, it is always $\ge 0$.

Compute binomial probabilities using formula.
Find mean, variance and standard deviation of binomial distribution.
Apply binomial distribution to simple real-life situations.

questions.text: State the conditions under which a binomial distribution is applicable.
questions.answer: Conditions: (i) Fixed number $n$ of trials, (ii) Each trial has two possible outcomes (success or failure), (iii) Probability of success $p$ is constant for every trial, (iv) Trials are independent.

questions.text: Write the probability mass function of a binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$.
A coin is tossed $4$ times. Assuming a fair coin, find the probability of getting exactly $2$ heads.
Find the mean and variance of a binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$.
questions.answer: Mean $= E(X) = np$, Variance $= \operatorname{Var}(X) = np(1 - p)$.

questions.text: In a binomial distribution $B(10, 0.3)$, find $P(X = 0)$ and $P(X = 10)$.
A die is thrown $5$ times. What is the probability of getting exactly three times a $4$?
A manufacturer of bulbs finds that $5\%$ of the bulbs are defective. If he packs $20$ bulbs in a box, what is the expected number of defective bulbs per box?
questions.answer: Here $n = 20$, $p = 0.05$. Expected number $= np = 20 \times 0.05 = 1$.

questions.text: If $X \sim B(n,p)$, express the standard deviation of $X$.
questions.answer: Standard deviation $\sigma = \sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(X)} = \sqrt{np(1 - p)}$.

questions.text: For a binomial distribution, $n = 8$ and $p = 0.4$. Find $P(X \ge 6)$.
